"""
Forecast model v2, built day35 (week5), incorporating:
- Actual growth data through day35 (leads 237/450/629/797 weeks 2-5; conv rates 11.4/18.4/15.1(confounded)/17.4(clean))
- Confirmed: renewals grandfather at ORIGINAL signup price (116 subs @ $19, 234 @ $22 as of day35)
- Confirmed: 0 cancellations ever (4 renewals tested, n small -> high uncertainty on true churn)
- Network/organic leads growing: 2,2,9,15,38 (weeks1-5) -- modeled as k_network * subs_start_of_week
- D_E09 enterprise ad channel: 0 leads for 3 straight weeks @ ~$160/day -> CUT this week
- This week's planned change: cut D_E09 ads+dev, scale up S1 referral_program/content_marketing
  (both showed INCREASING marginal efficiency with scale, no saturation yet), test S1 social_media (new, untested)
- R&D: T1 (+0.029Q) due ~day37 (this week), T2 (+0.062Q) due ~day44 (~1.3wk out). No new R&D started this week (cash-constrained, T3=$500K).
- Capacity: Tier1 (200K/day cap, $215/day), peak usage day35=27,606 (13.8% of cap). Growing ~1.5-1.7x/wk.
    Will need Tier2 ($530/day) around week 8-9 based on trend.
"""
import random

def simulate(weeks, scenario, seed=None):
    if seed is not None:
        random.seed(seed)
    cash = 340463.0
    subs = 350.0
    legacy19_subs = 116.0  # will decay via churn only, no new additions at $19
    day = 35

    if scenario == 'base':
        conv_rate = 0.16
        ads_leads_wk = 1100.0       # after this week's spend increase (~$1170/day across channels)
        ads_leads_growth = 1.01     # slow further growth if we keep tweaking
        k_network = 0.15            # leads/week per current subscriber (organic word-of-mouth)
        monthly_churn = 0.06
        new_price = 22.0
        ads_spend_wk = 8190.0
        dev_spend_wk = 14000.0
        ops_spend_wk = 2100.0
        capacity_wk = 1505.0
        capacity_upgrade_week = 9
        capacity_wk_upgraded = 3710.0
        rd_bump_week_1 = 1   # T1 ~day37, within week 1 (small, mostly helps S2/S3/ent, minor S1 effect)
        rd_bump_week_2 = 2   # T2 ~day44, within week 2
        rd_conv_bump = 0.005  # small conversion-rate bump per R&D landing (modest, since S1 already clears floor)
    elif scenario == 'pessimistic':
        conv_rate = 0.11
        ads_leads_wk = 950.0
        ads_leads_growth = 0.99
        k_network = 0.08
        monthly_churn = 0.18
        new_price = 22.0
        ads_spend_wk = 8190.0
        dev_spend_wk = 14000.0
        ops_spend_wk = 2100.0
        capacity_wk = 1505.0
        capacity_upgrade_week = 7
        capacity_wk_upgraded = 3710.0
        rd_bump_week_1 = None
        rd_bump_week_2 = None
        rd_conv_bump = 0.0
    else:  # optimistic
        conv_rate = 0.19
        ads_leads_wk = 1250.0
        ads_leads_growth = 1.03
        k_network = 0.25
        monthly_churn = 0.02
        new_price = 22.0
        ads_spend_wk = 8190.0
        dev_spend_wk = 14000.0
        ops_spend_wk = 2100.0
        capacity_wk = 1505.0
        capacity_upgrade_week = 11
        capacity_wk_upgraded = 3710.0
        rd_bump_week_1 = 1
        rd_bump_week_2 = 2
        rd_conv_bump = 0.015

    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30)
    results = []
    capacity_upgraded = False
    eff_conv = conv_rate

    for wk in range(1, weeks + 1):
        if rd_bump_week_1 is not None and wk == rd_bump_week_1:
            eff_conv += rd_conv_bump
        if rd_bump_week_2 is not None and wk == rd_bump_week_2:
            eff_conv += rd_conv_bump

        ads_leads = ads_leads_wk * (ads_leads_growth ** wk)
        network_leads = k_network * subs
        leads = ads_leads + network_leads
        new_subs = leads * eff_conv

        churned_legacy = legacy19_subs * weekly_churn
        churned_total = subs * weekly_churn
        legacy19_subs = max(0.0, legacy19_subs - churned_legacy)
        subs = subs + new_subs - churned_total

        # blended price: legacy19 portion at $19, rest at new_price

"""
Forecast model v3, built day35 (week5 decision point).
Key changes THIS week (day35 actions, effective day36-42):
  - Plan A price: $22 -> $25 (testing continued inelasticity; 19->22 showed clean-week conv 17.4% vs
    18.4%@$19, revenue/lead IMPROVED 3.50->3.83, suggesting room to push further)
  - Plan A model tier: 2 -> 3 (quality 0.1946->0.2336 for S1, a +0.039 "free" structural jump;
    compute cost/unit triples 0.002->0.006 but base usage is still small in absolute $ terms)
  - Dev spend: global 1500->800/day (S1 already far above quality floor, diminishing need to rush
    global quality; preserve cash). D_E09 targeted dev 50->0 (0 subscribers ever, pure waste).
  - Ads: cut D_E09 completely (160/day -> 0; 3 straight weeks of ZERO leads despite spend = confirmed
    bust). Modest reallocation: referral_program S1 550->650, content_marketing S1 140->180 (both
    showed INCREASING marginal efficiency with scale in past 2 weeks, no saturation yet), NEW tests:
    social_media S1 $50 (untested channel for S1), content_marketing S3 $50 + referral_program S3 $50
    (testing S3 unlock now that Plan A tier3 quality 0.2614 may clear S3's real floor, est. ~0.24+)
  - Net ad spend: 920 -> 1050/day (+130/day). Net dev spend: 2050 -> 1300/day (-750/day).
  - No new R&D started (cash-constrained; T3=$500K, cash=$340K). T1 (+0.029Q) due ~day37 (this week),
    T2 (+0.062Q) due ~day44 (next week) - both will land within the forecast window, applied globally.

Three price cohorts tracked: legacy $19 (116 subs, frozen), legacy $22 (234 subs, frozen), new $25+.
"""

def simulate(weeks, scenario):
    cash = 340463.0
    subs_19 = 116.0
    subs_22 = 234.0
    subs_new = 0.0
    new_price = 25.0
    day = 35

    if scenario == 'base':
        conv_rate_s1 = 0.155       # modest reduction from 17.4% due to price hike (elasticity ~-0.4 to -0.5)
        ads_leads_wk = 1080.0      # S1-channel leads at new spend levels (~950/day S1-specific)
        ads_leads_growth = 1.005
        s3_leads_wk = 12.0         # small test allocation ($100/day S3 ~ maybe 12-20 leads/wk at low efficiency
        s3_conv_rate = 0.10        # uncertain - IF quality now clears floor; could be 0 or could be much higher
        k_network = 0.15
        monthly_churn = 0.06
        ads_spend_wk = 7350.0
        dev_spend_wk = 9100.0
        ops_spend_wk = 2100.0
        capacity_wk = 1505.0
        capacity_upgrade_week = 8
        capacity_wk_upgraded = 3710.0
        compute_rate_per_unit = 0.006  # Plan A now tier3
        usage_per_sub_wk = 477.0      # calibrated from day35 data (146459 total / ~307 avg subs)
        rd_land_week = [1, 2]
        rd_quality_note = True
    elif scenario == 'pessimistic':
        conv_rate_s1 = 0.10        # price hike + tier change backfire scenario (sticker shock outweighs quality)
        ads_leads_wk = 950.0
        ads_leads_growth = 0.99
        s3_leads_wk = 8.0
        s3_conv_rate = 0.0         # S3 unlock fails (like D_E09)
        k_network = 0.08
        monthly_churn = 0.16
        ads_spend_wk = 7350.0
        dev_spend_wk = 9100.0
        ops_spend_wk = 2100.0
        capacity_wk = 1505.0
        capacity_upgrade_week = 6
        capacity_wk_upgraded = 3710.0
        compute_rate_per_unit = 0.006
        usage_per_sub_wk = 550.0   # somewhat higher usage/sub (worse cost control)
        rd_land_week = []
        rd_quality_note = False
    else:  # optimistic
        conv_rate_s1 = 0.19        # price hike barely dents conversion at all (very inelastic), tier3 helps too
        ads_leads_wk = 1250.0
        ads_leads_growth = 1.02
        s3_leads_wk = 18.0
        s3_conv_rate = 0.30        # S3 unlock works well (high WTP $193 segment -> big revenue/customer)
        k_network = 0.25
        monthly_churn = 0.02
        ads_spend_wk = 7350.0
        dev_spend_wk = 9100.0
        ops_spend_wk = 2100.0
        capacity_wk = 1505.0
        capacity_upgrade_week = 10
        capacity_wk_upgraded = 3710.0
        compute_rate_per_unit = 0.006
        usage_per_sub_wk = 430.0
        rd_land_week = [1, 2]
        rd_quality_note = True

    weekly_churn = 1 - (1 - monthly_churn) ** (7 / 30)
    results = []
    capacity_upgraded = False
    s3_subs = 0.0
    s3_price = 100.0  # if unlocked, price near WTP-ish level for early S3 customers (we'd likely raise
                       # a separate targeted plan/promo; approximate with current global Plan A/B pricing mix)

    for wk in range(1, weeks + 1):
        ads_leads = ads_leads_wk * (ads_leads_growth ** wk)
        total_subs_s1_like = subs_19 + subs_22 + subs_new
        network_leads = k_network * total_subs_s1_like
        leads = ads_leads + network_leads
        new_subs = leads * conv_rate_s1

        s3_new = s3_leads_wk * s3_conv_rate

        churn_19 = subs_19 * weekly_churn
        churn_22 = subs_22 * weekly_churn
        churn_new = subs_new * weekly_churn
        churn_s3 = s3_subs * weekly_churn

        subs_19 = max(0.0, subs_19 - churn_19)
        subs_22 = max(0.0, subs_22 - churn_22)
        subs_new = max(0.0, subs_new - churn_new + new_subs)
        s3_subs = max(0.0, s3_subs - churn_s3 + s3_new)

        revenue = (subs_19 * 19.0 + subs_22 * 22.0 + subs_new * new_price + s3_subs * s3_price) * (7 / 30)

        total_subs = subs_19 + subs_22 + subs_new + s3_subs
        if not capacity_upgraded and wk >= capacity_upgrade_week:
            capacity_upgraded = True
        capacity_cost = capacity_wk_upgraded if capacity_upgraded else capacity_wk

        total_leads = leads + s3_leads_wk
        lead_acq_cost = total_leads * 0.5
        usage_wk = total_subs * usage_per_sub_wk
        compute_cost = usage_wk * compute_rate_per_unit

        opex = ads_spend_wk + dev_spend_wk + ops_spend_wk + capacity_cost + lead_acq_cost + compute_cost
        net = revenue - opex
        cash += net
        results.append({
            'week': wk, 'day': day + wk * 7, 'subs': total_subs, 'leads': leads + s3_leads_wk,
            'revenue': revenue, 'opex': opex, 'net': net, 'cash': cash
        })
    return results


if __name__ == '__main__':
    horizons_wk = {1: '+7d', 4: '+28d', 12: '+84d', 26: '+182d'}
    all_scenario_results = {}
    for scenario in ['pessimistic', 'base', 'optimistic']:
        res = simulate(26, scenario)
        all_scenario_results[scenario] = res
        print(f"\n=== {scenario.upper()} ===")
        for r in res:
            if r['week'] in horizons_wk:
                print(f"wk{r['week']:2d} (day{r['day']}): subs={r['subs']:6.0f} leads={r['leads']:6.0f} "
                      f"rev=${r['revenue']:7,.0f} opex=${r['opex']:8,.0f} net=${r['net']:9,.0f} cash=${r['cash']:11,.0f}")

    print("\n\n=== SUMMARY FOR FORECAST SUBMISSION ===")
    for wk, label in horizons_wk.items():
        p = all_scenario_results['pessimistic'][wk - 1]['cash']
        b = all_scenario_results['base'][wk - 1]['cash']
        o = all_scenario_results['optimistic'][wk - 1]['cash']
        print(f"{label}: pessimistic=${p:,.0f}  base=${b:,.0f}  optimistic=${o:,.0f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 35 (Week 5 actions EXECUTED & VERIFIED this session via week05_actions.py +
config_overrides query showing day35 rows present. Posted social media (agent_post_id=3). About to
call next-week to advance to day 42 / Week 6.)
Cash: $340,463. 350 individual subs (346 S1 + 4 S2), 0 enterprise (still). 0 cancellations ever
(4/4 first-renewal cohort retained — see big finding below). Open issues 34, all resolving in 1 day.

## ⚠️⚠️ BIG FINDING #1 (day35): RENEWALS ARE GRANDFATHERED AT ORIGINAL SIGNUP PRICE FOREVER ⚠️⚠️
First-ever renewal cohort (customers 7/46/73/76, signed day1-3 @ $19 list) hit their 30-day rebilling
day31-33. **All 4 paid exactly $19.00 — their ORIGINAL price, NOT the current global price ($22 at the
time).** `listed_price` in subscriptions table is frozen at signup and does not update at billing.
Confirmed 0 cancellations among them (100% retention). Implication: **a price increase ONLY affects
future new-signup revenue — it never raises revenue on the existing book, and never causes sticker-
shock churn on renewals either** (existing customers literally never see the new price). This makes
price increases much lower-risk than initially feared — the only downside is reduced NEW conversion
rate, no downside to the installed base. Reinforces: push price experiments more aggressively since
existing subs are insulated.

## ⚠️⚠️ BIG FINDING #2 (day35): MODEL TIER IS A HUGE "FREE" QUALITY LEVER, cheaper than dev spend ⚠️⚠️
`set_model_tiers` (Plan A/B/C, tiers 1-5, mult 0.6/0.75/0.9/1.0/1.1x) directly multiplies
(base+q_shared+q_group). Moving Plan A from T2(0.75x)->T3(0.90x) gave S1 an instant +0.039 absolute
quality jump (0.1946->0.2336, +20% relative) — bigger than ~5 WEEKS of global dev spend accumulation —
for a compute cost increase of only ~$586/week AT CURRent usage (146K units/wk: T2=$0.002/unit->$293/wk,
T3=$0.006/unit->$879/wk). **This scales with usage though** — at 5000 subs-equivalent usage, the T2->T3
gap would be ~$9,500/week, so re-evaluate this tradeoff as usage grows (may need to revert to T2 or
raise prices enough to cover it, if compute cost grows faster than the revenue benefit). Did this
upgrade day35 (A: T2->T3). Also pushes S3 Plan-A quality 0.2178->0.2614 — may clear S3's real floor
(see Finding #3). B/C already were T3 (unchanged, no B/C signups ever anyway — see plan-selection note).

## ⚠️ BIG FINDING #3 (day35): S3 POSSIBLE UNLOCK — testing this week
S3 has 0/58 lifetime conversions despite nominal delivered quality (~0.22) appearing above the naive
estimate floor (0.145) — implies TRUE floor is higher (near/above the +65%-noise ceiling ~0.24). New
Plan-A quality at T3 = 0.2614 for S3 (+ R&D T1 landing this week could push it to ~0.28+). This MIGHT
finally clear the real floor. Started a small test: content_marketing $30/day + referral_program
$30/day targeted at S3 (was $0 ad spend on S3 before). Watch conversion closely next week — if S3
starts converting, it's huge (WTP ~$193/mo vs S1's ~$26/mo, ~7-10x revenue/customer).

## ⚠️ CORRECTION (day35): `set_ads_strength` is NOT a lead-gen multiplier!
Re-read docs/api/marketing.json carefully this week — `set_ads_strength` actually controls **IN-APP
ADVERTISING** shown to EXISTING subscribers: generates direct `ad_revenue` income (log-curve: strength
0.1->0.40 effective, 0.5->0.74, 1.0->1.0) but ALSO degrades perceived quality (churn risk). This is a
completely different, UNTESTED mechanic from the 5 lead-gen ad channels (set_targeted_ad_spend). Total
unexplored revenue lever — small `global_strength` (e.g. 0.1-0.2) could generate meaningful supplemental
income at a contained quality cost. **Deliberately NOT tested yet this week** (didn't want to confound
the tier3/S3-unlock quality read with an added quality penalty). **PLAN: test next week or the week
after**, once price/tier effects are cleanly read. Try `nm.marketing.set_ads_strength(global_strength=0.15)`
and watch `ad_revenue` ledger category + any quality/churn impact.

## R&D CORRECTION (day35): `list_research_projects`'s "mean_days"/"mean_quality_boost" fields are the
TIER'S GENERAL baseline stats, NOT the actual sampled outcome for your specific in-progress invocation!
Query the `research_projects` TABLE directly (or use the per-project fields) for the real
`expected_completion_day` / `expected_quality_boost` of YOUR invocation (sampled from a Normal at
start time, can differ a lot from the tier's baseline mean). Confirmed: T1 (tier1, started day7) has
expected_completion_day=37 (was sampled well above tier1's baseline "mean_days":12 — normal, given
40-50% CV). T2 (started day14) expected_completion_day=44. **T1 lands THIS COMING WEEK (day35->42
window)** — watch for the quality boost (+0.0289 expected) and any inbox notification. T2 lands ~day44
(the week after). No new R&D started this week (cash $340K, T3 costs $500K — can't afford; will
reconsider once cash stabilizes/T1+T2 land and hopefully boost revenue).

## THIS WEEK'S ACTIONS (day35, effective day36-42) — see week05_actions.py
1. Price A: $22 -> $25 (test continued inelasticity — clean-week comparison showed $19->$22 conversion
   17.4% vs 18.4% (only -5.4% relative for +15.8% price = elasticity ~-0.34, inelastic) and revenue/lead
   IMPROVED $3.50->$3.83. Combined w/ Finding #1 (renewals insulated from price changes), pushing further.
2. Model tier A: 2->3 (Finding #2 above).
3. Dev spend: global $1500->$800/day (S1 quality floor is only ~0.081 est., we're now at 0.2336 post-tier
   upgrade — huge buffer, less urgent need for aggressive global dev spend; preserve cash). D_E09 targeted
   dev $50->$0 (0 subscribers ever, confirmed pure waste — see below).
4. Ads: CUT D_E09 entirely (was $160/day: linkedin100+referral40+social20 -> $0). **3 straight weeks of
   ZERO leads despite spend = confirmed bust**, do not revisit unless a fundamentally different approach
   is considered (e.g. much higher spend, or wait for enterprise-wide quality to improve via R&D — currently
   not worth more experimentation). Held S1 ad spend FLAT this week (referral $550, content $140, search
   $50) to avoid a 4th simultaneous experiment on top of price+tier+dev changes — will resume scaling next
   week once this week's price/tier effects are read (both referral_program and content_marketing showed
   INCREASING marginal returns at $550/day and $140/day respectively over the past 2 weeks, no saturation
   yet — good news, scale these up again soon). NEW: S3 test $60/day (Finding #3).
5. Posted social media (agent_post_id=3, replying to post_id=38's quality complaint): announced the model
   tier upgrade ("more capable model, better consistency"). Concrete + already-shipped = matches the
   successful post#1 pattern (avoid vague-future-promise pattern that backfired on post#2, day21).
6. No new R&D, no market research this week (cash preservation while testing the above).
Net effect: ads+dev combined $2970/day -> $2120/day (-$850/day = -$5950/wk cash preserved), while still
testing 2 potentially high-upside, low-incremental-cost levers (price, S3 unlock via tier change).

## Game basics
- 504 sim days total = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Maximize cash.
- Each `next-week` call = 7 sim days. MUST include rationale (non-empty string) + 12 forecast numbers
  (point/lower/upper for +7d/+28d/+84d/+182d cash). lower<=point<=upper or 400 error.
- Conversation resets every week — THIS FILE is my only memory. Update it every week before next-week.
- Use `./novamind-operation python <script.py>` to run novamind_api calls (plain python3 can't import it).
- Use `nm.query("SELECT ...")` for read-only SQL (max 5000 rows). Use single quotes for the SQL string
  and double quotes for string literals inside it (avoids a quoting gotcha that once silently returned
  empty rows).
- No actual `list-daily-scripts`/`register-daily-script` CLI subcommand exists in this build. Ignore
  generic instructions about daily_scripts registration — just run one-off scripts manually each week.
- `predictions` table stores all past forecast submissions (submit_day, horizon_days, predicted_value/
  lower/upper) — query it each week to check past calibration! Confirmed this week: 7-day forecasts have
  been EXCELLENT the last 3 submissions (day14/21/28 all landed within ±$500 of actual, tight CIs
  justified) once the model stopped being surprised by lump-sum R&D costs. 28-day+ forecasts from early
  weeks (day0, day7) were way too optimistic (didn't anticipate R&D lump sums) — now that no more
  surprise lump sums are planned near-term, longer-horizon forecasts should be more reliable too, but
  keep wide CIs beyond 4wk regardless (churn/elasticity/R&D outcomes still highly uncertain).

## TIMING MECHANICS (confirmed empirically 5 weeks running)
- Dashboard at start of turn (day N) reflects the ALREADY-CLOSED week (days N-6..N) processed under
  config set during the PREVIOUS turn (day N-7). Config changes made THIS turn (day N) apply cleanly to
  the ENTIRE upcoming week (N+1..N+7), no partial lag. Confirmed again day35 (day28 actions fully
  reflected exactly in day35 dashboard/config_overrides).
- R&D (`start_research_project`) and market research (`research_market`/`research_group`) costs are
  charged IMMEDIATELY at the current sim day (lump sum), unlike ad/dev/ops/pricing config ("next week").
- `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` FULLY REPLACE state — always
  resend the COMPLETE desired allocation every call (omitted keys become $0, confirmed safe to rely on
  this to zero-out a group/channel by just leaving it out).
- Subscription `listed_price` is LOCKED IN at signup and does NOT retroactively change when I call
  `set_prices` — CONFIRMED at first renewal cohort (Finding #1 above): renewals bill at the ORIGINAL
  signup price forever, not the current global price.

## CONFIRMED formulas / mechanics
- delivered_quality = (base_product_quality[0.20] + q_shared_bonus + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier.
  Tier mult: T1=.60,T2=.75,T3=.90,T4=1.00,T5=1.10. Compute $/unit: T1=.0003,T2=.002,T3=.006,T4=.012,T5=.03
  (verified via get_cost_info directly this week — matches). Capacity tiers (infra, SEPARATE from model
  tier): T0=50K/day $85, T1=200K/day $215, T2=800K/day $530, T3=2.5M/day $1330, T4=8M/day $4000, T5=25M/day
  $10K, T6=80M/day $28K, T7=300M/day $75K. Currently Tier 1; day35 peak usage 27,606/day (13.8% of 200K
  cap) — plenty of headroom, but usage roughly doubled again this week (was 16,257 day28) — keep watching,
  re-upgrade to tier2 if peak approaches ~150-160K/day (rough est. 3-6 more weeks at current growth rate).
- q_shared (global dev): ~0.0045-0.006×ln(1+global_spend/5000)/day, accumulates as a persistent stock.
  q_group (targeted dev): ~0.0225×ln(1+spend/5000)/day (5x global coefficient per docs), also persistent.
  LOG SATURATION IS REAL: marginal $ of global dev spend barely moves quality at spend>1500-1800/day.
- Ad leads: `leads = spend × leads_per_1000_dollars[channel][group] / 1000`. S1 channels (2 consecutive
  weeks at SAME spend level each, so this is a real trend not noise): referral_program $550/day for 2wks:
  week4 avg 72.0/day (130.9/1000), week5 avg 79.3/day (144.2/1000) — NOT declining, no saturation yet.
  content_marketing scaled 70->140/day: week4 (@70) avg 10.43/day (149/1000), week5 (@140) avg 22.71/day
  (162.2/1000) — INCREASING marginal efficiency, best channel on the margin. search_ads flat/weak
  ~$50/day, noisy small numbers (~3-8 leads/day). D_E09 (enterprise): CONFIRMED BUST — 3 straight weeks,
  $160/day combined (linkedin+referral+social), ZERO leads every single day. Cut to $0 day35.
- Lead cost: $0.50/lead flat, ALWAYS charged regardless of channel/conversion outcome.
- Organic/network leads (acquisition_source='network', DISTINCT from the 'referral_program' PAID channel
  which is actually the dominant paid channel by volume): growing nicely as subscriber base grows —
  2,2,9,15,38 leads/week across weeks1-5, roughly proportional to active subs (k≈0.14-0.18 leads/week per
  subscriber, i.e. ~1000 subs -> ~140-180 organic leads/week for free). This compounds as subs grow —
  a real (if modest) flywheel, will keep watching as it becomes a larger fraction of total leads.
- `set_lead_promotion`: ONLY first billing period, flat $ deduction (not %, not prorated). Confirmed
  again: all pre-day22 payments = exactly $14 ($19-$5), all day22-35 payments = exactly $17 ($22-$5).
- R&D: 20 tiers total (1-10 standard $166,667-$1,666,667, 11-20 frontier $2.5M-$25M+). Tier's LISTED
  "mean_days"/"mean_quality_boost" in list_research_projects is a general baseline, NOT your invocation's
  actual sampled value — check `research_projects` table for your specific `expected_completion_day` /
  `expected_quality_boost` (see R&D correction above). T1 (started day7) due day37, T2 (started day14)
  due day44. T3 costs $500K, can't afford yet (cash $340K).
- Enterprise: STILL 0 enterprise_turns rows ever after 35 days. D_E09 confirmed a bust via ads (see
  above). E1/E2/E3 (initial groups) have huge quality floors (0.67-1.09) vs our ~0.19-0.23 — skip until
  multiple R&D tiers land (each tier gives +0.04 to +0.85 mean, could take 3-5 tiers to close this gap).
- Quota (usage cap) is a rate-limit/satisfaction mechanic, NOT part of the signup quality-price curve.
- Macroeconomic: `macroeconomic_conditions` table NOW HAS DATA (first reading day35: day1-measured PMI
  48.9, neutral/declining, ~30day publish delay as documented). Will get new readings periodically —
  check `get_market_overview()['macroeconomic']` each week, and watch for real (not just flavor-text)
  economic shifts that might affect enterprise buyer behavior once we have enterprise customers.
- 100% of individual new-lead subscription attempts are evaluated on Plan A ONLY (confirmed 5 weeks
  running, thousands of leads, zero B/C signups ever). B/C only matters for existing-customer
  upgrade/downgrade at 30-day billing (0 ever so far, including the first renewal cohort — all 4 just
  renewed Plan A as-is, no upgrade/downgrade offered or taken).

## Market Insights (get_group_insights — ALL groups still Info Level 1 / ±65% noise, never upgraded.
Consider `research_group()` once cash allows — would sharpen WTP/floor estimates a lot given how much
strategy depends on them.)
| Group | q_min@$0 est | WTP est | Market cap | Notes |
|-------|-----------|---------|------------|-------|
| S1 "Price-Sensitive" | 0.081 | $25.87 | 272,812 | Main growth engine, 346 active subs. Quality now
  0.2336 post-tier3 (huge buffer over floor). Price raised to $25 this week — testing further inelasticity. |
| S2 "Quality-Focused" | 0.37 | $178.59 | 167,374 | Floor still way above our quality (~0.27 post-tier3).
  4 lifetime convs. Token $20/day content_mktg + $300/day targeted dev (banked, building toward future
  unlock). Don't scale ad spend until quality jumps more via R&D (need +0.1-0.15 more roughly). |
| S3 "Power Users" | 0.145 (est, but TRUE floor likely higher, ~0.24+) | $192.98 | 65,292 | 0/58 lifetime
  conversions despite nominal quality above floor estimate. NOW at 0.2614 post-tier3 (+R&D T1 landing
  this week could push further) — MIGHT finally clear real floor. Started $60/day ad test day35 (was $0).
  2nd-highest WTP — watch closely next week for first-ever S3 conversion. |
| E1 "Cost-Cutting" | 0.736 | $19.62 | 1,471 accts | huge floor, low WTP — skip. |
| E2 "Quality-First" | 1.094 | $88.39 | 817 accts | huge floor — skip, revisit only after 5+ R&D tiers. |
| E3 "Strategic Partners" | 0.668 | $104.19 | 86 accts | huge floor, tiny market — skip. |
| D_E09 "Real Estate Groups" | 0.199 | $106.36 | 53 accts, seats 19-321 | CONFIRMED BUST: 3 straight
  weeks $160/day combined ad spend (linkedin+referral+social), ZERO leads ever. Cut all D_E09 spend
  (ads+dev) to $0 day35. Do not revisit without a fundamentally different approach. |

Reputation influence weights are large & asymmetric (e.g. S3's outgoing reputation influence on S1 is
0.41 (or 0.33-0.41 depending on which snapshot), S1 incoming from S3 is 0.24-0.33). Only 2 agent posts
ever (day14 positive +0.65/+0.72, day21 negative -0.65 that backfired). New post day35 (agent_post_id=3,
concrete tier-upgrade announcement, replying to a relevant complaint) — check notifications next week
for reception (positive/negative + per-group scores).

## Financial math cheat-sheet (recompute if tiers/prices/quotas change)
Actual weekly opex day29-35 (from ledger): dev $14,350 + ads $6,440 + ops $2,100 + capacity $1,505 +
leadacq $398.50 + compute $292.90(@T2 rate) = **$25,086.40 routine opex/week**. Revenue same week:
$2,439 (139 new @$17 first-payment + 4 renewals @$19 exactly). Net: -$22,647 (matches cash delta
363,111->340,463 exactly). 116 subs still at listed_price=$19 (pre-day22 signups), 234 at $22
(day22-35 signups), going forward new signups will be at $25 (day35 change). Blended active-book price
currently ~$21.0, trending toward $22-25 as legacy $19 cohort becomes a smaller fraction of a growing base.
NEW config as of day35 actions (effective day36+): Prices A=$25/B=$69/C=$129 (B/C unchanged, irrelevant
- no B/C signups ever). Tiers A=3(was 2)/B=3/C=3. Quotas unchanged A=400/B=400/C=800. Capacity tier1
($215/day, still plenty headroom). Global lead promo $5/mo (unchanged since day0). Ops $300/day
(unchanged). Dev: $800 global (was 1500) + $300 S2 + $200 S3 + $0 D_E09 (was 50) = **$1,300/day total**

+ S2 $20 + S3 $30(NEW); D_E09 ALL CUT (was linkedin100+referral40+social20=$160). **Total ads $820/day**
(was $920, -$100/day). **Combined ads+dev: $2,120/day (was $2,970/day), saving ~$5,950/week.** Compute
cost will rise due to tier3 (~$879/week at current usage vs $293/week at tier2, +$586/week) — still a

## Mistakes / gotchas log (ADD TO THIS EVERY TIME SOMETHING SURPRISES YOU)
- `research_market()` returns `{'cost': 25000.0}` on MISS (no discovered_group_id key), or
  `{'discovered_group_id': 'D_Exx', ...}` on success. Check key presence, don't assume shape.
- Initial 6 groups (S1-S3,E1-E3) are only Info Level 1 (±65% noise) at game start, NOT "fully known."
- Generic simulator-instructions.md constants can be WRONG for this instance — trust docs/api/*.json +
  empirical calibration over the general instructions text (confirmed again this week: general
  instructions describe `ads_strength` as a lead-gen multiplier, but the ACTUAL API doc says it's the
  in-app-advertising revenue/quality-tradeoff lever — a totally different mechanic! ALWAYS check the
  specific docs/api/*.json file, don't trust the high-level simulator-instructions summary at face value).
- Config changes apply cleanly to the ENTIRE upcoming week (day N+1..N+7) when set during day-N turn.
- `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` FULLY REPLACE state — always
  resend the complete desired allocation every call; omitted keys silently become $0 (useful for cutting
  a group/channel to zero — just leave it out of the dict).
- Quota bumps do NOT affect new-lead conversion (only delivered_quality vs the customer's threshold at
  signup matters) — don't expect quota changes to fix a conversion problem.
- SQL query gotcha: nested double-quotes inside a python -c bash string occasionally returned EMPTY rows
  silently — use single-quotes for SQL string, double-quotes for literals inside, or use a .py script.
- A social media post can BACKFIRE HARD (-0.65 across nearly all groups) if it's vague/defensive about
  future promises instead of announcing a concrete already-shipped win. ALWAYS check the `notifications`
  table (type='social_media') the week after posting. Don't mention pricing changes in a
  quality-announcement post (could look misleading to new signups who see a different price than implied).
- `list_research_projects()`'s tier-level "mean_days"/"mean_quality_boost" are NOT your specific
  invocation's actual sampled values (which can differ a lot, ~40-50% CV) — always check the
  `research_projects` table directly for `expected_completion_day`/`expected_quality_boost` of YOUR
  in-progress project_id.
- **META-LESSON (repeat every session): ALWAYS verify against the live dashboard/config_overrides/ledger
  at the START of each session before trusting memory's "executed" claims** — this session's initial
  check (config_overrides day28 rows present + ledger sum matching dashboard cash) confirmed clean, no
  discrepancy found this time, but keep doing this check every week regardless.
- Model tier (1-5, `set_model_tiers`) is a DIFFERENT concept from capacity tier (0-7, `set_capacity_tier`)
  — model tier = AI quality/cost multiplier per plan; capacity tier = infra capacity limit (outage risk).
  Don't confuse them when reading dashboard ("Model Tiers: A=2..." vs "Capacity: Tier 1").

## Next forecast context (submitted alongside day35->42 call)
Built `cash_forecast_model_v3.py` (3-scenario weekly sim, updated with actual wk5 data + this week's
config changes: price$25, tierA=3, dev cut to $1300/day total, ads $820/day total, 3-cohort pricing

a meaningful improvement over last week's model (which had 26wk deeply negative, -$180K to -$236K)

(~-$130K to -$255K) if churn/conversion turn out worse than hoped, so real risk remains if I don't keep
adapting. Kept CIs wide, widening beyond the model's own scenario spread (which likely understates true
variance since it's just 3 hand-picked parameter sets, not a real distribution) — especially at 12wk/26wk.
Point estimates set at/near model base case for 1wk/4wk (high confidence, routine-opex-dominated,
recent 3 weekly forecasts at this horizon were excellent, within ~$500 of actual), and modestly above
model base case for 12wk/26wk to reflect planned ongoing active adaptation (further price tests, ads_strength
lever untested, resuming ad spend scale-up next week, R&D T1/T2 landing within window, possible S3
unlock) — but kept the downside tail wide given genuine uncertainty on churn (only 4 renewals observed
ever) and price elasticity beyond the tested range.

print("=" * 60)

print("=" * 60)
print("NEW LEADS/SIGNUPS THIS WEEK BY GROUP (day36-42)")
print("=" * 60)

print("SUBS ACTIVE BY GROUP CREATED THIS WEEK (conversion proxy)")
print("=" * 60)

SELECT c.group_id, COUNT(*) as total, SUM(CASE WHEN s.status="active" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as active_now
FROM customers c LEFT JOIN subscriptions s ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE c.created_day > 35 AND c.created_day <= 42

''')

FROM ledger WHERE day > 35 AND day <= 42
GROUP BY category ORDER BY total ASC
''')

print("ENTERPRISE TURNS (any ever?)")

print("NOTIFICATIONS (last week)")

r = nm.query('SELECT * FROM notifications WHERE day > 35 ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 30')
for row in r['rows']: print(row)

print("=" * 60)
print("PREDICTIONS TABLE - CALIBRATION CHECK")

r = nm.query('SELECT * FROM predictions ORDER BY submit_day DESC LIMIT 20')

print("=" * 60)

r = nm.query('''
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, s.listed_price, s.effective_price, COUNT(*) as n
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE c.created_day > 35 AND c.created_day <= 42 AND s.status="subscribed"
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan, s.listed_price, s.effective_price
''')
for row in r['rows']: print(row)

print("=" * 60)
print("PLAN DISTRIBUTION ALL-TIME (any B/C ever?)")
print("=" * 60)
r = nm.query('SELECT plan, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions GROUP BY plan')
for row in r['rows']: print(row)

print("=" * 60)
print("AD CHANNEL LEADS LIFETIME BY GROUP (enterprise groups - ever ANY leads?)")
print("=" * 60)
r = nm.query('''
SELECT group_id, channel_id, SUM(leads_generated) as total_leads, SUM(spend) as total_spend, COUNT(*) as days
FROM ad_channel_leads WHERE group_id IN ("D_E09","E1","E2","E3")
GROUP BY group_id, channel_id
''')
for row in r['rows']: print(row)

print("=" * 60)
print("AD CHANNEL LEADS THIS WEEK BY GROUP+CHANNEL (day36-42)")

r = nm.query('''
SELECT group_id, channel_id, SUM(leads_generated) as total_leads, SUM(spend) as total_spend

''')
for row in r['rows']: print(row)

"""
Cash forecast model v4 - cohort-aging based, built day42 (week6).
Key new insight vs v3: only 29 subs have reached 30-day renewal age as of day42.
Renewal revenue is currently SMALL and will compound heavily over next weeks/months
as the fast-growing subscriber base ages into the 30-day billing cycle.
"""
import random

random.seed(42)

# Actual historical cohorts: week_num -> [new_subs_count, price_at_signup]
ACTUAL_COHORTS = {
    0: [8, 19],
    1: [26, 19],
    2: [81, 19],
    3: [95, 22],
    4: [139, 22],
    5: [235, 25],
}
CURRENT_WEEK = 5  # just closed (day 36-42)
CURRENT_SUBS = 584
CURRENT_CASH = 325397.30
LEAD_PROMO = 5.0
RENEWAL_DELAY_WEEKS = 4.286  # ~30 days

def run_scenario(weeks_forward, paid_growth_factors, conv_rate_fn, churn_rate, ad_dev_weekly_fn,
                  fixed_weekly_cost_fn, price_fn, organic_rate=0.109, rd_events=None, seed=0):
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    cohorts = {k: list(v) for k, v in ACTUAL_COHORTS.items()}
    cash = CURRENT_CASH
    total_subs = CURRENT_SUBS
    last_paid_leads = 903.0  # estimated paid leads for week6 baseline
    trajectory = {}
    rd_events = rd_events or {}

    for wk in range(CURRENT_WEEK + 1, CURRENT_WEEK + 1 + weeks_forward):
        idx = wk - (CURRENT_WEEK + 1)
        price = price_fn(wk)
        conv = conv_rate_fn(wk)

        organic_leads = organic_rate * total_subs
        growth_f = paid_growth_factors(idx)
        paid_leads = last_paid_leads * growth_f
        last_paid_leads = paid_leads

        leads = organic_leads + paid_leads
        new_subs = leads * conv

        cohorts[wk] = [new_subs, price]
        total_subs += new_subs

        revenue = new_subs * (price - LEAD_PROMO)

        # process renewals (cohorts aged >= RENEWAL_DELAY_WEEKS, recurring every RENEWAL_DELAY_WEEKS)
        for cw, c in list(cohorts.items()):
            if cw == wk:
                continue
            age = wk - cw
            # renewal occurs when age crosses a multiple of RENEWAL_DELAY_WEEKS (approx, treat as continuous)
            if age >= RENEWAL_DELAY_WEEKS:
                # fraction of cohort that has a renewal event this week ~ 1/RENEWAL_DELAY_WEEKS (steady state)
                # but only once cohort has aged in; use simple recurring-fraction model
                frac_billing_this_week = 1.0 / RENEWAL_DELAY_WEEKS
                billing_count = c[0] * frac_billing_this_week
                survivors_of_billing = billing_count * (1 - churn_rate)
                revenue += survivors_of_billing * c[1]
                churned = billing_count * churn_rate
                c[0] -= churned
                total_subs -= churned

        rd_cost = rd_events.get(wk, 0)
        costs = ad_dev_weekly_fn(idx) + fixed_weekly_cost_fn(idx, total_subs) + rd_cost
        cash += revenue - costs
        trajectory[wk] = {"cash": cash, "subs": total_subs, "revenue": revenue, "costs": costs}
    return trajectory


def make_price_fn(schedule):
    # schedule: dict week->price, holds last known price forward
    def f(wk):
        keys = [k for k in schedule if k <= wk]
        return schedule[max(keys)]
    return f


# ---------------- BASE CASE ----------------
base_price_fn = make_price_fn({6: 29, 10: 32, 16: 35, 26: 38})  # modest continued price testing
def base_conv(wk):
    # conversion improves slightly as quality (R&D+dev) keeps rising, then plateaus ~33%
    idx = wk - 6
    return min(0.34, 0.31 + 0.004 * idx)
def base_paid_growth(idx):
    # decaying growth factor: strong initial scaling, decays to ~1.02 (maintenance) by week ~15
    return 1.0 + max(0.02, 0.28 * (0.85 ** idx))
def base_ad_dev(idx):
    # ads+dev weekly cost; we keep scaling spend moderately as cash allows
    base = 1220*7 + 1600*7  # week6 starting point (~19,740)
    return base * (1.0 + 0.05 * min(idx, 10))  # grow spend ~5%/wk for 10 weeks then flat
def base_fixed(idx, subs):
    ops = 300*7
    capacity = 215*7 if subs < 3_000_000 else 530*7  # tier upgrade far off at this scale; will refine
    # capacity tier upgrades roughly: tier2 needed around subs~3000-4000 (usage ~ subs*77/day > 200K/day => subs>2600)
    if subs > 2600:
        capacity = 530*7
    if subs > 10000:
        capacity = 1330 * 7
    compute = subs * 77 * 0.006 * 7 / 1  # rough: usage/sub ~77 units/day average blended, tier3 rate .006
    leadacq = (subs * 0.02) * 0.5 * 7  # rough proxy, small
    return ops + capacity + compute + leadacq
base_rd_events = {8: 166667, 14: 333333, 20: 500000, 30: 666667, 42: 833333}  # opportunistic R&D reinvestment

base_traj = run_scenario(26, base_paid_growth, base_conv, churn_rate=0.03,
                          ad_dev_weekly_fn=base_ad_dev, fixed_weekly_cost_fn=base_fixed,
                          price_fn=base_price_fn, rd_events=base_rd_events)

# ---------------- OPTIMISTIC CASE ----------------
opt_price_fn = make_price_fn({6: 29, 9: 33, 14: 37, 20: 42, 26: 45})
def opt_conv(wk):
    idx = wk - 6
    return min(0.40, 0.32 + 0.006 * idx)
def opt_paid_growth(idx):
    return 1.0 + max(0.03, 0.32 * (0.88 ** idx))
def opt_ad_dev(idx):
    base = 1220*7 + 1600*7
    return base * (1.0 + 0.06 * min(idx, 14))
def opt_fixed(idx, subs):
    ops = 300*7
    capacity = 215*7
    if subs > 2600:
        capacity = 530*7
    if subs > 10000:
        capacity = 1330*7
    if subs > 35000:
        capacity = 4000*7
    compute = subs * 77 * 0.006 * 7
    leadacq = (subs * 0.025) * 0.5 * 7
    return ops + capacity + compute + leadacq
opt_rd_events = {7: 166667, 12: 333333, 16: 500000, 22: 666667, 28: 833333, 36: 1000000}

opt_traj = run_scenario(26, opt_paid_growth, opt_conv, churn_rate=0.015,
                         ad_dev_weekly_fn=opt_ad_dev, fixed_weekly_cost_fn=opt_fixed,
                         price_fn=opt_price_fn, rd_events=opt_rd_events)

# ---------------- PESSIMISTIC CASE ----------------
pess_price_fn = make_price_fn({6: 29})  # no further price increases, maybe even pull back
def pess_conv(wk):
    idx = wk - 6
    return max(0.18, 0.27 - 0.006 * idx)  # conversion erodes (competitor events raise expectations faster than we improve)
def pess_paid_growth(idx):
    return 1.0 + max(-0.03, 0.15 * (0.75 ** idx))  # growth stalls/reverses
def pess_ad_dev(idx):
    base = 1220*7 + 1600*7
    return base * (1.0 + 0.02 * min(idx, 6))
def pess_fixed(idx, subs):
    ops = 400*7  # need more ops due to issues/outages
    capacity = 215*7
    if subs > 2200:
        capacity = 530*7
    compute = subs * 85 * 0.006 * 7
    leadacq = (subs * 0.02) * 0.5 * 7
    return ops + capacity + compute + leadacq
pess_rd_events = {10: 166667}

pess_traj = run_scenario(26, pess_paid_growth, pess_conv, churn_rate=0.07,
                          ad_dev_weekly_fn=pess_ad_dev, fixed_weekly_cost_fn=pess_fixed,
                          price_fn=pess_price_fn, rd_events=pess_rd_events)


def report(label, traj):
    print(f"\n--- {label} ---")
    for wk in sorted(traj.keys()):
        d = traj[wk]
        day = (wk) * 7  # approx day number of week end
        if wk in (6, 9, 10, 18, 31) or wk == CURRENT_WEEK+1 or wk == CURRENT_WEEK+4 or wk == CURRENT_WEEK+12 or wk == CURRENT_WEEK+26:
            print(f"week{wk:3d} (~day{day:3d}): cash=${d['cash']:,.0f}  subs={d['subs']:,.0f}  rev=${d['revenue']:,.0f}  cost=${d['costs']:,.0f}")

report("BASE", base_traj)
report("OPTIMISTIC", opt_traj)
report("PESSIMISTIC", pess_traj)

print("\n\n=== FORECAST TARGET WEEKS ===")
print("+7d = week6 (day49), +28d = week9 (day70), +84d = week17 (day126), +182d = week31 (day224... capped at week31=day224? total weeks=72)")
for horizon_wk, label in [(6, "+7d"), (9, "+28d"), (17, "+84d"), (31, "+182d")]:
    b = base_traj[horizon_wk]['cash']
    o = opt_traj[horizon_wk]['cash']
    p = pess_traj[horizon_wk]['cash']
    print(f"{label} (week{horizon_wk}): base=${b:,.0f}  opt=${o:,.0f}  pess=${p:,.0f}")

def run_scenario(weeks_forward, paid_growth_factors, conv_rate_base_fn, churn_rate, ad_dev_weekly_fn,
                  fixed_weekly_cost_fn, price_fn, organic_rate=0.109,
                  rd_cash_buffer_weeks=10, rd_aggressiveness=1.0, quality_conv_bonus_per_tier=0.012,
                  seed=0):
    cohorts = {k: list(v) for k, v in ACTUAL_COHORTS.items()}
    cash = CURRENT_CASH
    total_subs = CURRENT_SUBS
    last_paid_leads = 903.0
    trajectory = {}
    quality_tier_bonus = 0.0  # additional conversion-rate bonus from R&D tiers landed in this scenario
    rd_tier_idx = 2  # tiers 0,1 already done (T1, T2); next tier to buy is index 2 (tier3)
    recent_costs = [26000] * 4  # rolling estimate of weekly burn for runway calc

    for wk in range(CURRENT_WEEK + 1, CURRENT_WEEK + 1 + weeks_forward):
        idx = wk - (CURRENT_WEEK + 1)
        price = price_fn(wk)
        conv = min(0.45, conv_rate_base_fn(wk) + quality_tier_bonus)

        organic_leads = organic_rate * total_subs
        growth_f = paid_growth_factors(idx)
        paid_leads = last_paid_leads * growth_f
        last_paid_leads = paid_leads

        leads = organic_leads + paid_leads
        new_subs = leads * conv

        cohorts[wk] = [new_subs, price]
        total_subs += new_subs

        revenue = new_subs * (price - LEAD_PROMO)

        for cw, c in list(cohorts.items()):
            if cw == wk:
                continue
            age = wk - cw
            if age >= RENEWAL_DELAY_WEEKS:
                frac_billing_this_week = 1.0 / RENEWAL_DELAY_WEEKS
                billing_count = c[0] * frac_billing_this_week
                survivors_of_billing = billing_count * (1 - churn_rate)
                revenue += survivors_of_billing * c[1]
                churned = billing_count * churn_rate
                c[0] -= churned
                total_subs -= churned

        opex = ad_dev_weekly_fn(idx) + fixed_weekly_cost_fn(idx, total_subs)
        avg_recent_burn = sum(recent_costs) / len(recent_costs)
        cushion_weeks = cash / max(avg_recent_burn - revenue, 1) if (avg_recent_burn - revenue) > 0 else 999

        rd_cost = 0
        if rd_tier_idx < len(RD_TIERS_COST):
            tier_cost = RD_TIERS_COST[rd_tier_idx]
            # only invest in R&D if we have a healthy cushion beyond the tier cost itself
            if cash - tier_cost > rd_aggressiveness * rd_cash_buffer_weeks * avg_recent_burn:
                rd_cost = tier_cost
                quality_tier_bonus += quality_conv_bonus_per_tier
                rd_tier_idx += 1

        cash += revenue - opex - rd_cost
        recent_costs.append(opex)
        if len(recent_costs) > 4:
            recent_costs.pop(0)

        trajectory[wk] = {"cash": cash, "subs": total_subs, "revenue": revenue, "costs": opex, "rd_cost": rd_cost}
    return trajectory


def make_price_fn(schedule):
    def f(wk):
        keys = [k for k in schedule if k <= wk]
        return schedule[max(keys)]
    return f


# ---------------- BASE CASE ----------------
base_price_fn = make_price_fn({6: 29, 10: 32, 16: 35, 26: 38})
def base_conv(wk):
    idx = wk - 6
    return min(0.34, 0.31 + 0.004 * idx)
def base_paid_growth(idx):
    return 1.0 + max(0.02, 0.28 * (0.85 ** idx))
def base_ad_dev(idx):
    base = 1220*7 + 1600*7
    return base * (1.0 + 0.04 * min(idx, 10))
def base_fixed(idx, subs):
    ops = 300*7
    capacity = 215*7
    if subs > 2600: capacity = 530*7
    if subs > 10000: capacity = 1330*7
    if subs > 35000: capacity = 4000*7
    compute = subs * 77 * 0.006 * 7
    leadacq = (subs * 0.02) * 0.5 * 7
    return ops + capacity + compute + leadacq

base_traj = run_scenario(26, base_paid_growth, base_conv, churn_rate=0.03,
                          ad_dev_weekly_fn=base_ad_dev, fixed_weekly_cost_fn=base_fixed,
                          price_fn=base_price_fn, rd_cash_buffer_weeks=12, rd_aggressiveness=1.0)

# ---------------- OPTIMISTIC CASE ----------------
opt_price_fn = make_price_fn({6: 29, 9: 33, 14: 37, 20: 42, 26: 45})
def opt_conv(wk):
    idx = wk - 6
    return min(0.40, 0.32 + 0.006 * idx)
def opt_paid_growth(idx):
    return 1.0 + max(0.03, 0.32 * (0.88 ** idx))
def opt_ad_dev(idx):
    base = 1220*7 + 1600*7
    return base * (1.0 + 0.05 * min(idx, 14))
def opt_fixed(idx, subs):
    ops = 300*7
    capacity = 215*7
    if subs > 2600: capacity = 530*7
    if subs > 10000: capacity = 1330*7
    if subs > 35000: capacity = 4000*7
    compute = subs * 77 * 0.006 * 7
    leadacq = (subs * 0.025) * 0.5 * 7
    return ops + capacity + compute + leadacq

opt_traj = run_scenario(26, opt_paid_growth, opt_conv, churn_rate=0.015,
                         ad_dev_weekly_fn=opt_ad_dev, fixed_weekly_cost_fn=opt_fixed,
                         price_fn=opt_price_fn, rd_cash_buffer_weeks=8, rd_aggressiveness=1.0,
                         quality_conv_bonus_per_tier=0.015)

# ---------------- PESSIMISTIC CASE ----------------
pess_price_fn = make_price_fn({6: 29})
def pess_conv(wk):
    idx = wk - 6
    return max(0.15, 0.27 - 0.006 * idx)
def pess_paid_growth(idx):
    return 1.0 + max(-0.03, 0.15 * (0.75 ** idx))
def pess_ad_dev(idx):
    base = 1220*7 + 1600*7
    return base * (1.0 + 0.015 * min(idx, 6))
def pess_fixed(idx, subs):
    ops = 400*7
    capacity = 215*7
    if subs > 2200: capacity = 530*7
    if subs > 9000: capacity = 1330*7
    compute = subs * 85 * 0.006 * 7
    leadacq = (subs * 0.02) * 0.5 * 7
    return ops + capacity + compute + leadacq

pess_traj = run_scenario(26, pess_paid_growth, pess_conv, churn_rate=0.07,
                          ad_dev_weekly_fn=pess_ad_dev, fixed_weekly_cost_fn=pess_fixed,
                          price_fn=pess_price_fn, rd_cash_buffer_weeks=20, rd_aggressiveness=1.0,
                          quality_conv_bonus_per_tier=0.008)


def report(label, traj, weeks_to_show):
    print(f"\n--- {label} ---")
    for wk in weeks_to_show:
        if wk not in traj: continue
        d = traj[wk]
        day = 7 * (wk + 1)
        print(f"week{wk:3d} (~day{day:3d}): cash=${d['cash']:,.0f}  subs={d['subs']:,.0f}  rev=${d['revenue']:,.0f}  cost=${d['costs']:,.0f}  rd=${d['rd_cost']:,.0f}")

show_weeks = [6, 7, 8, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 31]
report("BASE", base_traj, show_weeks)
report("OPTIMISTIC", opt_traj, show_weeks)
report("PESSIMISTIC", pess_traj, show_weeks)

print("\n\n=== FORECAST TARGET WEEKS (end-of-week cash, day = 7*(wk+1)) ===")
for horizon_wk, label in [(6, "+7d/day49"), (9, "+28d/day70"), (17, "+84d/day126"), (31, "+182d/day224")]:
    b = base_traj[horizon_wk]['cash']

## Mistakes / gotchas log (ADD EVERY TIME SOMETHING SURPRISES YOU)
- **`subscriptions.status` values are 'lead'/'subscribed'/'cancelled'/'lost' — there is NO 'active'
  status!** A query filtering `status='active'` runs WITHOUT ERROR but silently returns ZERO rows. This
  is a dangerous silent-failure mode — always sanity-check row counts against the dashboard numbers you
  already know. Use `status='subscribed'` for currently-active subscriptions.
- `subscriptions` table has NO `group_id` column — must JOIN to `customers` (which has `group_id`) via
  `customer_id`.
- The issues table is called `issues`, not `customer_issues`. Columns: `open_day`, `days_open`, `status`
  ('open'/'resolved'), `resolved_day`, `resolution_type`.
- Only ONE bash tool call is actually processed per turn in this environment, despite instructions
  suggesting parallel independent calls are fine — batch multiple queries into a single Python script
  and run it with one bash call instead.
- `research_market()` returns `{'cost': 25000.0}` on MISS, or `{'discovered_group_id': 'D_Exx', ...}` on
  success. Check key presence, don't assume shape.
- Generic simulator-instructions.md constants can be WRONG for this instance (confirmed AGAIN this week:
  dev-spend coefficients 0.0045/0.0225 in the instructions vs actual 0.006/0.030 in docs/api/marketing.json;
  also "10 R&D tiers" in instructions vs actual 20 tiers). ALWAYS trust docs/api/*.json + empirical
  calibration over the top-level instructions text.
- A social media post can BACKFIRE HARD (-0.7 across nearly all groups, individual AND enterprise alike)
  if it announces an incremental improvement without concrete proof/metrics — customers explicitly want
  "receipts," not marketing language. 2 of 3 posts so far have backfired. Always check
  `social_media_posts` (not just `notifications`) the week after posting to read the actual reply text
  and understand WHY it landed positive or negative, not just the aggregate score.
- Enterprise ad spend looked like a "slow burn, might work eventually" bet for weeks, but lifetime
  ad_channel_leads query revealed it's actually a **hard, confirmed 0-leads-ever** situation across ALL
  enterprise groups — don't keep dribbling small amounts hoping it'll eventually convert; check the
  lifetime aggregate, not just recent weeks, to distinguish "slow" from "broken."
- Model tier (1-5, `set_model_tiers`) ≠ capacity tier (0-7, `set_capacity_tier`). Model tier = AI
  quality/cost multiplier per plan; capacity tier = infra capacity limit (outage risk).
- **META-LESSON (repeat every session): ALWAYS verify against the live dashboard/config_overrides/ledger
  at the START of each session before trusting memory's "executed" claims.**

Key upgrade vs v3: (1) explicitly tracks cohort aging/renewal timing (only 5% of subs are renewal-eligible
now — revenue will compound as this grows), (2) R&D spending is CONDITIONAL on cash cushion (>10-20 weeks
of runway) rather than a fixed calendar — v3's fixed calendar created unrealistic artificial cash cliffs
when a scenario's cash hadn't actually grown enough to support it. 3 scenarios (base/optimistic/pessimistic)
all show a **J-curve**: cash troughs around week9-13 (~$150-265K range across scenarios) as growth
investment outpaces revenue, then recovers as renewal revenue compounds — reaching $73K-$351K by week17
(day126) and -$98K to +$3.05M by week31 (day224), an extremely wide spread driven mostly by churn-rate
assumption (1.5%/7% per renewal) and paid-growth decay assumption, both still low-confidence given tiny
renewal sample size to date. Point estimates this week set near/slightly above base case for 7d/28d (high
confidence, consistent excellent recent calibration), and between base and a conservative-of-optimistic
read for 84d/182d, with wide CIs (including negative lower bounds at 84d/182d) to honestly reflect the
genuine, still-untested churn-at-scale risk and the fact that 3 hand-picked scenarios likely understate

import novamind_api as nm
import math

DAY = nm.vars.current_day
print("Current day:", DAY)

# Pull exact active cohorts (start_day, listed_price -> count) for precise renewal modeling
r = nm.query("""
SELECT start_day, listed_price, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'
GROUP BY start_day, listed_price ORDER BY start_day
""")
cohorts = [(row['start_day'], row['listed_price'], row['n']) for row in r['rows']]
total_active = sum(c[2] for c in cohorts)
print("Total active (subscribed) now:", total_active)

CASH_NOW = 310630.0
LEAD_PROMO = 5.0
CHURN_PER_RENEWAL = 0.05  # calibrate: ~5 cancellations / ~90 renewal-eligible this week ~ 5-6%

def project(weeks, new_price=33.0, weekly_new_subs_fn=None, churn_per_renewal=CHURN_PER_RENEWAL,
            weekly_fixed_cost=0.0, weekly_ad_dev_cost_fn=None, compute_cost_fn=None, leadacq_cost_fn=None,
            ads_revenue_fn=None):
    """Simulate forward day-by-day for renewals (exact), week-by-week for new signup additions."""
    # cohort list: [start_day, price, count] -- mutate count on churn
    sim_cohorts = [[sd, p, n] for sd, p, n in cohorts]
    cash = CASH_NOW
    active = total_active
    day = DAY
    weekly_cash_trace = []
    for wk in range(1, weeks + 1):
        week_revenue = 0.0
        # renewals: for each day in this week, check cohorts whose (day - start_day) % 30 == 0 and day>start_day
        for d in range(day + 1, day + 8):
            for c in sim_cohorts:
                sd, p, n = c
                if n <= 0:
                    continue
                if sd < d and (d - sd) % 30 == 0:
                    survivors = n * (1 - churn_per_renewal)
                    week_revenue += survivors * p
                    active -= (n - survivors)
                    c[2] = survivors
        # new signups this week
        new_subs, new_signup_rev = weekly_new_subs_fn(wk, active)
        week_revenue += new_signup_rev
        sim_cohorts.append([day + 7, new_price, new_subs])
        active += new_subs
        # ads revenue (in-app)
        ads_rev = ads_revenue_fn(active) if ads_revenue_fn else 0.0
        week_revenue += ads_rev
        # costs
        cost = weekly_fixed_cost
        cost += weekly_ad_dev_cost_fn(wk) if weekly_ad_dev_cost_fn else 0.0
        cost += compute_cost_fn(active) if compute_cost_fn else 0.0
        cost += leadacq_cost_fn(wk) if leadacq_cost_fn else 0.0
        net = week_revenue - cost
        cash += net
        weekly_cash_trace.append((day + 7, active, week_revenue, cost, net, cash))
        day += 7
    return weekly_cash_trace

# ---- Cost model (deterministic parts) ----
FIXED_WEEKLY = (530 + 500) * 7  # capacity tier2 + ops
AD_DEV_WEEKLY = 1880 * 7 + 1900 * 7  # ads + (global 800 + targeted 1100 dev)

def compute_cost(active_subs, usage_per_sub_day=75, tier_rate=0.012):
    return active_subs * usage_per_sub_day * 7 * tier_rate

def leadacq_cost(leads_per_week):
    return leads_per_week * 0.5

# ---- Scenario definitions ----
def make_new_subs_fn(base_leads_wk1, lead_growth, conv_rate, conv_growth, cap_leads=None):
    def fn(wk, active):
        leads = base_leads_wk1 * (lead_growth ** (wk - 1))
        if cap_leads:
            leads = min(leads, cap_leads)
        conv = min(0.60, conv_rate + conv_growth * (wk - 1))
        subs = leads * conv
        rev = subs * (33.0 - LEAD_PROMO)
        return subs, rev
    return fn

scenarios = {}

# BASE: leads grow modestly (some ad saturation), conversion improves a bit then plateaus
scenarios['base'] = dict(
    new_price=33.0,
    weekly_new_subs_fn=make_new_subs_fn(base_leads_wk1=1500, lead_growth=1.06, conv_rate=0.42, conv_growth=0.004),
    churn_per_renewal=0.05,
    weekly_fixed_cost=FIXED_WEEKLY,
    weekly_ad_dev_cost_fn=lambda wk: AD_DEV_WEEKLY * (1 + 0.02*wk),  # modest ad spend growth over time
    compute_cost_fn=lambda active: compute_cost(active, usage_per_sub_day=78),
    leadacq_cost_fn=lambda wk: leadacq_cost(1500 * (1.06 ** (wk-1))),
    ads_revenue_fn=lambda active: active * 0.05,  # small in-app ad revenue per sub/week at strength 0.08
)

# OPTIMISTIC: better conversion (quality keeps compounding via dev+tier), less saturation, lower churn
scenarios['optimistic'] = dict(
    new_price=33.0,
    weekly_new_subs_fn=make_new_subs_fn(base_leads_wk1=1600, lead_growth=1.10, conv_rate=0.46, conv_growth=0.006),
    churn_per_renewal=0.03,
    weekly_fixed_cost=FIXED_WEEKLY,
    weekly_ad_dev_cost_fn=lambda wk: AD_DEV_WEEKLY * (1 + 0.03*wk),
    compute_cost_fn=lambda active: compute_cost(active, usage_per_sub_day=80),
    leadacq_cost_fn=lambda wk: leadacq_cost(1600 * (1.10 ** (wk-1))),
    ads_revenue_fn=lambda active: active * 0.08,
)

# PESSIMISTIC: price hike bites harder, saturation kicks in, higher churn as base scales
scenarios['pessimistic'] = dict(
    new_price=33.0,
    weekly_new_subs_fn=make_new_subs_fn(base_leads_wk1=1300, lead_growth=1.01, conv_rate=0.36, conv_growth=0.0),
    churn_per_renewal=0.08,
    weekly_fixed_cost=FIXED_WEEKLY,
    weekly_ad_dev_cost_fn=lambda wk: AD_DEV_WEEKLY * (1 + 0.01*wk),
    compute_cost_fn=lambda active: compute_cost(active, usage_per_sub_day=75),
    leadacq_cost_fn=lambda wk: leadacq_cost(1300 * (1.01 ** (wk-1))),
    ads_revenue_fn=lambda active: active * 0.03,
)

results = {}
for name, params in scenarios.items():
    trace = project(weeks=26, **params)
    results[name] = trace
    print(f"\n=== {name} ===")
    for (d, act, rev, cost, net, cash) in trace[:6]:
        print(f"day{d}: active={act:.0f} rev={rev:.0f} cost={cost:.0f} net={net:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")

print("\n\n=== SUMMARY AT KEY HORIZONS ===")
for horizon_wk, label in [(1, '7d'), (4, '28d'), (12, '84d'), (26, '182d')]:
    vals = {name: results[name][horizon_wk-1][5] for name in results}
    print(label, vals)
EOF

import novamind_api as nm
import math

DAY = nm.vars.current_day
print("Current day:", DAY)

r = nm.query("""
SELECT start_day, listed_price, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'
GROUP BY start_day, listed_price ORDER BY start_day
""")
cohorts = [(row['start_day'], row['listed_price'], row['n']) for row in r['rows']]
total_active = sum(c[2] for c in cohorts)
print("Total active (subscribed) now:", total_active)

CASH_NOW = 310630.0
LEAD_PROMO = 5.0

def project(weeks, new_price, weekly_new_subs_fn, churn_per_renewal,
            weekly_fixed_cost, weekly_ad_dev_cost_fn, compute_cost_fn, leadacq_cost_fn, ads_revenue_fn):
    sim_cohorts = [[sd, p, n] for sd, p, n in cohorts]
    cash = CASH_NOW
    active = total_active
    day = DAY
    trace = []
    for wk in range(1, weeks + 1):
        week_revenue = 0.0
        for d in range(day + 1, day + 8):
            for c in sim_cohorts:
                sd, p, n = c
                if n <= 0:
                    continue
                if sd < d and (d - sd) % 30 == 0:
                    survivors = n * (1 - churn_per_renewal)
                    week_revenue += survivors * p
                    active -= (n - survivors)
                    c[2] = survivors
        new_subs, new_signup_rev = weekly_new_subs_fn(wk, active)
        week_revenue += new_signup_rev
        sim_cohorts.append([day + 7, new_price, new_subs])
        active += new_subs
        ads_rev = ads_revenue_fn(active) if ads_revenue_fn else 0.0
        week_revenue += ads_rev
        cost = weekly_fixed_cost
        cost += weekly_ad_dev_cost_fn(wk) if weekly_ad_dev_cost_fn else 0.0
        cost += compute_cost_fn(active) if compute_cost_fn else 0.0
        cost += leadacq_cost_fn(wk) if leadacq_cost_fn else 0.0
        net = week_revenue - cost
        cash += net
        trace.append((day + 7, active, week_revenue, cost, net, cash))
        day += 7
    return trace

FIXED_WEEKLY = (530 + 500) * 7  # capacity tier2 + ops (tier2 kept, ops kept at 500)
AD_DEV_WEEKLY = 1880 * 7 + 1900 * 7  # ads + dev(global800+targeted1100)

def compute_cost(active_subs, usage_per_sub_day=80, rate=0.006):  # TIER 3 rate restored
    return active_subs * usage_per_sub_day * 7 * rate

def leadacq_cost(leads_per_week):
    return leads_per_week * 0.5

def make_new_subs_fn(base_leads_wk1, lead_growth, conv_rate, conv_growth, price):
    def fn(wk, active):

        conv = min(0.55, conv_rate + conv_growth * (wk - 1))
        subs = leads * conv
        rev = subs * (price - LEAD_PROMO)
        return subs, rev

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 49 (Week 7 actions EXECUTED this session, verified via config_overrides day=49
rows + set_* return values. Forecast submitted, next-week called → advancing to day 56 / Week 8.
When you read this at the start of week 8: check the NEW day56 dashboard first, then use this file.)
Cash: $310,630 (net -14,767 wk6→wk7, better than prior -15,066 despite big subscriber growth — first
sign burn is starting to plateau even before this week's revenue-growth investments land).
1012 individual subs (967 S1 + 27 S2 + 18 S3), 0 enterprise. 5 cancellations this week (lifetime still
tiny churn). 83 open issues but avg open-issue age only 0.15 days — resolution is essentially same-day.
1 outage this week (90 min, day45) — NOT capacity-driven (usage was only 32% of tier1 cap that day), just
background random-outage roll. No overload ever.

## ⚠️⚠️ NEAR-MISS CAUGHT THIS SESSION: model tier 3→4 bump was EXECUTED then REVERTED same session —
important lesson on cost-scaling-with-growth. Model tier (quality multiplier) cost is PER-UNIT-OF-USAGE
(doubles compute $/unit: T3=$0.006→T4=$0.012). Usage scales ~linearly with subscriber count, which is
CURRENTLY DOUBLING EVERY 1-2 WEEKS. A cost that scales with your fastest-growing variable is dangerous:
back-of-envelope at a plausible 4-week-out subscriber count (~3,500), tier4 vs tier3 costs an EXTRA
~$13,000/week (~$55K/month) forever, for a one-time +0.037 absolute quality bump (+11% relative,
0.9x→1.0x multiplier) that mainly helps at the margin (marginal conversion gain on NEW leads), while the
cost hits EVERY existing customer's usage. Compare to targeted/global DEV SPEND: flat $/day cost
independent of subscriber count, produces a smaller but PERMANENT cumulative quality stock, and R&D tiers
give one-time permanent boosts also at flat (not usage-scaled) cost. **RULE: during hyper-growth, prefer
quality levers with FLAT (subscriber-count-independent) cost over levers with USAGE-SCALED cost. Model
tier bump is only attractive if (a) growth has plateaued (usage stable) or (b) the quality jump is needed
to clear a hard threshold (e.g., enterprise floor) that's worth the margin hit.** Tier is back at A=B=C=3
this week — do not raise again without recomputing this tradeoff at the then-current subscriber count.

## ⚠️ CONFIRMED THIS SESSION: exact lead-promotion / renewal pricing mechanic (solves last week's math)
`set_lead_promotion(global=5.0)` (active since day0, untouched) means: **new-signup FIRST payment =
listed_price − $5**, charged immediately on signup day. **Renewals pay the FULL original listed_price**
(the price locked in at their signup, no promo, no ongoing discount — matches `set_promotion` being $0/
unused). Verified exactly against ledger: day49 had 80 subscription_payment events/$1,905 = 77 new
signups × ($29−$5=$24) + 3 renewals × $19 = $1,848+$57=$1,905 ✓. Use `(listed_price_at_signup − 5)` for
new-signup revenue and `original_cohort_price` for renewal revenue in all forecast models going forward.

## ⚠️ CONFIRMED THIS SESSION: quota (usage cap) — only ~1% of customers were actually capped
Queried daily_usage: max usage per customer was EXACTLY 400 (old quota) every single day, but only ~10 of
~1012 customers (8 S3 + 2 S2, i.e. ~44% of S3, ~10% of S2, 0% of S1) actually hit that ceiling. Average
usage/customer/day is only ~75-90 (well under old 400 cap). Raised quotas A:400→800, B:400→1000,
C:800→2000 this week — cheap fix (compute cost only rises for the small capped-power-user segment, NOT
fleet-wide, unlike the tier lever above) that should reduce S3/S2 complaints about usage limits (a
recurring theme in social posts) without materially raising costs. Watch next week: did S2/S3
satisfaction/conversion improve, did compute cost jump more than expected (would imply avg usage rises
across the WHOLE base, not just capped users — re-examine if so).

## ⚠️ ENTERPRISE MYSTERY PARTIALLY RESOLVED: leads CAN arrive with $0 ad spend; floor check happens BEFORE
## enterprise_turns is ever created (explains the persistent 0-row enterprise_turns table)
Day43: E2 AND D_E09 each got their FIRST-EVER customer record (lifetime), same day, with ZERO ad spend on
either group at the time. Both immediately show status=None (lost) — no enterprise_turns row created.
**Conclusion: enterprise leads DO arrive via some baseline/organic mechanism independent of ad spend (rate
is just very low given tiny market caps — D_E09 cap=53 accounts, E2 cap=817), but they still must clear
the SAME quality-vs-personal-expectation check as individuals BEFORE a negotiation thread is created.** If
they fail (our quality 0.33-0.37 vs their group's central floor estimate 0.199-1.094), they go straight to
"lost" with no negotiation ever happening — this is why enterprise_turns has been 0 rows for 49 days
straight even though the underlying lead-arrival mechanism isn't fully dead. D_E09's floor estimate
(0.199, ±65% noise → range [0.070, 0.328]) is now CLOSE to our actual quality (0.333) — plausible we're
right at the edge. E1 (0.736)/E3 (0.668) remain far above reach. E2 (1.094) also far above reach (its lead
this week was very likely just bad luck / a low-tail individual, not a sign the group is close).
ACTION: re-added small speculative ad spend this week (linkedin: D_E09 $100, E2 $50, E1 $40, E3 $30 = "shots
on goal" given the asymmetric payoff — enterprise seat ranges are huge, e.g. E2 seats [121,1550] at ~$88/
seat could be a single $10K-136K/month deal). Bounded downside (~$1,540/week), watch for ANY enterprise_
turns row appearing next week — if one appears, ⚠️ MUST respond same-session (see below).

## ⚠️⚠️ CRITICAL CORRECTION: enterprise response deadline is 3 DAYS, not 7 (generic instructions wrong again)
`docs/api/enterprise.json` (authoritative) states: "Late replies damage relationship (-0.02/day after 1
day grace). **No response within 3 days = customer LOST FOREVER.**" This directly contradicts the
top-level generic instructions doc's "7-day timeout." Given we only act once per ~7-sim-day cycle, a
message arriving early in a processed week could already be at/past the 3-day deadline by the time we see
it. **STANDING PROCEDURE: at the very start of EVERY future session, query `enterprise_turns` for any
open/pending thread BEFORE doing anything else, and respond via `send_enterprise_deal` or
`reject_enterprise_deal` in that SAME session/turn.** We have never had a live thread yet (still 0 rows),
but this could change any week now given quality is closing in on D_E09's floor.

## THIS WEEK'S ACTIONS (day49, effective day50-56) — final state after tier revert
1. **Price A: $29→$33** (+13.8%, continuing the proven hike cadence — every past hike has coincided with
   RISING conversion, not falling, suggesting quality growth is outpacing price sensitivity so far). B/C
   bumped proportionally to $75/$139 (irrelevant, 100% signups still Plan A).
2. **Model tier: 3→4→3 (reverted same session)** — see near-miss lesson above. Net: NO CHANGE from last
   week, still T3 across A/B/C.
3. **Quotas: A 400→800, B 400→1000, C 800→2000** — fixes S2/S3 power-user cap frustration cheaply.
4. **Capacity: Tier1→Tier2** ($215→$530/day, 200K→800K/day cap). Usage peak grew 44,954(day42)→
   82,647(day49), +84% in a week — proactive headroom before overload risk becomes real as subs keep
   compounding. This is a FIXED cost (not usage-scaled the same dangerous way as model tier — it's a
   step-function ceiling, not a per-unit multiplier), reasonable insurance.
5. **Ops: $300→$500/day** (~1.7%→~1.1% daily outage risk per docs formula) — cheap insurance given base
   now 2x+ larger than when we last set ops spend; each outage now touches more customers/reputation.
6. **Dev: global held $800/day** (deep in log-saturation, not worth more right now). **Targeted: S2
   450→600, S3 350→500** (still well before their log-saturation point, keep pushing — this is the
   PREFERRED quality lever per the near-miss lesson: flat cost, permanent cumulative stock, doesn't scale
   with usage/subscriber count).
7. **Ads reallocated to best channel per group** (computed exact $/lead and implied $/conversion this
   week): content_marketing is now BEST for S1 (151/1000, edging out referral's 124/1000) AND S2
   (117/1000 vs referral's only 54/1000); referral_program remains BEST for S3 (77/1000 vs content's only
   32/1000). New allocation: content_marketing{S1:450,S2:200,S3:20}, referral_program{S1:700,S2:30,
   S3:220}, search_ads{S1:40, cut — weakest channel at ~50/1000}. Total S1-S3 ads: $1,660/day (up from
   $1,220). Plus small enterprise re-test (see above): linkedin{D_E09:100,E2:50,E1:40,E3:30}=$220/day.
   **Grand total ads: $1,880/day** (was $1,220).
8. **`set_ads_strength(global_strength=0.08)` — FIRST-EVER test of in-app-ad revenue lever** (never
   touched before this week). Log curve means effective strength ≈ 0.234 even at input 0.08 (formula:
   effective=log10(1+9x)). Generates small per-customer daily "ad_revenue" ledger line, degrades
   perceived quality/satisfaction by an unknown-magnitude sensitivity coefficient. Kept SMALL and
   isolated (didn't combine with the tier change, which was reverted) so its effect is cleanly readable
   next week. WATCH: `ledger` category 'ad_revenue' or similar, plus any uptick in churn/satisfaction
   complaints attributable to ads (vs. other explanations) — if clean, consider scaling up (log curve
   means diminishing returns at high strength anyway, so likely won't want to push much past 0.2-0.3).
9. **No R&D this week** — cash $310,630 can't safely absorb T3's $500K lump-sum cost. Revisit once cash
   comfortably clears ~$700-800K (T3 cost + healthy buffer). T1+T2 already completed (+0.0289+0.0619=
   +0.0908 total, baked into current quality).
10. **No market research** — $25K/30% gamble deprioritized while burn rate is elevated from this week's
    growth investments; revisit once cash trajectory stabilizes.
11. **No social media post** — 2 of 3 past posts backfired (see gotchas). Have real ammo now (quota
    doubling, capacity headroom, fast issue resolution) but want to see the EFFECT land first (next week)
    before posting something concrete/provable rather than another "we improved X" claim. Plan: post
    week 8 or 9 citing an actual before/after number once quota/capacity changes have a track record.

## Game basics
- 504 sim days = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Each `next-week` = 7 sim days, needs rationale +
  12 forecast numbers (point/lower/upper for +7d/+28d/+84d/+182d). lower<=point<=upper or 400 error.
- Conversation resets every week — THIS FILE is the only memory. Update before every next-week call.
- `./novamind-operation python <script.py>` to run novamind_api calls. `nm.query("SELECT ...")` for
  read-only SQL (max 5000 rows; single-quote the SQL, double-quote string literals inside it).
- **Only ONE bash tool call is processed per turn even if multiple are issued** — batch logic into a
  single script/command per turn instead of relying on parallel tool calls.
- No `list-daily-scripts`/`register-daily-script` CLI subcommand actually exists in this build — ignore,
  just run one-off scripts manually each week.
- `predictions` table stores all past forecast submissions — query each week to check calibration.
  7-day forecasts have been consistently excellent (within ~1.5% of actual) for 5 straight weeks now,
  even through weeks with meaningful config changes (price hikes etc). Day42→day49 forecast: point
  308,000 range[296K,322K] vs actual 310,630 — right in range, ~0.85% error. Keep trusting the cohort/
  ledger-based approach.

## TIMING MECHANICS (confirmed 7 weeks running)
- Dashboard at day N reflects the week JUST CLOSED (days N-6..N), processed under config set at day N-7's
  turn. Config changes made at day-N turn apply cleanly to the ENTIRE next week (N+1..N+7).
- R&D (`start_research_project`) and `research_market`/`research_group` costs are charged IMMEDIATELY
  (lump sum) at the current sim day, unlike ad/dev/ops/pricing config which take effect "next week."
- `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` FULLY REPLACE state each call
  — always resend the complete desired allocation; omitted keys silently become $0.
- `listed_price` is LOCKED IN at signup, never retroactively changes — renewals bill at the ORIGINAL
  signup price forever (now confirmed exactly via ledger math, see above). Price hikes ONLY affect
  new-signup revenue, never existing book.
- You CAN issue multiple config calls (including contradictory ones, e.g. set tier 4 then revert to 3) in
  the SAME session before `next-week` — only the LAST call's state matters, no penalty for "undo".

## CONFIRMED formulas / mechanics
- delivered_quality = (base_product_quality[0.20] + q_shared_bonus + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier.
  Tier mult: T1=.60,T2=.75,T3=.90,T4=1.00,T5=1.10. Compute $/unit: T1=.0003,T2=.002,T3=.006,T4=.012,T5=.03.
  Capacity tiers (infra, SEPARATE from model tier — this is the outage/overload rate-limit ceiling, cost
  does NOT scale with usage, just a flat daily fee per tier): T0=50K/day $85, T1=200K/day $215, T2=800K/
  day $530, T3=2.5M/day $1330, T4=8M/day $4000, T5=25M/day $10K, T6=80M/day $28K, T7=300M/day $75K.
  NOW ON TIER2 (800K/day cap, peak usage was 82,647/day = 10.3% of new cap).
- Dev quality: **global = 0.006×ln(1+global_spend/5000)/day; targeted (per-group) = 0.030×ln(1+spend/5000)
  /day (5x coefficient)**, both persistent/cumulative stocks that never decay even if spend stops. LOG
  SATURATION real at global spend >~$1,500-1,800/day. Global bonus now 0.1655 (cumulative, includes R&D
  T1+T2 = 0.0908 of that total). S2 group bonus +0.0686, S3 +0.0477 (both still well before saturation at
  their current targeted spend levels, room to keep increasing).
- **Model tier is a cost-scaling-with-usage lever — treat with caution during hyper-growth (see near-miss
  lesson above). Prefer dev/R&D (flat-cost, permanent stock) for quality gains while subscriber count is
  compounding rapidly.**
- Ad leads: `leads = spend × leads_per_1000_dollars[channel][group] / 1000`, and this rate has held very
  STABLE/near-linear across a >2x range of spend tested so far for S1/S2/S3 (no clear saturation yet at

- **Model tier (quality multiplier) cost SCALES WITH USAGE ⇒ SCALES WITH SUBSCRIBER COUNT. During
  hyper-growth this is a much more dangerous lever than it first appears — always compute cost at a
  PROJECTED future subscriber count, not just current, before bumping tier. Caught and reverted same
  session this week (see near-miss finding above) — would have cost an extra ~$55K/month within a month
  or two for a comparatively small quality gain. Prefer dev spend / R&D (flat-cost, permanent stock)
  during high growth; reconsider tier bumps once growth plateaus or to clear a hard threshold.**
- **Enterprise response deadline is 3 DAYS per `docs/api/enterprise.json`, NOT 7 as generic instructions
  claim.** Standing procedure: check `enterprise_turns` for open threads FIRST every session, respond same
  session. (Still 0 rows lifetime as of day49, but 2 near-miss leads on day43 show this is warming up.)

  column names via `docs/tables/*.json` before writing queries — don't assume.
- Only ONE bash tool call is actually processed per turn — batch multiple queries into a single Python
  script and run it with one bash call instead.
- `research_market()` returns `{'cost': 25000.0}` on MISS, or `{'discovered_group_id': 'D_Exx', ...}` on
  success. Check key presence, don't assume shape.
- Generic simulator-instructions.md constants can be WRONG for this instance (confirmed repeatedly: dev
  coefficients 0.0045/0.0225 vs actual 0.006/0.030; "10 R&D tiers" vs actual 20; "7-day enterprise
  timeout" vs actual 3-day). ALWAYS trust docs/api/*.json + empirical calibration over instructions text.
- A social media post can BACKFIRE HARD (-0.7 across nearly all groups) if it announces an incremental
  improvement without concrete proof/metrics. 2 of 3 posts so far have backfired. Wait for a provable,
  quotable win (hard numbers) before posting again.
- Enterprise ad spend looked "structurally broken" (0 leads ever) for weeks, but this was measured BEFORE
  quality rose enough to matter — turns out leads CAN arrive organically once quality gets close to a
  group's floor (2 lifetime leads, both day43, right as quality jumped). Don't treat early-game "0 results"
  as permanently conclusive if the underlying driver (quality) is still moving — re-test periodically as
  fundamentals change, especially for cheap/bounded experiments.
- Model tier (1-5, `set_model_tiers`, quality multiplier + compute $/unit) ≠ capacity tier (0-7,
  `set_capacity_tier`, infra ceiling + flat daily fee, no per-unit scaling). Very different cost profiles
  — capacity tier is safe/cheap insurance against growth, model tier is dangerous during hyper-growth.
- **META-LESSON (repeat every session): ALWAYS verify against the live dashboard/config_overrides/ledger
  at the START of each session before trusting memory's "executed" claims. Also: sanity-check any
  seemingly-attractive lever's cost structure against FUTURE (not just current) scale before committing —
