# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 84 (Week 12 actions EXECUTED this session). Forecast submitted, next-week called
→ advancing to day 91 / Week 13. Cash: $176,588 (net -40,673 wk11→wk12, second brutal week in a row).
**CONVERSION CRISIS DID NOT RESOLVE from the day77 quota-revert — it got WORSE. Made BIG changes this
week: price cut (A 33→27), massive ad-spend cuts, dev spend redirected to S1, AND a runway-driven
across-the-board fixed-cost cut. Read the sections below carefully before acting in week 13.**

## 🚨 TOP-LEVEL SITUATION (read this first)
1. **S1 individual conversion is in freefall and NOT recovering**: 42.5%(day63-69, pre-crisis) →
   10.5%(70-76, quota=200 crisis) → 3.4%(77-83, AFTER quota reverted to 1000!) → 1.4%(84-90, 1 day
   sample). S2 similar pattern (48.8%→11.4%→5.6%→4.6%). S3 partially recovering (68.9%→12.0%→15.7%→0%,
   noisy/small-n). **The quota revert + apology post did NOT fix new-lead conversion**, even though it
   DID fix existing-customer churn (cancellations back down to ~1.9%/week from the 6.3% crisis spike) and
   DID get positive social sentiment (post 7 scored +0.65 across all groups). This is a critical
   dissociation: reputation/sentiment toward EXISTING customers healed, but NEW LEAD conversion kept
   collapsing. Two candidate root causes identified this week (see #2, #3) — likely BOTH matter.
2. **NEW DISCOVERY — hidden macro recession**: `get_market_overview()`'s macroeconomic field is a
   **STALE, ~30-day-delayed READ** (shows PMI=49.0 "neutral/recovering" from a day31 measurement — the
   `macroeconomic_conditions` table only has 2 rows total, day1 and day31, because readings publish
   ~30 days after the day they're measured). **The REAL current PMI is much worse and only visible via
   flavor text in `get_social_posts`**: posts explicitly cite PMI=45.6 (day70) declining to PMI=44.5
   (day84) — solidly in "contraction" territory (42-48 band) — with recurring themes of budget
   freezes, ROI scrutiny, delayed renewals, "six-month payback" demands. **Do not trust
   get_market_overview's macro field as current — cross-check social posts for real-time PMI mentions.**
   This contraction is a plausible independent (or compounding) driver of the conversion collapse,
   especially for the price-sensitive S1 segment, and is OUTSIDE my control — may persist for months
   (business cycles aren't quick). Re-check social posts for PMI figures every week.
3. **NEW DISCOVERY — S1 quality neglect**: S1 has received ZERO targeted dev spend in 84 days (all
   targeted dev went to S2/S3 only). S1 delivered quality (0.3579) is the LOWEST of all 7 known groups
   despite being 80%+ of the subscriber base (3143/3914). Meanwhile 8+ competitor quality-boost
   announcements hit the social feed in just the last 2 weeks (RivalTech/CloudPeak/NexGen/ApexSaaS/
   QuantumEdge), each permanently raising customer expected quality per game mechanics. Hypothesis:
   competitor-driven expectation creep crossed above S1's stagnant quality bar, contributing to
   conversion collapse independent of the quota fiasco. ACTION TAKEN: started S1 targeted dev spend
   (see below) for the first time ever.
4. **NEW STRUCTURAL DISCOVERY — S3 is unprofitable on EVERY plan, always has been**: computed real
   per-customer weekly contribution margin (revenue − compute only, using actual day78-84 usage/ledger
   data, cross-validated to <1% error): **S1-A ≈ +$4.51/wk/customer (healthy). S2-A ≈ +$1.05/wk, S2-B ≈
   +$3.14/wk (healthy/breakeven). S3-A ≈ -$9.34/wk, S3-B ≈ -$17.55/wk, S3-C ≈ -$48.81/wk (ALL deeply
   NEGATIVE).** S3's true usage (~400-465 units/day) is 2-2.5x what ANY current plan's price/tier
   combo can cover profitably — this is a genuine product/pricing gap, not a bug, and has been true the
   entire game (just never quantified before). 307 of 389 S3 customers are on Plan A (worst-margin
   option for them). Breakeven price for a tier5(C) plan at S3's usage would need to be ~$370/mo (vs
   current $159→now $219) — likely above S3's actual willingness to pay. **Did NOT fully fix this week
   (too risky to overhaul mid-crisis with 3 other big levers already pulled) — bumped Plan C price
   159→219 (near-zero risk, only 2 customers use it) as a down payment. REVISIT in week 13-14: consider
   a genuine redesign (e.g., a cheaper-model-tier high-quota plan specifically for power users) or
   accept S3 as a deliberate loss-leader for its reputation-halo value (huge outgoing reputation
   influence on S1/E2/E1, see prior insight) and just cap/throttle new S3 acquisition instead.**
5. **RUNWAY CRISIS**: built a per-group cohort-billing cash-flow model calibrated to actual usage/
   compute/revenue data. At the PRIOR spend structure (~$42K/wk fixed: ads+dev+ops+capacity), model
   showed cash going deeply negative within 12-16 weeks REGARDLESS of conversion-recovery scenario
   (pessimistic/base/optimistic all converged to insolvency by ~week 15-19), because growth under the
   current tier/pricing structure keeps adding proportionally-unprofitable S2/S3 customers whose
   compute costs outpace revenue as fast as new profitable S1 customers help. **Executed an aggressive,
   across-the-board fixed-cost cut this week** (see Actions below) bringing fixed weekly spend from
   ~$42K → ~$23.4K/week. Revised model shows breakeven around week 12 (~day168) instead of deep
   insolvency, buying much more time regardless of which recovery scenario plays out — but even this
   revised model still trends negative by week 26 (~day266) as the base grows and S2/S3 mix drags
   margin down again. **This means further structural fixes (S3 pricing/tier redesign, R&D quality
   boosts enabling higher prices, or continued spend discipline) will be needed in the coming 1-3
   months — this is NOT a one-week fix, it's an ongoing strategic priority.**

## ACTIONS TAKEN DAY84 (week 12), full list:
1. `set_prices(A=27, B=69, C=219)` — Plan A cut 33→27 (S1 WTP estimate is only $25.87±65%, price had
   drifted up 74% from day0's $19 while S1 quality stagnated; ONLY affects new signups, existing book
   unaffected — low-risk lever). Plan C bumped 159→219 (barely used, 2 customers, near-zero-risk
   precursor to fixing its deeply negative margin). Plan B unchanged (mixed margin across S2/S3, didn't
   want a 4th simultaneous variable on the more heavily-populated plan).
2. Ad spend SLASHED and reallocated: S1 1700/day→160/day (content_marketing 700→80, referral_program
   900→80, social_media 100→0). S2 420/day→170/day (content 300→100, referral 60→40, social 60→30). S3
   360/day→230/day (referral 320→200, social 40→30, kept relatively more intact — still converting
   ~15%, reasonable CAC, and reputation-halo value). Rationale: at the CRASHED conversion rates
   (3-5% S1/S2), CAC was $150-235/customer against thin ARPU — bad economics; not worth maintaining old
   spend levels while conversion is broken. Total ads/week: $17,360 → $3,920.
3. Dev spend REDIRECTED + cut: added S1 targeted dev spend for the FIRST TIME EVER (700/day) — this is
   the single highest-conviction structural fix (closes the neglected quality gap for 80% of the base).
   Cut S2 targeted 750→300, S3 targeted 700→300 (given their negative unit economics, further quality
   investment there is lower-priority, though not zeroed — S3 retains some due to reputation-halo
   value). Cut global dev 800→200 (global mostly helps dead enterprise groups; targeted is 5x more
   efficient per $ for whichever group gets it). Total dev/week: $15,750 → $10,500.
4. Ops held at $750/day (didn't cut — protecting operational stability/issue-resolution speed during
   this fragile reputation-recovery period; issues ARE resolving fast, ~0.02-0.7 days avg, don't want to
   risk a new outage/slow-resolution shock on top of everything else).
5. Capacity held at Tier 2 (usage peaked 525-556K/day this week = 65-70% of 800K cap, headroom remains
   but MONITOR — if usage keeps climbing, Tier 3 ($1330/day, 2.5M cap) may be needed; don't preemptively
   upgrade during a cash crisis unless overload actually materializes).
6. ads_strength stays at 0.0 (disabled day77, NOT re-enabled — conversion crisis unresolved, keep the
   quality penalty off; revisit once conversion shows real recovery).
7. Posted social media (agent_post_id=8, replying to post 158's budget-pressure theme): announced the
   price cut concretely ("$33→$27... cutting our price, not our quality"). Concrete/specific, directly
   responsive to the dominant current social theme (macro budget scrutiny) — matches the pattern that's
   scored well before (concrete numbers > vague promises).
8. Did NOT do R&D (cash too tight, T1 alone is $166,667 — can't risk it at $176,588 cash). Did NOT do
   market research ($25K/attempt, can't justify during cash crisis). Enterprise still 100% dead (0
   threads in 84 days) — cheap to keep checking, not worth active investment.
NET EFFECT: fixed weekly spend (ads+dev+ops+capacity) cut from ~$42,070 (pre-crisis baseline) /
~$34,720 (mid-session, before the runway-driven second round of cuts) down to **$23,380/week**.

## WHAT TO CHECK FIRST THING IN WEEK 13 (day91 dashboard + queries):
- Conversion rates by group (day85-91 leads): did the price cut move the needle for S1/S2 at all? If
  S1 conversion is STILL <10% despite an 18% price cut, that's strong evidence price/quality isn't the
  binding constraint right now — look harder at reputation-stock recovery speed and macro (check social
  posts for new PMI figures — is it still 44.5, better, or worse?).
- Cancellation rate: should stay near the ~1.9%/week level (not spike back up) — confirms existing-
  customer sentiment stayed healthy after this week's changes (price cuts don't affect existing
  customers so shouldn't move this metric much either way).
- Recompute cash burn rate with actual week13 ledger data — does it match the ~$23,380/week fixed-cost
  model, or are there surprises (e.g., compute cost trending differently than expected)?
- Check `agent_social_media_posts` effect_by_group for post 8 (price cut announcement) reception.
- Re-run the group-level contribution-margin analysis (see script `week12_usage_check.py` as a
  template) with fresh usage data — did S1/S2/S3 usage patterns shift at all?
- If conversion is STILL near-zero for S1/S2 after this week's price cut, consider: (a) reputation is a
  slow-healing stock that just needs more TIME regardless of what I fix, so be patient another 1-2
  weeks before concluding price/quality didn't work; (b) a bigger, more concrete quality proof-point
  (wait for S1 dev-spend group bonus to actually show up, or complete R&D once affordable) might be
  needed rather than more price cuts; (c) macro contraction may simply be suppressing the whole market
  and no amount of my own action fixes that — focus on retention + patience over growth spend until PMI
  improves.
- Reconsider whether to cut ad spend EVEN FURTHER (toward near-zero) if conversion still hasn't budged,
  since spend on a fundamentally-broken funnel is pure waste — vs. holding current reduced levels to
  keep some signal/pipeline alive for when things recover.
- Revisit the S3 structural-unprofitability finding: is it worth designing a new plan tier (e.g. cheap
  model tier + high quota, no fancy quality multiplier) specifically to make power-user economics work?
  Or deliberately cap S3 acquisition and treat existing S3 base as a reputation investment?

## KEY LESSON FROM THIS WEEK'S MISTAKE-CHAIN:
Week 11 (day77) I assumed "revert the quota mistake → conversion recovers." It didn't — conversion kept
falling for another full week. **Single mechanical fixes to a multi-causal reputation/conversion crisis
can fail even when the "obvious" root cause is addressed — there can be multiple compounding causes
(here: quota fiasco reputation damage + hidden macro recession + long-neglected S1 quality gap, all
hitting at once), and reputation/sentiment stocks may take MULTIPLE weeks to fully heal even after the
mechanical trigger is fixed.** Don't assume a single-week fix will show up as a single-week recovery —
budget 2-4 weeks minimum to see if a corrective action is working before concluding it failed or
piling on more changes. But ALSO don't be complacent: I made a SECOND round of even-bigger changes this
week (price + ads + dev + fixed-cost overhaul all at once) rather than just waiting — given the runway
math showed genuine insolvency risk, decisive action beat cautious patience here. Balance: fix
obviously-broken economics fast (ad spend into a crashed funnel = pure waste, cut it), but give
reputation-mediated effects (quality, sentiment) more time to show results before judging them.

## Game basics
- 504 sim days = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Each `next-week` = 7 sim days, needs rationale +
  12 forecast numbers (point/lower/upper for +7d/+28d/+84d/+182d). lower<=point<=upper or 400 error.
- Conversation resets every week — THIS FILE is the only memory. Update before every next-week call.
- `./novamind-operation python <script.py>` to run novamind_api calls. `nm.query("SELECT ...")` for
  read-only SQL (max 5000 rows; single-quote the SQL, double-quote string literals inside it; add LIMIT
  or GROUP BY to avoid truncation warnings on raw per-row queries).
- **Only ONE bash tool call is processed per turn even if multiple are issued** — batch logic into a
  single script/command per turn instead of relying on parallel tool calls.
- `predictions` table stores all past forecast submissions (columns: submit_day, horizon_days, metric,
  predicted_value, predicted_lower, predicted_upper, submitted_at) — query each week to check
  calibration. Day77's 7-day forecast (pt 190K [158K-222K]) technically held (actual 176,588, inside
  the CI but 7% below point) — 10 of 11 weekly forecasts have now been in-range; keep checking weekly.
- `agent_social_media_posts` table has `effect_by_group` and `reasoning_by_group` JSON columns — READ
  THESE after posting to see exactly how each group reacted and why.
- `ad_channel_leads` table (channel_id, group_id, day, leads_generated, spend) is GOLD for verifying
  which channels actually work — query it fresh every week before deciding ad allocation.
- `notifications` table surfaces social-post performance summaries — check weekly.
- **`macroeconomic_conditions` table / `get_market_overview()`'s macro field is DELAYED ~30 days and
  currently only has 2 rows (day1, day31) — DO NOT treat it as current. Cross-check `get_social_posts`
  for real-time PMI mentions in flavor text (posts openly cite specific PMI values, e.g. "PMI at 44.5")
  — this is the only way to see TRUE current macro conditions before the official delayed report.**

## TIMING MECHANICS (confirmed 12 weeks running)
- Dashboard at day N reflects the week JUST CLOSED (days N-6..N), processed under config set at day N-7's
  turn. Config changes made at day-N turn apply cleanly to the ENTIRE next week (N+1..N+7).

  `billing_day_mod30` cycle.** (Verified via ledger: customer created day78 had a subscription_payment

  locked in at signup) — raising OR cutting quota affects existing customers' usage ceiling immediately.

  recent satisfaction/reputation shocks, not a fixed constant.
- You CAN issue multiple/contradictory config calls in the SAME session before `next-week` — only the

print("Day:", DAY, "Cash now:", CASH_NOW)

def get_cohorts(group):
    r = nm.query(f"""
        SELECT s.start_day, s.listed_price, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n
        FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
        WHERE c.group_id='{group}' AND s.status='subscribed'
        GROUP BY s.start_day, s.listed_price, s.plan ORDER BY s.start_day
    """)
    return [(row['start_day'], row['listed_price'], row['plan'], row['n']) for row in r['rows']]

TIER_COMPUTE = {'A': 0.006, 'B': 0.012, 'C': 0.03}
USAGE_AVG = {
    ('S1','A'): 76.8, ('S1','B'): 86.8,
    ('S2','A'): 161.5, ('S2','B'): 154.3,
    ('S3','A'): 411.3, ('S3','B'): 400.6, ('S3','C'): 409.1,
}
def usage_of(g, plan):
    return USAGE_AVG.get((g,plan), USAGE_AVG.get((g,'A'), 100))

cohorts_by_group = {g: get_cohorts(g) for g in ['S1','S2','S3']}

FIXED_WEEKLY = 23380.0   # REVISED (more aggressive cuts this session)
NEW_PLAN_MIX = {
    'S1': [('A', 27.0, 1.0)],
    'S2': [('A', 33.0, 0.9), ('B', 69.0, 0.1)],
    'S3': [('A', 34.0, 0.75), ('B', 69.0, 0.20), ('C', 219.0, 0.05)],
}
LEAD_PROMO_S1 = 5.0

def project(weeks, leads_wk1_by_group, lead_growth_by_group, conv_recovery_curve, base_conv_by_group, churn_curve):
    sim = {g: [[sd,p,pl,n] for sd,p,pl,n in cohorts_by_group[g]] for g in ['S1','S2','S3']}
    cash = CASH_NOW
    day = DAY
    trace = []
    for wk in range(1, weeks+1):
        week_revenue = 0.0
        week_compute = 0.0
        churn_rate = churn_curve[min(wk-1,len(churn_curve)-1)]
        total_active = 0
        leads_total = 0
        for g in ['S1','S2','S3']:
            for c in sim[g]:
                sd,p,pl,n = c
                if n <= 0: continue
                for d in range(day+1, day+8):
                    if sd < d and (d-sd) % 30 == 0:
                        survivors = n*(1-churn_rate)
                        week_revenue += survivors*p
                        c[3] = survivors
                week_compute += c[3]*usage_of(g,pl)*7*TIER_COMPUTE.get(pl,0.006)
            leads = leads_wk1_by_group[g]*(lead_growth_by_group[g]**(wk-1))
            leads_total += leads
            recov = conv_recovery_curve[min(wk-1,len(conv_recovery_curve)-1)]
            conv = base_conv_by_group[g]*recov
            new_subs = leads*conv
            promo = LEAD_PROMO_S1 if g=='S1' else 0.0
            for plan, price, frac in NEW_PLAN_MIX[g]:
                n_this = new_subs*frac
                week_revenue += n_this*(price-promo)
                week_compute += n_this*usage_of(g,plan)*7*TIER_COMPUTE[plan]
                sim[g].append([day+7, price, plan, n_this])
            total_active += sum(c[3] for c in sim[g])
        cost = FIXED_WEEKLY + week_compute + leads_total*0.5
        net = week_revenue - cost
        cash += net
        trace.append((day+7, round(total_active), round(week_revenue), round(week_compute), round(cost), round(net), round(cash)))

## 🚨 TOP-LEVEL SITUATION (read this first)
1. **NEW KEY INSIGHT — S1 price was likely AT/ABOVE willingness-to-pay, capping conversion via a hard
   budget gate, independent of quality/reputation.** `get_group_insights('S1')` shows willingness_to_pay
   ≈ $25.87 (±65% noise). We were charging $27 (i.e., AT/above the mean WTP estimate) even after last

   they can pay, separate from the quality-price curve gate), pricing at/above the mean WTP estimate
   likely excludes over half the segment on affordability alone, regardless of quality or reputation
   healing. **ACTION: cut Plan A 27→19 this week** (global — Plan A is shared across all groups, cost is
   near-zero since `listed_price` is LOCKED IN at signup and never retroactively changes for the 3893
   existing customers; only affects future new signups). Verified margin stays positive even at $19

   +$1.17/wk/customer). This is THE key experiment to watch next week — if S1 conversion (2.5% this
   week, up from 1.4%) jumps meaningfully (>10%), the WTP-gate hypothesis is confirmed and further
   price/volume strategy should follow; if it stays flat, the constraint is elsewhere (macro/reputation)
   and I should stop cutting price further.

  turn. Config changes made at day-N turn apply cleanly to the ENTIRE next week (N+1..N+7).

  — always resend the complete desired allocation; omitted keys silently become $0. Not calling a
  function at all leaves previous state untouched.
- `listed_price` is LOCKED IN at signup, never retroactively changes — renewals bill at the ORIGINAL
  signup price forever. Price hikes/cuts ONLY affect new-signup revenue, never existing book. This makes
  `set_prices` changes essentially FREE OPTIONALITY to test — zero downside risk to existing revenue.
- `set_promotion(by_group_plan=...)` is an ONGOING discount that DOES apply to existing subscribers at
  their next billing cycle (unlike listed_price) — "Customers evaluate plans at (list_price - promotion)
  on billing day." CAUTION: this applies uniformly to a (group,plan) bucket regardless of each
  customer's own historical listed_price, so sizing a promotion to offset a NEW higher sticker price
  risks deeply discounting (even flooring to $0) existing customers who signed up at a much LOWER
  historical price. Not a clean tool for "raise sticker + subsidize one group back down" — the noise/
  variance in historical signup prices makes this dangerous. `set_lead_promotion` only discounts the
  FIRST billing period for brand-new leads (reverts to full price at 30-day renewal) — useful for
  temporary tests but carries bait-and-switch churn risk at renewal if the reverted price doesn't clear
  the customer's bar.

  30 days thereafter on the `billing_day_mod30` cycle.

  locked in at signup). Treat quota changes as customer-experience-critical (week11 quota-cut incident
  caused a severe multi-week reputation/conversion crisis) — avoid touching quotas unless usage data

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 98 (Week 14 actions EXECUTED). Cash $163,930 pre-action (net -156 wk13→wk14,
essentially flat). Forecast submitted, next-week called → advancing to day105/Week 15.

## 🚨 TOP-LEVEL SITUATION (read this first)

### THE BIG MOVE THIS WEEK: cut model tier A 3→2, B 4→3 (C stays 5, no individuals use it)
**Critical discovery: this week's near-breakeven (-$156) was a BILLING-CYCLE ILLUSION, not real
equilibrium.** Built exact bday-bucket (start_day%30) model of active subs → confirmed customers bill in
lumpy weekly waves (this week's bday-bucket=1337 payments; NEXT week's bucket=only 702 — a ~48% revenue
swing on billing timing alone, nothing to do with business health). **The TRUE smoothed weekly economics
(monthly_revenue/30×7, i.e. active_base × avg_price, averaged over a full 30-day cycle) = ~$29,800/wk
revenue vs ~$43-47K/wk costs at old tiers = REAL underlying burn of ~$13-17K/week**, not the ~$0 the
single lucky week suggested. This forced a much bigger structural fix than incremental tweaking.
- **Compute cost is ~half of total costs and is a DIRECT function of model tier** (0.002/0.006/0.03 per
  unit at T2/T3/T5 vs 0.006/0.012/0.03 at old T3/T4/T5). Cutting Plan A tier 3→2 and Plan B tier 4→3 saves
  **~$13,485/week in compute** (verified exact via per-group-plan usage×count calc, not just estimate) —
  more than half our total weekly cost base. This is the single biggest lever in the entire game so far.
- **Risk analysis that justified pulling the trigger despite quality-floor uncertainty:** `set_model_tiers`
  is GLOBAL PER-PLAN (not per-group) — cannot target S1 only. Checked population concentration: S1 (huge
  floor buffer, floor=0.081 vs new T2 quality 0.333, ~4x margin) and S3 (floor=0.145 vs 0.416, ~2.9x
  margin) are SAFE with large margin. **S2 is the risk: 354/394 (90%!) of S2 is on Plan A**, floor=0.37±65%
  (range 0.13-0.61), new T2 quality=0.4427 → roughly ~35% chance (if floor uniform in range) the new
  quality is BELOW S2's true floor. BUT: even in the total-catastrophe case (100% of S2 churns), S2's
  entire revenue is only ~$2,717/wk — dwarfed by the ~$10,068/wk in S1+S3 savings alone (which are
  virtually risk-free). **Downside is bounded and net-positive even in the worst case; upside if safe
  (~65% likely) is the full $13,485/wk.** This asymmetry is why the trade was taken. Mitigants: (a) bumped
  S2 targeted dev spend 300→500/day to build extra quality buffer over time, (b) Plan B also moved to T3
  which delivers the SAME quality S2-A had before (0.5313) at a higher price ($69) — if S2-A customers
  no longer clear their bar, Plan B is a natural, affordable (WTP=$178) upgrade path, likely reducing
  actual cancellations vs a hard cutoff.

  people) this week, REVERT to `set_model_tiers(A=3,B=4,C=5)` immediately** — conversion is the fastest
  read (shows up same week) since churn effects lag to 30-day billing marks. If S2 looks fine (conversion

### Other actions taken day98 (week14):
1. `set_model_tiers(A=2, B=3, C=5)` — see above.
2. `set_targeted_dev_spend(S1=850, S2=500[was 300], S3=150)` — S2 bump is tier-cut risk mitigant.

   Added to address a specific S1 customer social-media complaint (5+ day support wait) — global ops

   post pattern (direct reply + concrete number).
6. Prices held (A=19, B=69, C=219) — unchanged, only 1 week of post-cut data so far, want more signal

   already in flight; preserve buffer to react if S2 reverts needed.

## KEY NEW INSIGHT — organic/network leads are the REAL profitable growth engine, not paid ads
Checked `customers.acquisition_source` for this week's leads: **S1 got 362/569 leads (64%!) from
'network' source (self-referral from the 3083-strong existing base) at essentially zero cost (~$0.5
lead-acq fee only)**, converting at ~5.25% — CAC ≈ $9.5/customer vs LTV ≈ $81-88. Hugely profitable.
Meanwhile PAID channels (content_marketing, referral_program) cost $4.76-7.14/lead before the $0.5 fee,
giving CAC $115-149 — marginal-to-negative given current low conversion. **This means the core business
IS healthy/profitable at the unit level once you separate organic (great) from paid (currently weak)
growth — paid ads are a small, cuttable drag, not the main engine.** Re-test scaling paid ads back up
once conversion trend (see below) climbs further (would lower CAC proportionally).

## CONFIRMED MECHANICS & FORMULAS (validated empirically across 14 weeks — trust this over generic docs)
- 504 sim days = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Each `next-week` needs rationale + 12 forecast
  numbers (point/lower/upper for +7d/+28d/+84d/+182d). lower<=point<=upper or 400 error.
- **BILLING LUMPINESS IS REAL AND LARGE — always model it, never extrapolate a single week's revenue
  rate.** `subscriptions.start_day % 30` (= billing_day_mod30) determines which of 30 buckets each
  customer bills in; each customer pays exactly once per 30 days on their bucket day. Bucket sizes are
  VERY uneven (ranged 61-243 in current book) because historical signup volume was uneven (crisis weeks
  had few signups, recovery weeks more). To forecast ANY horizon correctly: (1) pull exact cohorts
  (start_day, listed_price, plan, count) per group, (2) simulate week-by-week which bday buckets fall in
  which future week, (3) for longer horizons (12wk/26wk) it's fine to use the SMOOTHED average
  (monthly_revenue = Σ active_customer_price, weekly ≈ ×7/30) since lumpiness averages out over multiple
  cycles. Scripts: `week14_forecast_v3.py` has the reusable `project()` function — copy/adapt each week
  rather than rebuilding from scratch. This approach nailed day84's 7d-forecast to within 0.7% error.
- `./novamind-operation python <script.py>` for novamind_api calls. `nm.query("SELECT ...")` for
  read-only SQL (max 5000 rows; single-quote SQL, double-quote string literals inside; use LIMIT/GROUP BY
  to avoid truncation). **Only ONE bash tool call processed per turn — batch logic into a single
  script/command, don't rely on parallel tool calls.**
- **`set_targeted_ops_spend` ACTUAL signature is `(targeted_spend: Dict[str,float])` only — passing
  `by_group=`/`by_plan=`/`by_group_plan=`/`by_customer=` as separate kwargs (as the API doc example
  shows) raises `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument`. The doc is WRONG/aspirational here; always use
  `targeted_spend={group_id: $/day}` (treated as by-group targeting).** This is a NEW correction this
  week — previously ops was only ever set via global `set_daily_spend`.
- `set_targeted_ad_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend`/`set_targeted_ops_spend` FULLY REPLACE state each call
  — always resend the complete desired allocation; omitted keys silently become $0.
- `listed_price` LOCKED IN at signup forever (renewals bill original signup price). `set_prices` changes
  ONLY affect NEW signups — zero downside risk to existing revenue, free to experiment with.
- Model tier (1-5, compute-rate/quality multiplier) and usage quota are BOTH LIVE for ALL existing
  customers immediately (not signup-locked, unlike price) — changing them affects the whole current base
  on that plan letter instantly. Model tier is set PER-PLAN-LETTER globally (A/B/C), same tier applies to
  every group using that plan — no per-group override exists for tier (unlike dev/ops/ads spend which DO
  support per-group targeting). Quota changes are proven dangerous (week11 crisis) — avoid unless usage
  data shows the quota is actually binding.
- Tier multipliers/compute cost (from `get_cost_info()`): T1=.60×/$0.0003, T2=.75×/$0.002, T3=.90×/$0.006,
  T4=1.00×/$0.012, T5=1.10×/$0.03 per usage unit. Capacity tiers (infra, SEPARATE lever, just outage
  insurance, doesn't touch quality): T0=50K/day $85 ... T2=800K/day $530 (currently here, usage running
  300-570K/day, still headroom) ... T7=300M/day $75K.
- delivered_quality = (base_product_quality[0.20] + q_shared_bonus[global, from global dev spend] +
  q_group_bonus[per-group cumulative, from targeted dev spend]) × tier_multiplier[per PLAN letter].
  q_group_bonus is the SAME across all plans within a group (only tier_multiplier differs by plan) —
  confirmed this week: this is why moving S2 from Plan A(new T2) to Plan B(new T3) exactly restores their
  OLD Plan-A-at-T3 quality level (0.5903×0.90=0.5313 either way), a clean natural upgrade path.
- Dev quality growth: empirically, targeted per-group rate ≈ **0.0225** × ln(1+targeted_spend/5000)/day
  (NOT the 0.030 "5×" coefficient stated in docs/api/marketing.json — actual observed S1 bonus growth
  +0.0248/week at 850/day spend matches 0.0225 almost exactly, matches 0.030 poorly). Both bonuses are
  cumulative/permanent stocks that never decay even if spend stops. As of day98 (pre-this-week's-changes):
  global_bonus=0.1988, S1_bonus=+0.0454, S2_bonus=+0.1915, S3_bonus=+0.1563.
- `get_group_insights(group_id)` (all still Info Level 1, ±65% noise, day98 readings): S1 WTP=$25.87,
  usage=91.1/day(measured actual ~76.5), qfloor=0.081, mkt_cap=272,812. S2 WTP=$178.59, usage=231.5/day

  qfloor=0.668. **All enterprise qfloors exceed max deliverable quality (~0.44 even at old T5) — enterprise
  is structurally blocked, confirmed over 98 days with 0 enterprise_turns rows ever.** Don't invest until
  quality raised substantially via R&D (need ~1-2 mid-tier R&D projects, ~+0.2-0.3 boost) AND cash healthy.

  quality-floor uncertainty, but costs more than we want to spend while mid-tier-change-bet; revisit if
  cash cushion grows AND the tier change looks safe (no need if it's already working).
- R&D: 20 tiers. Costs: T1 $166,667, T2 $333,333, T3 $500K, T4 $666,667, T5 $833,333, T6 $1M, T7 $1.17M,
  T8 $1.33M, T9 $1.5M, T10 $1.67M, T11 $2.5M, T12 $3.67M, T13 $5M. Mean days: T1=12,T2=17,T3=23,T4=32,
  T5=42... Mean quality boost: T1=.04,T2=.07,T3=.11,...T10=.85 (high variance ~40-50% CV on both). T1 done

  subscriptions (JOIN customers). No `status` column on customers at all. `customers.customer_type`:

Reconciled ledger exactly this week: day105 session set ads={} and ops={S1:150,S3:100}(+750 global).

(exactly 1 day at old $900/day + 6 days at new $1000/day). **Conclusion: a setting changed during a
session shown on day D takes effect starting day D+1, and stays live through day D+7 (i.e. the entirety
of the week that produces the NEXT dashboard, minus that first locked-in day).** So changes I make TODAY
(day112) will apply days113-118, with day112 itself still reflecting whatever was live at the end of the
day105 session. Practically: treat changes as "almost fully live within the week you make them" — no
need to wait an extra week to see clean effects. Old memory said "next week" meaning a full week lag;
that overstated the delay by ~6 days. R&D and market research spending, by contrast, still charge/act
IMMEDIATELY at call time (unchanged/confirmed).

($29-36/mo, the majority of the base) hardest at their 30-day re-eval. This week's precise test
(due-this-week-at-billing-checkpoint vs cancelled, by price tier, S1 group): **$19→4/84=4.8%,
$29→11/291=3.8%, $33→11/235=4.7%.** All three price tiers fail their checkpoint at essentially the SAME
~4-5% rate. **This disproves the "high legacy price = high risk" hypothesis — it's a roughly uniform
background churn rate across S1 regardless of price paid**, most likely a fixed tail of
quality-sensitive individuals within the S1 persona mix whose expectations (drifting upward from time +
competitor events) finally exceed delivered quality (0.3718 for Plan A) at whatever price they're on.

bucket-verified). **Reusable technique for future weeks:** compute exact due-vs-cancelled by

conflate pool size differences and give misleading tier comparisons).

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)
# days that just elapsed: 112 (last dashboard day) +1 .. 119 -> actually week is day112->119, 7 days: 113-119
days = list(range(113,120))
buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
print("days elapsed this week:", days)
print("billing_day_mod30 buckets due this week:", buckets)

buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)

print("\n=== DUE THIS WEEK (bday in buckets, started before this week, still had a chance to bill) BY GROUP: subscribed vs cancelled ===")
q = f"""
SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
  AND s.start_day <= 112
  AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.status
ORDER BY c.group_id, s.status
"""
r = nm.query(q)
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n=== Same but only those that were ACTIVE at start of week (i.e. not already cancelled before day112) ===")
q2 = f"""
SELECT c.group_id,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 112 AND 119 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_this_wk,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as still_subscribed,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day < 112) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_before,
       COUNT(*) as total
FROM subscriptions s
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
  AND s.start_day <= 112
  AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
GROUP BY c.group_id
"""
r2 = nm.query(q2)
for row in r2['rows']:
    print(row)
EOF

buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)

SELECT s.listed_price,

       SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as still_subscribed,

JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE c.group_id='S1'

  AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')

GROUP BY s.listed_price
ORDER BY s.listed_price
"""

random.seed(42)

with open('week17_cohorts.json') as f:
    cohorts = json.load(f)

CURRENT_DAY = 119
CASH_NOW = 134712.0

# promotions now active (by group)
PROMO = {"S1": 12.0, "S2": 15.0, "S3": 15.0}

# usage per customer per day (from day118 actuals), by plan
USAGE_PER_CUST = {"A": 69.26, "B": 198.11, "C": 300.0}  # C guess, no data
TIER_MULT_COST = {2: 0.002, 3: 0.006, 4: 0.012, 5: 0.03}
PLAN_TIER = {"A": 2, "B": 4, "C": 5}  # current live config

NEW_PLAN_PRICE = {"A": 14.0, "B": 49.0, "C": 150.0}

FIXED_DAILY = {
    "capacity": 530.0,
    "ops": 850.0,
    "dev": 1700.0,
}
LEAD_COST = 0.5

def simulate(days_horizon, fail_rate_fn, new_signups_per_day_fn, label=""):
    """
    fail_rate_fn(group, week_idx) -> probability a due customer cancels at checkpoint
    new_signups_per_day_fn(day_idx) -> number of new Plan-A signups per day (all new leads assumed plan A at new price)
    """
    # state: list of dicts {group, plan, price, bday, is_new(bool)}
    state = []
    for c in cohorts:
        state.append({
            "group": c["group_id"], "plan": c["plan"], "price": c["listed_price"],
            "bday": c["billing_day_mod30"], "n": c["n"]
        })
    cash = CASH_NOW
    history = {}
    for day_offset in range(1, days_horizon+1):
        day = CURRENT_DAY + day_offset
        week_idx = day_offset // 7
        bucket = day % 30
        revenue = 0.0
        # process billing for groups whose bday matches
        new_state = []
        for row in state:
            if row["bday"] == bucket:
                fr = fail_rate_fn(row["group"], week_idx)
                survivors = row["n"] * (1 - fr)
                eff_price = max(0.0, row["price"] - PROMO.get(row["group"], 0.0))
                revenue += survivors * eff_price
                if survivors > 0.5:
                    new_row = dict(row); new_row["n"] = survivors
                    new_state.append(new_row)
            else:
                new_state.append(row)
        state = new_state
        # new signups (assume plan A, new price, spread across bday buckets = today's bucket)
        n_new = new_signups_per_day_fn(day_offset)
        if n_new > 0:
            state.append({"group": "NEW", "plan": "A", "price": NEW_PLAN_PRICE["A"], "bday": bucket, "n": n_new})
            revenue += 0  # first billing happens next cycle (30 days later) -- conservatively no immediate revenue
        # total active subs & usage-based compute cost
        total_by_plan = {"A": 0.0, "B": 0.0, "C": 0.0}
        for row in state:
            total_by_plan[row["plan"]] += row["n"]
        compute_cost = sum(total_by_plan[p] * USAGE_PER_CUST[p] * TIER_MULT_COST[PLAN_TIER[p]] for p in ["A","B","C"])
        # leads arrive regardless of conversion; assume ~424/week flat (60/day) organic leads generate lead cost
        leads_today = 424.0/7.0
        lead_cost = leads_today * LEAD_COST
        total_cost = FIXED_DAILY["capacity"] + FIXED_DAILY["ops"] + FIXED_DAILY["dev"] + compute_cost + lead_cost
        cash += revenue - total_cost
        if day in (CURRENT_DAY+7, CURRENT_DAY+28, CURRENT_DAY+84, CURRENT_DAY+182):
            history[day] = {"cash": cash, "subs": sum(r["n"] for r in state), "rev_today": revenue, "cost_today": total_cost}
    return cash, history, state

# ---------------- SCENARIOS ----------------
# Base case: promotion+targeted tier bump brings fail rates down from this week's observed
# (S1~34%, S2~36%, S3~75%) to a moderate elevated-but-improved level, slowly recovering as
# dev spend & tenure accumulate; assume no further mega-shocks (but normal small ones continue, roughly priced in)
def base_fail(group, week_idx):
    start = {"S1": 0.20, "S2": 0.20, "S3": 0.45}[group]
    floor = {"S1": 0.06, "S2": 0.05, "S3": 0.12}[group]
    # improve toward floor over ~20 weeks
    rate = max(floor, start - 0.007*week_idx)
    return rate

def base_signups(day_idx):
    return 424.0/7.0 * 0.10  # 10% conversion resumes

def opt_fail(group, week_idx):
    start = {"S1": 0.14, "S2": 0.14, "S3": 0.30}[group]
    floor = {"S1": 0.04, "S2": 0.03, "S3": 0.06}[group]
    rate = max(floor, start - 0.012*week_idx)
    return rate

def opt_signups(day_idx):
    return 424.0/7.0 * 0.25

def pess_fail(group, week_idx):
    start = {"S1": 0.32, "S2": 0.34, "S3": 0.65}[group]
    floor = {"S1": 0.18, "S2": 0.18, "S3": 0.40}[group]
    # slow improvement, or even worsening near-term if more shocks hit (add slight noise-like bump mid-horizon)
    rate = max(floor, start - 0.003*week_idx)
    return rate

def pess_signups(day_idx):
    return 424.0/7.0 * 0.01

for label, fr, ns in [("BASE", base_fail, base_signups), ("OPT", opt_fail, opt_signups), ("PESS", pess_fail, pess_signups)]:
    cash_final, hist, state = simulate(182, fr, ns, label)
    print(f"\n=== {label} ===")
    for day, d in sorted(hist.items()):
        print(f"day{day} (+{day-CURRENT_DAY}d): cash=${d['cash']:,.0f} subs={d['subs']:,.0f} rev_today=${d['rev_today']:,.0f} cost_today=${d['cost_today']:,.0f}")

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 119 (Week 17 actions EXECUTED). Cash $134,712 → advancing to day126/Week 18.

## 🚨🚨 TOP-LEVEL SITUATION: WE HIT A MAJOR COMPETITOR-SHOCK CRISIS THIS WEEK — read this first

### What happened (day112→119)
Cash fell $145,171→$134,712 (-$10,459). Dashboard showed **0 new individual subscribers from 424 new
leads** (0% conversion) and **338 cancellations** (way above the usual ~150-170/week baseline). Dug in
and found:
1. **New-lead conversion has been ~0% since day108** (11 days before I caught it — see "process fix"
   below). Every single `subscriptions` row created day108-119 has status='lost'. This is NOT new this
   week, it's been silently broken/worsening for a while.
2. **Checkpoint (30-day billing re-eval) failure rate EXPLODED this week.** Measured exact due-cohort
   pass/fail (bday-bucket method): **S1 34.0% fail (was ~4-5%), S2 36.5% (was ~1.9%), S3 75.0% (was
   ~2-4%)**. This is a massive, sudden multi-week-scale increase, not noise.
3. **Root cause found in social feed**: FOUR huge competitor quality-boost events hit in 2 days —
   day114 two events @ **+0.1853** each, day115 two events @ **+0.2503** each (posts 233-236, all tagged
   group **S1**). Compare to the prior ~10 days' events which were only +0.015-0.02 each. This dwarfs
   anything seen in the game so far and permanently raised customer quality expectations (per game
   mechanics, competitor-driven expectation shifts are irreversible except via dev spend/R&D).
   Reaction posts are literally captioned "the bar just got reset" / "NovaMind... need to move fast."
4. Fail rate DOES still vary with price (confirms quality-price curve still working, just the bar
   shifted up): S1 $22→14.6% fail vs $33→41.1%, $36→30.9% (n=82/236/320). S3 failed almost uniformly
   regardless of price (68-100% at every price point) — S3 ("power users") appear far more
   quality-driven/less price-elastic than S1/S2, so price levers help S1/S2 much more than S3.
   Likely also a **tenure-loyalty confound**: brand-new leads have zero tenure bonus (existing docs:
   up to +0.13 Q_perceived at 12mo, ln(1+months) growth) so they face a strictly higher effective bar
   than similarly-priced existing customers — explains why 100%-of-leads-fail even at prices where
   *existing* customers at similar prices only fail 15-40%.

### Response executed this week (day119 session, live ~day120 per 1-day config lag)
1. **`set_promotion(by_group={"S1":12, "S2":15, "S3":15})`** — NEW LEVER, first use this game.
   Recurring $/mo discount for EXISTING subscribers, applied at (list_price − promotion) on their NEXT
   30-day billing eval — i.e. it lands exactly at the checkpoint moment that's failing them. This is
   the single highest-leverage tool for the crisis: directly lowers the quality bar per the
   quality-price curve for the entire existing base, timed perfectly. (Confirmed: **`set_promotion` DOES
   get logged in `config_overrides`** — correction to old memory, which said it wasn't logged; that was
   just because it had never been called before.)
2. **`set_model_tiers(A=2, B=4, C=5)`** — bumped ONLY Plan B (2→4 skipped, stayed at 2 for A to protect
   margin — see margin note below). B has only 116 customers so absolute compute-cost delta is small,
   and disproportionately serves S2/S3 (71 of 116 B customers are S3) — the group hit hardest and least
   price-responsive, so a direct quality lever matters most there.
3. **`set_prices(A=14, B=79, C=150)`** for NEW signups only (existing listed_price is locked forever,
   zero risk to current revenue). Cut A from $19 (-26%) and C from $219 (-31%) to try to reopen the
   completely-dead top-of-funnel. **Left B at $79 (actually RAISED from $69)** — see margin correction.
4. **⚠️ MARGIN NEAR-MISS, CAUGHT AND FIXED THIS SESSION**: initially set B price to $49 to match the
   "cut prices to help conversion" theme, but then checked actual Plan-B usage data:
   mean=198.11 units/day, median=153, p90=446 (quota is 1200, so heavy users have lots of headroom).
   At NEW tier 4 ($0.012/unit), mean-usage compute cost = **$71.32/month — which EXCEEDS a $49 price!**
   Even the OLD tier 3 ($0.006/unit) was already thin/negative for the top usage quartile (p75=272u/day
   → $48.96/mo compute vs $69 price). **Fixed by raising new-signup B price to $79** instead of cutting
   it — existing $69 customers are unaffected by `set_prices` and get the tier-4 quality bump for FREE
   (pure retention upside), while new signups now have positive (if thin) margin.
   **LESSON: before combining a tier bump with a price cut on the same plan, always pull actual
   mean/median/p90 daily-usage data for that plan and check `usage × new_tier_cost_per_unit × 30` against
   the proposed new price. Tier changes can 2-10x compute cost per unit — easy to accidentally price
   below cost.** (Reference: tier cost/unit = T1 $0.0003, T2 $0.002, T3 $0.006, T4 $0.012, T5 $0.03.)
5. **`set_ads_strength(global_strength=0.0)`** — reverted the day112 in-app-ads test. Confirmed
   calibration: ad_revenue was ~$87-96/day (~$630/week), decaying slowly as subscriber base shrank —
   real but small. Given the crisis, cut this speculative satisfaction-penalty risk; $630/week isn't
   worth any incremental churn risk while we're fighting a much bigger fire. Revisit only after
   stabilization.
6. **Social post (agent_post_id=13, day119)**, replying to post 236 (the dramatic +0.2503 competitor
   post, group S1): announced the model upgrade + price cuts, LEADING with the quality-investment framing
   ("stronger models... investing in quality AND passing savings"), not leading with the discount.
   **IMPORTANT LESSON from historical post data (agent_post_id=9, day91, effect_by_group)**: a
   pure price-cut announcement ($27→$19) scored **+0.75 for S1, +0.72 for S3, but −0.65 for S2** — S2
   ("quality-focused") explicitly reads aggressive discounting as "signals unsustainable unit
   economics/desperation." **Going forward: never lead a social post with a price cut alone; always
   frame price/discount news secondary to a quality/investment narrative, especially in
   S2-relevant contexts.** Effect of post 13 not yet known (check next week).

### Why NOT bigger/more aggressive this week
- R&D still unaffordable (cheapest tier, T1 repeat, costs $166,667; cash is $134,712). HOLD until cash
  cushion is much bigger — do not let crisis pressure tempt an unaffordable bet.
- Didn't bump Plan A's tier (would 3x compute cost on 96% of the base, ~$7,500/wk extra) — chose to lean
  on the (free-ish, revenue-side) promotion lever first since empirical data show price/promotion alone
  meaningfully cuts fail rate for S1/S2. Will reconsider A-tier bump next week if promotion alone isn't
  enough (watch the data).
- Didn't touch dev/ops spend — too many simultaneous changes would confound next week's read. Dev spend
  log-curve means a quick bump wouldn't materially help this week anyway.

## 📋 PROCESS FIX — ADD TO EVERY WEEK'S CHECKLIST GOING FORWARD
**This crisis was findable 11 days earlier if I'd checked it.** The dashboard shows "New Individual
Subscribers" directly — I must **always compare New Leads vs New Subscribers explicitly every week**
(conversion rate = New Subscribers / New Leads). If conversion rate is near 0%, treat it as a
same-day emergency investigation, don't wait for cancellations to also spike. Also: **always skim
`get_social_posts(days=14)` for competitor-quality-boost magnitudes every week** — a string of
+0.015-0.02 events is normal background noise; anything ≥0.10 is a mega-shock requiring immediate
pricing/promotion/tier response, not a wait-and-see approach.

## Cash trajectory log (update each week)
Day 0: $1,000,000 → Day 84: $176,588 → Day 91: $164,086 → Day 98: $163,930 → Day 105: $154,328 →
Day 112: $145,171 → **Day 119: $134,712** (-$10,459; this was the week the mega-shock's effects hit —
ledger confirms: development -$11,900, compute -$7,175, operations -$5,950, capacity -$3,710,
lead_acquisition -$225, ad_revenue +$645, subscription_payment +$17,856 = net -$10,459 exactly matching
cash delta). **Expect further declines over the next several weeks as the promotion ramps in (only ~7 of
30 bday-buckets renew per week, so full effect phases in over ~4 weeks) before (hopefully) stabilizing.**

## Forecast submitted day119 (for calibration check next week)
Built `week17_forecast_v2.py`: exact billing-cohort simulation (208 group/plan/price/bday buckets, all
3488 active subs) + 3 scenarios (BASE/OPT/PESS) varying post-intervention checkpoint-fail-rate

0-6 (days120-126), which are the FIRST cohorts to bill under the day119 promo (S1=$12,S2=$15,S3=$15)

wk8 27%, wk9 40%, wk10 10.5%, wk11 4.1%, **wk12 0%, wk13 0.3%, wk14 1.6%, wk15 1%, wk16 0%, wk17 0%,

AT ALL to a 26% list-price cut (A: $19→$14 on day119, still 100% lost at day126 with avg attempted

phase since day61 per `macroeconomic_conditions` table — table only has 4 rows total, day1/31/61/91,
updates ~every 30 days, last update day91, OVERDUE for a refresh — check `get_market_overview()` /
query the table again next week) and (b) brand-new leads get ZERO tenure-loyalty bonus (up to +0.13 at
12mo for existing customers), so they face the FULL, undiluted, ever-drifting-upward quality bar with
no cushion — while existing customers are cushioned by tenure + promotion. **Conclusion: do NOT cut
prices further chasing new-lead conversion — it's a quality-gap problem, not a price problem, and
further cuts just erode margin on the rare conversion that does occur.** Tested one cheap, free
experiment this week: bumped `lead_promotion` (new-leads-only, zero cost unless they convert) to

dead and I should stop testing it (it's free to leave at a modest level, but no more experiments needed).
**The only lever that could ever fix this is a big R&D quality jump** (R&D "provides quality jumps
impossible to achieve through dev spend alone"). Currently unaffordable (see below).

### 3. 🔑 CRITICAL NEW MECHANIC DISCOVERED: promotion "ramp-in" — revenue will keep falling for ~4 more weeks
`set_promotion` only updates a customer's `promotion` field AT THEIR NEXT 30-day billing checkpoint —
it does NOT retroactively apply to everyone immediately. Since only 7/30 billing buckets cycle per
week, a promotion CHANGE takes ~4-5 weeks to reach 100% of the base. Verified empirically today:
current active-base avg `promotion` for S1 is only $4.04 (vs the $12 setting that's been live since
day119) — i.e. only ~34% of S1 has the new promo so far. **Implication: blended revenue will keep
DECLINING for the next ~4 weeks purely from promo phase-in, even with zero further subscriber losses.**

CURRENT (partially-ramped) promo = $28,207, but once fully switched to the new promo = only $16,409

further over the next month — this is the known, already-priced-in mechanism, not a new crisis.**
**LESSON: whenever changing `set_promotion` going forward, remember the effect phases in over ~30 days
(≈4-5 weekly steps), not immediately — plan cash forecasts accordingly.**

revenue over 12 billing cycles (~360 days) = price × N0 × [1-(1-fail)^12]/fail. At 34% fail / $31.24

powerfully over many cycles. Don't second-guess the promotion decision on the basis of near-term ARPU
decline alone.

import novamind_api as nm

day = nm.vars.current_day
print("=== DAY", day, "===")

# 1. Checkpoint fail-rate methodology on newly due buckets (buckets for days127-133, i.e. last week)
# We want the NEXT set: buckets for days134-140 (already billed this past week were 127-133 -> now check freshness)
# Actually let's re-derive: buckets due in the week we just lived through (day127-133) to see fail rate that JUST happened
buckets_last_week = [d % 30 for d in range(127, 134)]
print("Buckets that were due day127-133:", buckets_last_week)

q = f"""
SELECT group_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status='cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as subscribed,
  COUNT(*) as total
FROM subscriptions
WHERE billing_day_mod30 IN ({','.join(map(str,buckets_last_week))})
  AND start_day <= 133
  AND group_id IN ('S1','S2','S3')
  AND status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
GROUP BY group_id
"""
r = nm.query(q)
print("\n-- Fail rate for buckets due day127-133 (S1/S2/S3) --")
for row in r['rows']:
    fail = row['cancelled']/(row['cancelled']+row['subscribed']) if (row['cancelled']+row['subscribed'])>0 else None
    print(row['group_id'], row, f"fail_rate={fail:.3f}" if fail is not None else "")

    print(row)

for row in r5['rows']:

r6 = nm.query("SELECT * FROM macroeconomic_conditions ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 5")

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))

import novamind_api as nm

# For S1 customers who had a checkpoint this week (billing_day_mod30 in 7-13, start_day<=126),
# compare issue history for those who cancelled (end_day 127-133) vs those still subscribed.
q = """
SELECT s.customer_id, s.status, s.end_day
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN (7,8,9,10,11,12,13)
  AND s.start_day <= 126
  AND c.group_id = 'S1'
  AND ( (s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 127 AND 133) OR s.status='subscribed' )
"""
r = nm.query(q)
cancelled_ids = [row['customer_id'] for row in r['rows'] if row['status']=='cancelled']
subscribed_ids = [row['customer_id'] for row in r['rows'] if row['status']=='subscribed']
print(f"cancelled this wk: {len(cancelled_ids)}, still subscribed: {len(subscribed_ids)}")

def issue_stats(ids, label):
    if not ids:
        print(label, "no ids")
        return
    ids_str = ",".join(str(i) for i in ids)
    q2 = f"""
    SELECT COUNT(*) as total_issues,
           SUM(CASE WHEN status='open' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as open_issues,
           AVG(days_open) as avg_days_open,
           COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) as customers_with_issues
    FROM issues WHERE customer_id IN ({ids_str})
    """
    r2 = nm.query(q2)
    print(label, "n_customers=", len(ids), r2['rows'])

issue_stats(cancelled_ids, "CANCELLED S1 this wk:")
issue_stats(subscribed_ids, "STILL SUBSCRIBED S1:")

# fraction of each group with at least one issue ever
def frac_with_issue(ids, label):
    if not ids: return
    ids_str = ",".join(str(i) for i in ids)
    q3 = f"SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) as n FROM issues WHERE customer_id IN ({ids_str})"
    r3 = nm.query(q3)
    n_with = r3['rows'][0]['n']
    print(label, f"{n_with}/{len(ids)} = {n_with/len(ids)*100:.1f}% have >=1 issue ever")

frac_with_issue(cancelled_ids, "CANCELLED:")
frac_with_issue(subscribed_ids, "SUBSCRIBED:")

This week I initially saw fail rates creeping up (S1 6.8%→10.0%, S2 6.7%→13.3%, S3 56.6%→68.1% — see

a cohort-level simulator using the REAL current subscription book (per group×billing-bucket, exact
listed_price/promotion/ramp-status from DB) projected all the way to day504, parameterized by
(devops $/week) → (assumed fail rate). Ran it across devops from $0 to $15,000/wk crossed with THREE
fail-rate-sensitivity assumptions (mild/moderate/aggressive improvement from spend) AND a worst-case
(spend has ZERO effect, fail rates return to full wk17 crisis levels 34%/36.5%/75% regardless). **In
EVERY single scenario tested — including the worst case where spend is assumed to do NOTHING — LOWER
devops spend produced MORE cash at every horizon out to day504.** E.g. at devops=$0/wk with crisis-level
fail rates (spend totally ineffective): day504 cash ≈ -$44K. At devops=$9,500/wk with the SAME crisis
fail rates: day504 cash ≈ -$547K. The mechanism: our revenue base (~$15-16K/wk) is now so small that
ANY devops spend approaching or exceeding that (e.g. $10-15K/wk) is 65-100%+ of total revenue — no
plausible retention benefit can pay that back, because even a fully-fixed retention problem only saves
you the marginal churned revenue, which is much smaller than the spend itself at this scale. **Lesson:
next time fail rates tick up, do NOT reflexively restore spend — first run the full-horizon simulator
(script preserved as `week19_forecast_sim3.py`, reusable — just refresh `week19_book.json` via
`week19_forecast_data.py` each time) across a spend range and a fail-rate-sensitivity range including

keep being true until/unless revenue grows substantially (which requires new acquisition, currently
dead, or R&D) — so bias should stay toward LOW discretionary spend for the foreseeable future.

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    q2 = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_this_wk,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as still_subscribed,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day < {week_start}) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_before,
           COUNT(*) as total
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND c.group_id IN ('S1','S2','S3')
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r2 = nm.query(q2)
    for row in r2['rows']:
        denom = row['cancelled_this_wk'] + row['still_subscribed']
        rate = row['cancelled_this_wk']/denom if denom>0 else None

import json

with open('week19_book.json') as f:
    book = json.load(f)

CASH0 = 125963.0
DAY0 = 133
END_DAY = 504
HORIZON = END_DAY - DAY0

TARGET_PROMO = {"S1": 12.0, "S2": 15.0, "S3": 25.0}

def build_cohorts():
    cohorts = []
    for row in book:
        g = row['group_id']
        if g not in TARGET_PROMO:
            continue
        ramped = abs(row['avg_promo'] - TARGET_PROMO[g]) < 1.0
        cohorts.append({
            'group': g, 'bucket': row['bucket'], 'n': row['n'],
            'listed_price': row['avg_listed'], 'promo': row['avg_promo'],
            'ramped': ramped, 'next_checkpoint': None,
        })
    for c in cohorts:
        b = c['bucket']
        nc = DAY0 - (DAY0 % 30) + b
        while nc <= DAY0:
            nc += 30
        c['next_checkpoint'] = nc
    return cohorts

COMPUTE_PER_SUB_PER_WEEK = 8153.11 / 3205
CAPACITY_PER_WEEK = 3710.0
LEAD_ACQ_PER_WEEK = 190.0

def run_scenario(devops_per_week, fail_rates, days_forward):
    sim_cohorts = build_cohorts()
    cash = CASH0
    total_subs = sum(c['n'] for c in sim_cohorts)
    trajectory = {}
    min_cash = cash
    min_cash_day = 0

    for day in range(DAY0+1, DAY0+1+days_forward):
        revenue_today = 0.0
        for c in sim_cohorts:
            if day == c['next_checkpoint'] and c['n'] > 0.01:
                if not c['ramped']:
                    c['promo'] = TARGET_PROMO[c['group']]
                    c['ramped'] = True
                eff_price = max(0.0, c['listed_price'] - c['promo'])
                fail = fail_rates[c['group']]
                billed_n = c['n']
                survivors = billed_n * (1 - fail)
                revenue_today += survivors * eff_price
                churned = billed_n - survivors
                c['n'] = survivors
                total_subs -= churned
                c['next_checkpoint'] += 30

        compute_today = COMPUTE_PER_SUB_PER_WEEK * total_subs / 7.0
        capacity_today = CAPACITY_PER_WEEK / 7.0
        lead_acq_today = LEAD_ACQ_PER_WEEK / 7.0
        devops_today = devops_per_week / 7.0

        cash += revenue_today - compute_today - capacity_today - lead_acq_today - devops_today
        if cash < min_cash:
            min_cash = cash
            min_cash_day = day - DAY0

        offset = day - DAY0
        if offset in (7, 28, 84, 182, 371):
            trajectory[offset] = cash

    return trajectory, cash, total_subs, min_cash, min_cash_day

# Sensitivity sweep: assume MILD fail-rate degradation as spend drops (weak causal link,
# consistent with crisis having been fixed via pricing not spend)
def fail_rates_for_spend(devops_wk):
    # baseline at devops=9500 (this-session original plan): S1=8%,S2=8%,S3=65%
    # at devops=0: S1=13%,S2=17%,S3=78%  (mild degradation, capped, NOT a return to 34%/75% crisis
    #    since that crisis was fixed by pricing/tier not spend)
    # linear interpolation between these anchors, clipped
    lo, hi = 0.0, 9500.0
    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, devops_wk / hi))
    s1 = 0.13 - t*(0.13-0.08)
    s2 = 0.17 - t*(0.17-0.08)
    s3 = 0.78 - t*(0.78-0.65)
    return {'S1': s1, 'S2': s2, 'S3': s3}

print(f"{'devops/wk':>12} {'S1fail':>7} {'S2fail':>7} {'S3fail':>7} {'+28d':>10} {'+84d':>10} {'+182d':>10} {'+371d(day504)':>14} {'min_cash':>12}")
for devops in [0, 700, 1400, 2100, 2800, 3500, 4200, 5250, 7000, 9500, 12000, 15000]:
    rates = fail_rates_for_spend(devops)
    traj, final_cash, final_subs, min_cash, min_cash_day = run_scenario(devops, rates, HORIZON)
    print(f"{devops:>12} {rates['S1']*100:>6.1f}% {rates['S2']*100:>6.1f}% {rates['S3']*100:>6.1f}% "
          f"${traj[28]:>9,.0f} ${traj[84]:>9,.0f} ${traj[182]:>9,.0f} ${traj[371]:>13,.0f} ${min_cash:>11,.0f}")

def build_cohorts():
    cohorts = []

        g, p = row['group_id'], row['plan']
        key = (g,p)
        if key not in TARGET_PROMO:
            continue
        target = TARGET_PROMO[key]
        ramped = abs(row['avg_promo'] - target) < 1.0
        cohorts.append({
            'group': g, 'plan': p, 'bucket': row['bucket'], 'n': row['n'],
            'listed_price': row['avg_listed'], 'promo': row['avg_promo'],
            'ramped': ramped, 'next_checkpoint': None,
        })
    for c in cohorts:
        b = c['bucket']
        nc = DAY0 - (DAY0 % 30) + b
        while nc <= DAY0:
            nc += 30
        c['next_checkpoint'] = nc
    return cohorts

def fail_rate_at_cycle(group, cycle, scenario):
    """cycle = number of 30-day checkpoints elapsed since day140 (0-indexed for the *next* one)."""
    base = BASE_FAIL[group]
    if scenario == 'plateau':
        return base
    elif scenario == 'moderate_accel':
        # growth decays from ~1.20 toward 1.0
        g = 1.0
        rate = base
        for i in range(cycle+1):
            growth = 1.0 + 0.20*(0.75**i)
            rate = min(0.97, rate*growth) if i>0 else rate
        return rate
    elif scenario == 'aggressive_accel':
        obs_growth = {"S1": 1.50, "S2": 1.90, "S3": 1.10}[group]
        rate = base
        for i in range(cycle):
            decay_growth = 1.0 + (obs_growth-1.0)*(0.7**i)
            rate = min(0.97, rate*decay_growth)
        return rate
    else:
        raise ValueError(scenario)

def spend_fail_adjustment(devops_wk, mode):
    """Additive pp adjustment to fail rate based on spend level. mode='irrelevant' -> 0 always."""
    if mode == 'irrelevant':
        return {"S1":0.0, "S2":0.0, "S3":0.0}
    # 'helps_a_little': at $0 spend, +3pp S1, +3pp S2, +1pp S3 (small); at >=5250 -> 0; linear
    ref = 5250.0
    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, devops_wk/ref))
    return {"S1": 0.03*(1-t), "S2": 0.03*(1-t), "S3": 0.01*(1-t)}

def run_scenario(devops_per_week, fail_scenario, spend_mode, days_forward, capacity_downgrade=True):
    sim_cohorts = build_cohorts()
    cash = CASH0
    trajectory = {}
    min_cash = cash
    cycle_count = {"S1":0, "S2":0, "S3":0}

    # applied to current population per group (population changes over time as cohorts churn)
    def total_pop():
        pop = {"S1":0.0,"S2":0.0,"S3":0.0}
        for c in sim_cohorts:
            pop[c['group']] += c['n']
        return pop

    for day in range(DAY0+1, DAY0+1+days_forward):
        revenue_today = 0.0
        adj = spend_fail_adjustment(devops_per_week, spend_mode)
        for c in sim_cohorts:

                g, p = c['group'], c['plan']
                target = TARGET_PROMO[(g,p)]
                if not c['ramped']:

                eff_price = max(0.0, c['listed_price'] - c['promo'])
                fail = min(0.97, fail_rate_at_cycle(g, cycle_count[g], fail_scenario) + adj[g])
                billed_n = c['n']
                survivors = billed_n * (1 - fail)
                revenue_today += survivors * eff_price

        pop = total_pop()

        compute_today = sum(c['n'] * COMPUTE_PER_CUST_MONTH[(c['group'],c['plan'])] / 30.0 for c in sim_cohorts)

        # capacity tier decision based on projected usage (peak-safety margin factor 1.3x avg)
        total_usage_day = sum(pop[g]*USAGE_PER_CUST_DAY[g] for g in pop)
        if capacity_downgrade:
            if total_usage_day*1.3 < 200000 and cur_tier > 1:
                cur_tier = 1
            if total_usage_day*1.3 < 50000 and cur_tier > 0:

        capacity_today = {2: CAPACITY_PER_WEEK_TIER2, 1: CAPACITY_PER_WEEK_TIER1, 0: CAPACITY_PER_WEEK_TIER0}[cur_tier] / 7.0

        devops_today = devops_per_week / 7.0

        cash += revenue_today - compute_today - capacity_today - lead_acq_today - devops_today
        if cash < min_cash:
            min_cash = cash

        offset = day - DAY0
        if offset in (7, 28, 84, 182, 364):

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 140 (Week 20 actions EXECUTED). Cash $117,437 → advancing to day147/Week 21.

## 🚨🚨 TOP-LEVEL STRATEGIC PIVOT THIS WEEK: went to ZERO discretionary dev+ops spend (from $5,250/wk),
## confirmed R&D is a dead end for the foreseeable future (already sunk $500K on it early game; next
## tier costs $500K vs our $117K cash), and identified WHY fail rates keep accelerating: a DENSE CLUSTER
## of competitor events (7+ distinct events in the last ~27 days, magnitudes 0.013–0.25!) is driving
## customer expectations up far faster than any affordable spend could ever counter. This is now a
## "harvest mode" business: minimize burn, extract revenue from the shrinking book, downsize infra as
## it shrinks, bank cash. See sections 1-3 below — read before ever considering a spend increase again.

### 1. Fail-rate checkpoint (methodology: `week20_checkpoint.py`, buckets = day%30 due this week)
- **S1: 10.0% (last wk) → 15.1% (this wk). S2: 13.3% → 25.6%. S3: 68.1% → 75.6%.** All THREE groups
  accelerated again, and worse than last week's jump. This is the 3rd straight week of acceleration:
  S1: 6.8→10.0→15.1 (×1.47,×1.51). S2: 6.7→13.3→25.6 (×1.99,×1.92). S3: 56.6→68.1→75.6 (×1.20,×1.11).
- **ROOT CAUSE FOUND (via `get_social_posts`, scanning for competitor mentions):** a wave of competitor
  events hit in the past ~4 weeks: day113 (+0.013), day114 (+0.185), day115 (+0.25!), day120 (ref to
  0.25 again), day138 (+0.061), day139 (+0.071), day140 (+0.063 ×2, two competitors same week). These
  are PERMANENT upward shifts to customer expected quality (per game mechanics) — a 0.25 single-event
  jump is *larger than our entire delivered quality for S1 Plan A* (0.406)! No affordable dev spend can
  plausibly close gaps this size (see R&D math below). **This — not our dev-spend cuts — is almost
  certainly the dominant driver of the fail-rate acceleration.** Confirmed via: our per-group dev bonus
  was FROZEN (identical to last week, since targeted spend has been $0 for 2 weeks) yet fail rate still
  jumped hugely — so the jump can't be from "we withdrew spend," it's from expectations rising against a
  flat quality bar. **Lesson: always check `get_social_posts(days=14+)` for competitor magnitude when
  fail rates jump — this explains a LOT that pure spend/ops analysis misses.**

### 2. R&D economics — fully clarified, now confirmed a dead end for the foreseeable future
Checked `list_research_projects()`: we ALREADY completed tier 1 (day7, cost $166,667, boost +0.0289) and
tier 2 (day14, cost $333,333, boost +0.0619) very early game — total **$500,000 spent, +0.0908 quality
delivered**, folded into the "global_bonus" we see on the dashboard (0.1955 today = q_shared-from-dev +
these two R&D boosts combined). **Tier 3 (next available) costs $500,000; tier 4 $666,667; tiers scale
up to tier 20 in the many millions.** We have $117,437 cash. Given competitor events regularly deliver
single-shot expectation jumps of 0.06–0.25, and our *combined two R&D wins ever* only total +0.09, R&D
at any tier we could remotely afford would NOT reliably close the gap even if we could save up for it —
and saving up is not realistically happening (cash is declining, not growing, even after this week's
cuts in the pessimistic scenario). **New conclusion: stop treating "save for R&D" as a live plan. It was
reasonable to try early (when cash was $1M+); at current scale it's not coming back into range. Revisit
ONLY if cash unexpectedly grows past ~$600-700K (comfortable buffer over tier-3's $500K), which is not
the base case in any of this week's simulations.**

### 3. 🔑 Full-horizon simulator (to day504) — spend=$0 dominates in EVERY scenario, more decisively
## than ever
Rebuilt the cohort simulator fresh (`week20_forecast_data.py` → `week20_book.json`, then
`week20_forecast_sim.py` / `week20_forecast_final.py`) using this week's REAL fail rates (15.1/25.6/
75.6%) as the base, crossed with 3 fail-rate-evolution scenarios (plateau / moderate_accel /
aggressive_accel, the latter two extrapolating the observed 3-week acceleration pattern with decaying
growth rates) AND 2 spend-sensitivity modes (spend truly irrelevant vs. spend helps a little).
**Result: at devops=$5,250/wk (last week's setting), day504 cash is NEGATIVE in ALL 3 fail scenarios
(-$84K to -$198K). At devops=$0/wk, day504 cash is POSITIVE in all 3 ($74.8K to $188.6K).** This is a
much larger, more decisive gap than last week's already-strong finding (because fail rates are now
higher, so the same $/week burn represents an even worse trade against a smaller/faster-shrinking
revenue base). **ACTION: cut ops ($650/day: $500 global+$150 S1 targeted) and dev ($100/day global) BOTH
to $0.** Also confirmed the CAPACITY TIER DOWNGRADE lever is huge: in the same scenario, day504 cash is
$188,610 with the model's downgrade logic enabled vs. $92,020 with it disabled — nearly 2x! **NOT safe
yet this week** (peak usage this week hit 409,730/day; tier-1 caps at 200,000/day) but this is the
single biggest lever to watch for going forward as the book shrinks. Re-run this simulator every week
(refresh book via `week20_forecast_data.py` pattern) before ANY spend change — process fix carried
forward unchanged from last week, now reinforced twice.

### 4. S3 Plan B/C confirmed COMPUTE-COST-NEGATIVE even at FULL list price (new finding this week)
Computed real per-customer margins (listed_price − promo − compute_cost) by group×plan using actual
usage this week (`week20_state.py` / `week20_usage_margin.py`):
- S1 A: net rev ~$22.13/mo, compute ~$4.61/mo → **margin +$17.52** (healthy)
- S2 A: net ~$23.13, compute ~$9.88 → **+$13.25** (healthy). S2 B: net ~$61.63, compute ~$57.60 →
  **+$4.03** (thin but positive)
- S3 A: net ~$24.79, compute ~$24.31 → **+$0.48** (breakeven)
- **S3 B: net ~$58.24, compute ~$148.25 → MARGIN = -$90.01/month/customer!** Even at ZERO promotion
  (full $73.58 list price), compute cost ($148.25) still exceeds it — this is NOT a promotion/discount
  problem, Plan B's list price itself can't cover Tier-4 compute cost at S3's heavy usage (~412
  units/day avg, quota is 1200/day so no quota throttling, they're just heavy users on an
  underpriced-for-them plan). S3 C similarly negative (~-$25/mo). Fixing via a Plan-B price hike big
  enough to matter (~2x, to ~$164) would also hit S2's 95 Plan-B customers (currently healthy/positive)
  — not worth the collateral risk to a segment we still want. Fixing via lower model tier for Plan B
  hurts quality for S2 too (risk of accelerating their churn, since quality-gap is the dominant churn
  driver) — also rejected.
- **ACTION TAKEN: restructured S3 promotion — set `by_group S3=0` + `by_group_plan S3:{"A":25}`,
  leaving S1=12/S2=15 unchanged.** Net effect: S3 Plan A keeps its full $25 discount (unchanged,
  roughly-breakeven segment, no reason to squeeze harder), while S3 Plan B/C promo drops from ~$15-22
  (mid-ramp) to $0 (full price) at each customer's NEXT billing checkpoint (~30-day ramp, same mechanic
  as always). This can't fix the underlying negative compute margin, but extracts more $ per customer
  before they inevitably churn (75.6% monthly fail regardless), and if it accelerates their departure
  that's fine too — stops the compute bleed sooner. Modest total upside (~few hundred $/week, decaying
  as S3 population — currently only 62 in B/C — keeps shrinking fast) but zero real downside.

### 5. Social media: SKIPPED posting this week (deliberate choice, not an oversight)
Our best-performing post pattern (+0.65 effect, used successfully 4x: posts 10/11/12/14) is "acknowledge
complaint + announce a concrete operational fix / budget commitment." **This week we are CUTTING
support/dev spend to zero, so posting that pattern would be dishonest and could damage credibility once
reality doesn't match the claim** (post 15 from last week already partially had this problem — watch its
week-2 effect for a natural experiment on whether customers notice/care about the gap between
announcement and actual magnitude). Decided to preserve the 1-post/week budget for a week when we have
something genuinely true to say. Check post 15's cumulative effect next week as a data point.

# For S1 customers who had a checkpoint this week (billing_day_mod30 in 7-13, start_day<=126),

q = """

FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN (7,8,9,10,11,12,13)
  AND s.start_day <= 126
  AND c.group_id = 'S1'
  AND ( (s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 127 AND 133) OR s.status='subscribed' )
"""
r = nm.query(q)

subscribed_ids = [row['customer_id'] for row in r['rows'] if row['status']=='subscribed']

    ids_str = ",".join(str(i) for i in ids)
    q2 = f"""

           SUM(CASE WHEN status='open' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as open_issues,
           AVG(days_open) as avg_days_open,
           COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) as customers_with_issues
    FROM issues WHERE customer_id IN ({ids_str})

def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    q2 = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_this_wk,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as still_subscribed,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day < {week_start}) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_before,
           COUNT(*) as total
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND c.group_id IN ('S1','S2','S3')
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r2 = nm.query(q2)
    for row in r2['rows']:

        print(row, f"fail_rate_this_wk={rate:.3f}" if rate is not None else "n/a")

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    q2 = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_this_wk,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as still_subscribed,
           COUNT(*) as total
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND c.group_id IN ('S1','S2','S3')
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r2 = nm.query(q2)
    for row in r2['rows']:
        denom = row['cancelled_this_wk'] + row['still_subscribed']
        rate = row['cancelled_this_wk']/denom if denom>0 else None
        print(row, f"fail_rate_this_wk={rate*100:.1f}%" if rate is not None else "n/a")
