# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 147, THIS session. Cash $113,425 at session start. Actions executed THIS session
## (day147, effective day148) → advancing to day154/Week 22 dashboard next.

## 🚨🚨 MAJOR STRATEGIC REVERSAL THIS SESSION: ops spend $0 → $900/day. READ THIS FIRST.
Last session (day140) cut ops+dev to true $0 as a "harvest mode" pivot, believing competitor-driven
quality drift was the dominant churn driver and ops spend didn't matter much (weak historical
issue-churn correlation). **This week's data proves that conclusion was WRONG / incomplete for the ops
side.** Evidence (all gathered day147, methodology in `week21_*.py` scripts):
1. **Issue resolution is 100% GATED on ops spend — a hard mechanical fact, not a soft correlation.**
   `SELECT resolution_type, COUNT(*) FROM issues GROUP BY resolution_type` → ONLY 'ops_resolved' or NULL
   exist as values, ever. At old $650/day ops: resolved ~400-419/day. The day after cutting to $0
   (day141): resolved collapsed to 3,3,1,1,1,6,1 per day. Backlog exploded 559→2457 open in ONE week.
   **At $0 ops spend, issues essentially NEVER resolve (~2/day trickle), regardless of backlog size.**
2. **Fail rate (checkpoint methodology) DOUBLED in one week, with ZERO new competitor events:**
   S1: 10.0%→15.1%→**32.1%**. S2: 13.3%→25.6%→**51.8%**. S3: 68.1%→75.6%→**87.8%**. The S1 jump
   (n=446 this week) is >10 standard errors from the prior week's rate — a real structural shift, not
   noise. `get_social_posts` scan confirmed NO new competitor quality-boost event since day140 (last one
   was day140 itself) — so this acceleration can't be attributed to competitor drift this time.
3. **Direct customer complaints exploded:** 6 distinct social posts (days140-147) specifically about
   unresolved support tickets — "submitted 10 days ago and radio silence," "passed around like a hot
   potato 3x this week," "got an auto-reply... it's been 36hrs and radio silence," and one **explicitly
   warning prospective customers away**: "thinking about trying NovaMind? heads up: great onboarding,
   then... radio silence." This directly damages both retention AND new-lead conversion/reputation.
4. **We broke our own public promise.** Our agent post #15 (day133) said "We're putting real budget
   back into support capacity this week... You'll hear from us much faster going forward" — then day140
   did the OPPOSITE (cut to true $0). Posts #11/12/14/15 (days105,112,126,133) all used an "acknowledge +
   concrete fix" pattern that historically scored +0.35 to +0.65 sentiment — but ONLY if followed
   through. This time we didn't, likely compounding the damage (customers see broken promises, not just
   slow support).
5. Per-customer historical issue-count correlation with churn is still WEAK (cancelled vs retained S1
   customers had similar total/open issue counts) — but this is because the backlog explosion is BRAND
   NEW (this week only); lagged satisfaction effects from newly-unresolved (10+ day old) tickets haven't
   fully hit the churn data yet. The timing/mechanism/social-post triangulation is the strong evidence,
   not the naive per-customer correlation (which looks backward at mostly-already-resolved history).

### ACTION TAKEN (day147, effective day148):
- **Restored ops spend: global $700/day + targeted S1 $200/day = $900/day total** (up from $0; ABOVE the
  old $650/day since backlog is now 4.4x bigger and needs a surge to clear). Dev stays at $0 (this
  crisis is about issue-resolution/satisfaction, NOT the quality-expectation gap — no new competitor
  event this week, so dev spend isn't the lever needed right now).
- **Posted honest social reply** (agent_post_id=16, replying to post 295): explicitly owns the mistake
  ("we cut support spend too far... that's on us") and announces the REAL restored spend. Chose candor
  over another vague promise given the broken-promise history — this time it's backed by an actual
  action already taken, not just words.
- Did NOT touch: prices, model tiers, quotas, promotions (S1/S2 unchanged, S3 ramp-down continues),
  capacity tier (stays 2), R&D (still unaffordable), enterprise (still 0 seats/dead).

### WATCH NEXT WEEK (day154) — did the reversal work?
- Check `issues` opened/resolved counts for days148-154 — expect resolved to jump back up from ~2/day
  toward ~100-400+/day (proportional to the restored $900/day vs old $650/day).
- Check backlog (`status!='resolved'` count) — expect it to start declining from 2457, not necessarily
  all the way back to the old ~559-1000 equilibrium in just one week (backlog is 4x bigger now).
- Re-run checkpoint fail-rate methodology (`week21_checkpoint.py` pattern, buckets due days148-154) for
  S1/S2/S3. KEY QUESTION: does the fail-rate spike start reverting, or keep climbing? Full reversal may
  take 2-4 weeks (satisfaction recovery isn't instant even once tickets start clearing).
  **If fail rates do NOT start improving within 2-3 weeks despite restored spend, STRONGLY consider that
  something else is going on (reputation damage may be "sticky"/slow to repair even after the mechanical
  cause is fixed, or competitor-driven drift has ALSO been quietly compounding) — don't just keep
  throwing money at ops indefinitely if it's not working; re-diagnose.**
- If it IS working: plan to taper ops spend gradually (proportional to shrinking backlog/population) —
  don't hold $900/day flat forever, that would over-spend on an ever-smaller customer base. Target
  tapering to something like $500-700/day once backlog is back under ~800-1000, then lower as the book
  itself naturally shrinks over the game's remaining life.
- Watch whether the honest social post (agent_post_id=16) helps sentiment — check
  `agent_social_media_posts` effect_by_group next week (~1wk lag to populate).

## Fail-rate checkpoint log (methodology: bucket = day%30, due this week; rate = cancelled/(cancelled+still_subscribed) among that week's due cohort)
| Week (days) | S1 | S2 | S3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| buckets 7-13 (127-133) | 10.0% | 13.3% | 68.1% |
| buckets 14-20 (134-140, old $650 ops) | 15.1% | 25.6% | 75.6% |
| buckets 21-27 (141-147, **$0 ops**) | **32.1%** | **51.8%** | **87.8%** |
Re-run weekly with fresh day ranges (script: adapt `week21_checkpoint.py`, just bump the day numbers).

## Usage / capacity tier status (re-check weekly — 2nd biggest lever after ops)
This week (141-147): avg usage 300,942/day, peak 377,775/day (day142). Declining slowly as book shrinks
(prior week: avg 329,808, peak 409,730). **Tier-1 cap is 200,000/day — peak still ~1.9x over that cap,
NOT safe to downgrade.** Need peak comfortably under 200K (with margin) before downgrading tier2→tier1
(saves $315/day = $2,205/wk). Re-check `service_day` table weekly (`week21_usage_check.py` pattern).
Given ops-restoration may slow the population decline (that's the point!), don't assume usage will keep
dropping as fast as the last 2 weeks suggested — re-measure, don't extrapolate blindly.

## Revenue run-rate & billing-bucket lumpiness (IMPORTANT for 1wk forecasts)
Net monthly revenue run-rate (smoothed): SUM(listed_price-promotion) over active book = $63,526/mo this
week (down from $74,981 two weeks ago) → **$14,823/wk if evenly distributed**. But actual weekly billing
is LUMPY — the 30 billing-day-mod-30 buckets range from 20 to 205 customers each (mean 95.7,
this-week's-due-buckets 21-27 summed to only 336 — well below average, hence actual ledger revenue was
only $6,883 this week). **Before forecasting next week's cash, always pull the SPECIFIC upcoming 7
buckets' population+revenue** (`SELECT ... WHERE billing_day_mod30 IN (next 7 bucket numbers)`), not just
the smoothed run-rate — huge difference (this week's smoothed estimate would have been ~2x the actual).
Next week (148-154, buckets 28,29,0,1,2,3,4) has an unusually RICH 912 customers due (~$23.7K gross
before expected attrition) — expect a revenue bounce-back next week for this reason alone, independent
of the ops-spend story.

## Full-horizon simulator (rebuilt this week: `week21_forecast_v2.py`) — key fix vs last week's version
Last week's simulator assumed ops spend stays FLAT forever in the "keep spending" scenarios, which
artificially made $0-spend dominate (fixed costs against a shrinking population look worse and worse).
**Fixed this week: ops spend now tapers proportionally to remaining population** (floor 15% of base) in
the "fix works" / "partial" scenarios. Result: all 3 scenarios (fix-works 45%, fails-cut-losses 20%,
partial 35% — weights reflect my belief the mechanistic evidence is fairly strong but not certain) now
converge to a much more plausible **$88K-$118K day504 range**, vs last week's simulator showing 2-3x
spread favoring zero-spend. **Re-run this simulator fresh every week** (update population/revenue/usage
constants at top from real queries) — and always sanity-check tapering logic is adaptive, not flat.

## Forecast submitted day147 (for calibration check next week)
**Calibration check on prior forecast (submitted day140, target day147):** predicted 1wk point=$114,500
[$108,500-$121,000]; ACTUAL=$113,425. 0.9% error, within CI — good. But that forecast was made BEFORE
discovering the ops-cut crisis, so the good near-term calibration masks the strategic error underneath.
This week's forecast (blended across the 3 scenarios above, weighted 45/20/35, then judgmentally widened
for unmodeled risks — new competitor events, outage risk, macro shifts, uncertainty re: whether the ops
reversal actually works):
Submitted: 1wk pt$110,500 [$104,000-$116,000]. 4wk pt$103,000 [$88,000-$117,000]. 12wk pt$97,000
[$70,000-$128,000]. 26wk pt$90,000 [$40,000-$150,000]. Wide 12wk/26wk intervals are deliberate — this
week's strategic reversal is a genuine fork in the road (works vs. doesn't) and I don't yet know which
branch we're on.

## Cash trajectory log (update each week)
Day 0: $1,000,000 → Day 91: $164,086 → Day 112: $145,171 → Day 126: $130,154 → Day 133: $125,963 →
Day 140: $117,437 → **Day 147: $113,425** (-$4,012; ledger: compute -$6,978, capacity -$3,710,
lead_acquisition -$208, operations $0, development $0, subscription_payment +$6,883 [due-buckets this
week were unusually sparse — 336 customers vs ~670 average — not a fundamental revenue drop, see
lumpiness note above]). This was the FIRST full week of true $0 ops/dev — and it back badly (see
critical reversal above). **Day 154 (next week) will be the first week reflecting restored $900/day ops
— the real test of whether this fixes the fail-rate spike.**

## 📋 PROCESS CHECKLIST — EVERY WEEK
1. Verify actual live config from the dashboard's "Current Config" line (ground truth) — confirmed
   accurate this week (Ops=$0/Dev=$0 as expected from last week's cut). `set_daily_spend` still isn't
   queryable via `config_overrides` — but `set_targeted_ops_spend`/`set_targeted_dev_spend` calls ARE
   logged there (confirmed again this week, id=53).
2. **Before ANY discretionary spend change: rebuild + re-run the full-horizon simulator**
   (`week21_forecast_v2.py` pattern) with FRESH population/revenue/usage data. Make sure spend tapers
   adaptively with population in every scenario (see fix above) — a flat-forever assumption biases
   results toward whichever policy has lower fixed cost.
3. Re-run checkpoint fail-rate methodology weekly for S1/S2/S3 on newly-due buckets. Track the RATE.
4. **When fail rate jumps, check THREE things, not just one:** (a) `get_social_posts(days=14+)` for
   competitor event mentions/magnitudes, (b) our OWN recent agent posts for promises we may have broken,
   (c) direct customer complaints about SPECIFIC operational problems (support delays, outages) by
   scanning ALL recent posts (not just keyword-filtered — complaint posts about internal ops issues
   won't match a "competitor" keyword filter). This week (c)+(b) were the real story, not competitor
   drift.
5. **Ops spend is not just "nice to have faster resolution" — it's a hard gate.** At $0, issues
   essentially never resolve (confirmed: `resolution_type` is only ever 'ops_resolved' or NULL/open;
   at $0 spend, resolved count collapses to ~1-6/day regardless of backlog size). Treat any proposal to
   cut ops to true $0 with extreme caution given this — prefer partial cuts first to test the mechanic's
   shape before going all the way to zero on any lever with a "CRITICAL/WARNING" flag in the docs.
6. For 1-week cash forecasts, pull the SPECIFIC next 7 billing buckets' due population (not just the
   smoothed 30-day run-rate) — weekly bucket sizes are highly lumpy (observed range 20-205 customers per
   single bucket).
7. Track promotion ramp: S3 B/C promo should keep ramping toward 0 (target unchanged this week).
8. Check New Leads vs New Subscribers weekly — still dead (398 leads, 0 subs this week). Also watch
   whether the "radio silence" complaint posts are suppressing lead CONVERSION further (reputation
   effect on lead arrival/conversion speed, per game mechanics) — plausible additional reason for the
   persistent 0-subscriber streak beyond pure quality-price mismatch.
9. Check `macroeconomic_conditions` monthly — stuck at day91's reading (45.3, contraction) as of day147,
   56 days overdue vs ~30-day cadence of first 3 updates. Social-media PMI mentions (post day141 cites
   "46.9") are flavor text and don't numerically sync with `get_market_overview()` (ground truth, 45.3) —

10. **Watch usage trend for capacity tier downgrade (T2→T1)** — 2nd biggest lever. This week: avg
    300,942/day, peak 377,775. Tier 1 caps at 200,000/day — still NOT safe (peak ~1.9x cap). Note: if the

    rate continues, re-measure fresh each week.
11. Watch issues opened/resolved counts as the PRIMARY signal of whether restored ops spend is working —

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    q2 = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_this_wk,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as still_subscribed,
           COUNT(*) as total
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND c.group_id IN ('S1','S2','S3')
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r2 = nm.query(q2)
    for row in r2['rows']:
        denom = row['cancelled_this_wk'] + row['still_subscribed']
        rate = row['cancelled_this_wk']/denom if denom>0 else None
        print(row, f"fail_rate_this_wk={rate*100:.1f}%" if rate is not None else "n/a")

checkpoint_report(127, 133, "3wks ago (buckets 7-13)")
checkpoint_report(134, 140, "2wks ago (buckets 14-20)")
checkpoint_report(141, 147, "THIS WEEK (buckets 21-27)")

### Commands

#### `novamind register-daily-script`

Register a Python script to run automatically at the start of each day.

The script content is snapshotted at registration time. Subsequent edits
to the source file will NOT affect the registered version. To update,
re-register the script.

If a script with the same filename already exists, it is overwritten.
Scripts are executed in alphabetical order at the start of each day,
with novamind_api pre-imported.

Args:
    script_path: Path to the Python script to register.

Example:
    novamind register-daily-script my_strategy.py

#### `novamind list-daily-scripts`

List all registered daily scripts.

Shows script names and sizes. Scripts run at the start of each day
in alphabetical order.

Example:
    novamind list-daily-scripts

#### `novamind remove-daily-script`

Remove a registered daily script.

Args:
    script_name: Filename of the script to remove.

Example:
    novamind remove-daily-script my_strategy.py

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 154 (Week 22). Cash $110,764 at week start → actions this session: NONE to
## config (deliberately held everything steady to get a clean read on the ops-spend fix). Posted 1
## social reply. Advancing to Week 23 / Day 161 dashboard next.

## ✅ HEADLINE RESULT: THE OPS-SPEND REVERSAL (from day147) IS WORKING. Confirmed with data.
Day147 restored ops spend $0→$900/day ($700 global + $200 S1-targeted) after diagnosing that $0 ops
spend caused issue-resolution to collapse and fail-rates to spike (see prior weeks' notes if needed —
that narrative is now resolved, condensing here). This week's evidence it's working:
1. **Issues resolved: 16/wk ($0 ops) → 3,481/wk ($900 ops).** Backlog (status!='resolved'): 2457→891
   (query) / 2087→365 (dashboard headline). Daily resolved counts started ~530-565/day early week,
   tapered to ~370-400/day late week as backlog shrank (less to resolve, not less capacity).
2. **Checkpoint fail-rate improved for S1 and S2** (see table below): S1 32.1%→26.1%, S2 51.8%→48.6%.
   S3 flat (87.8%→87.2%, tiny/terminal segment, not worth chasing). This is a PARTIAL cycle effect only
   (the billing cohort due this week mostly experienced the OLD $0-ops crisis for ~3 of their 4 weeks,
   with only the last week under restored spend) — expect FURTHER improvement over the next 2-4 weeks as
   more of each cohort's cycle happens entirely under restored spend.
3. Social sentiment turned positive re: the fix (posts day148 #298-302, sentiment scores 0.65 across
   individual groups per agent_post_id=16 effect data) — including one enterprise-flavor commenter (#302)
   expressing interest in "enterprise AI integration" (no actual enterprise lead materialized from it,
   see enterprise section below).
4. **⚠️ WATCH ITEM — issues-OPENED count is RISING through the week** (118→370/day, day148→154), even
   as resolved stayed high. Backlog is still shrinking net (resolved>opened) but the gap is narrowing —
   by day154 opened(370)=resolved(370) exactly. Two candidate explanations, NOT mutually exclusive: (a)
   lagged satisfaction-recovery — the crisis week's damage to satisfaction takes time to heal even after
   the mechanical fix, so elevated issue-generation may persist a bit before reverting; (b) a small new
   competitor event on day148 (ApexSaaS, +0.0117 quality, modest) nudging expectations up further. Rise
   is BROAD-BASED across S1/S2/S3 proportionally (not isolated to one group), consistent with (a) more
   than a group-specific problem. **NEXT WEEK: check whether opened-count reverts down (confirms lagged
   recovery, good) or keeps climbing/plateaus at ~370+/day (would mean a new higher equilibrium, needs
   more ops spend or re-diagnosis).** Backlog age this week: avg 11.3-17.1 days across groups (S3 oldest),
   max age 114 days for one ancient ticket — still elevated but should keep dropping if net-resolved holds.
5. Decision: held ops spend FLAT at $900/day this week (no taper yet, no increase either) — backlog not
   fully cleared, opened-count trend not yet confirmed reverting. Don't repeat the mistake of changing
   two things at once; let this experiment run clean one more week before adjusting.

## 🔍 MAJOR NEW FINDING: root-caused the persistent "0 new subscribers" mystery (flagged unresolved for
## many weeks). Likely mechanism: TENURE LOYALTY BONUS is propping up renewals; brand-new leads have none.
Confirmed via direct query: S1 last actually WON a new subscriber on **day107** (plan A) / day56 (plan
B). S2 last won day77-79. S3 last won day67-70. That's **47-98+ days of literally ZERO new conversions**
despite continuous lead flow (422-433 new leads/week) and existing lead promotions ($10 off for S1/S2/S3).
Every single lead in the last 21 days across all 3 groups (1002 S1 + 101 S2 + 78 S3 = 1181 total) ended
in status='lost'. Meanwhile EXISTING subscribers still pass their periodic 30-day quality check at 52-74%
(S1/S2) — clearly a different bar applies to renewals vs new leads. Best explanation: the game's **tenure
loyalty stickiness bonus** (additive Q_perceived boost growing with ln(1+months_subscribed), up to ~+0.13
at 12mo per game mechanics) is the ONLY thing separating a passing existing customer from a failing new
lead — the raw (drifted-up-over-154-days) expectation bar now apparently exceeds what we deliver for a
ZERO-tenure customer, but tenured veterans scrape by on the bonus. **Caveat: not fully proven.** The
group_insights quality_floor_q_min estimates (S1=0.081, noisy ±65%, info level 1, likely STALE/never
refreshed since day0) look way below our delivered quality (0.40+), which superficially contradicts a
pure "quality gap" story — but that estimate is for the floor "at $0 price" and may simply not reflect
154 days of accumulated drift + competitor events. Bottom line implications:
  - Ad spend on individual groups is CONFIRMED worthless right now (correctly at $0 already) — don't
    waste money there until/unless something structurally changes.
  - Only a MAJOR quality jump (R&D tier 3+, $500K+, currently unaffordous) or possibly much deeper
    lead-specific pricing/promotion cuts could plausibly revive new-lead conversion. Given cash
    constraints, neither is actionable right now.
  - **We are in permanent managed decline / harvest mode for the individual segment.** The only levers
    that matter now are: (1) retention of the existing tenured base via ops spend (proven to work, keep
    doing it), (2) cost discipline (taper spend proportionally as the base shrinks, don't overspend on a
    shrinking population), (3) avoid actions that accelerate churn (e.g., don't cut ops again, don't
    raise effective prices on existing subs).

## 🔍 Enterprise: confirmed structurally dead since day 0, deprioritized (not a recent problem)
Queried full history: `enterprise_turns` table is **completely empty — zero rows, ever** (no leads, no
threads, nothing, for E1/E2/E3, across all 154 days). Past attempts existed (modest LinkedIn ad spend
days49-105, up to ~$100-150/day combined across E1-E3) but were zeroed out day105 after presumably
yielding nothing, consistent with zero turns ever recorded. E-group quality floor estimates (info level 1,
±65% noise, likely stale): E1 q_min=0.736, E2=1.094(!), E3=0.668 — all far above our delivered E-quality
(0.2945-0.4319, ZERO group bonus ever targeted at E-groups, unlike S1/S2/S3 which got dev investment
early game). **Considered a small renewed LinkedIn test this week (E1, "cost-cutting" persona, cheapest
WTP/floor) — decided AGAINST it**: 55+ days of past nonzero spend already produced zero signal, cash is
tight, and I didn't want a second simultaneous experiment confounding the ops-spend read this week. MAYBE
revisit with a sustained multi-week small-budget (~$75-100/day) test ONLY once cash stabilizes/grows —
not now. Enterprise inbox check remains a 30-second routine weekly regardless (in case this changes).

## Fail-rate checkpoint log (methodology: bucket = day%30, due this week; rate = cancelled/(cancelled+still_subscribed) among that week's due cohort)
| Week (days) | S1 | S2 | S3 | Ops spend that week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| buckets 14-20 (134-140) | 15.1% | 25.6% | 75.6% | $650 (old normal) |
| buckets 21-27 (141-147) | 32.1% | 51.8% | 87.8% | $0 (crisis) |
| buckets 28-4 (148-154)  | **26.1%** | **48.6%** | 87.2% | $900 (restored, partial-cycle effect only) |
Re-run weekly (script: `week22_analysis.py` section 4, bump day ranges). Expect continued improvement
over next 2-4 weeks as more of each cohort's cycle falls entirely under restored spend.

## Usage / capacity tier status (re-check weekly)
This week (148-154): avg usage 266,912/day, peak 338,896/day (day149) — DOWN from last week (avg
300,942, peak 377,775), tracking population decline. **Tier-1 cap is 200,000/day — peak still ~1.7x over
that cap, NOT safe to downgrade yet.** Keep monitoring; if ops-fix slows churn as hoped, usage decline
will slow too — re-measure fresh each week, don't extrapolate. Downgrade T2→T1 saves $315/day=$2,205/wk
once peak comfortably clears 200K with margin (target peak <150-160K before switching).

## Revenue run-rate & billing-bucket lumpiness (IMPORTANT for 1wk forecasts — always pull specific buckets)
This week actual: 620 customers billed, $13,825 net (buckets 28,29,0-4 — as predicted last week, a richer
bucket set than the prior week's 336/$6,883). Net revenue by group (active book, monthly): S1 $43,228
(2272 cust, avg $19.03/mo net), S2 $7,900 (241 cust, avg $32.78), S3 $2,519 (65 cust, avg $38.75).
**Next week (days155-161, buckets 5,6,7,8,9,10,11) is an EXCEPTIONALLY RICH set: 1,012 customers due,
$21,865 gross-listed before attrition** (S1 855/$16,189, S2 116/$3,752, S3 41/$1,924) — these are the
single richest 7 contiguous buckets in the whole 30-bucket distribution (bucket sizes range 20-205, mean
85.9; buckets 5-11 = [201,205,181,135,124,91,75]). Applying current fail rates (~74% S1 pass, ~52% S2,
~13% S3) → expect ~$14,000-14,800 actually billed. **Always pull the SPECIFIC next-7-buckets due
population before forecasting** — smoothed run-rate is a bad proxy given this much lumpiness.

## Forecast model (rebuilt this week: `week22_forecast.py`) — hybrid method
Method: (1) use the PRECISE next-7-bucket billing data (above) for the 1-week revenue anchor — much more
accurate than a smoothed run-rate for short horizons; (2) use a 3-scenario Monte-Carlo-ish population/fail-
rate/ops-taper simulator for the trajectory shape across weeks 2-26+, then apply the week1 anchor's offset
to the whole trajectory. Scenarios: H1 fix-works-well (fail rates keep improving to a floor BETTER than
pre-crisis, weight 0.50), H2 stalls-worsens (improvement reverses, weight 0.20), H3 partial-plateau
(modest improvement then flat, weight 0.30) — weights reflect this week's real improvement evidence
(more confident than last week, but only 1 data point so not fully confident). Key structural insight from
the model: in the optimistic/partial scenarios, cash and population **bottom out around month 3-4 and
partially STABILIZE** as ops spend tapers proportionally to a shrinking-but-loyal "core tenured" base that
settles at a survivable pass-rate — i.e., harvest mode can plausibly reach a new equilibrium, not
necessarily going to zero. Only the "stalls/worsens" scenario (0.20 weight) trends toward near-total
population collapse by day504 (pop≈8). **Re-run this every week** with fresh population/revenue/usage/
fail-rate inputs — update the `groups` dict and scenario fail-rate/ops schedules from real data each time.

## Forecast submitted day154 (for calibration check next week)
**Calibration check on prior forecast (submitted day147, target day154):** predicted 1wk point=$110,500
[$104,000-$116,000]; ACTUAL=$110,764. 0.24% error, comfortably within CI — excellent calibration, keep
using the specific-bucket-based method for 1wk forecasts.
This week's forecast (hybrid method above): 1wk pt=$109,000 [$104,000-$114,000] (anchored to the precise
rich-bucket billing data minus expected ops/compute/capacity/lead-acq costs). 4wk pt=$100,000
[$88,000-$111,000]. 12wk pt=$90,000 [$66,000-$113,000]. 26wk pt=$91,000 [$50,000-$136,000]. Wide 12/26wk
bands deliberate — depends heavily on whether the ops-fix's improvement continues (real fork, 1 week of
confirming data isn't enough to narrow much yet).

## Cash trajectory log (update each week)
Day 0: $1,000,000 → Day 91: $164,086 → Day 112: $145,171 → Day 126: $130,154 → Day 133: $125,963 →
Day 140: $117,437 → Day 147: $113,425 → **Day 154: $110,764** (-$2,661; ledger: ops -$6,300 [restored
$900/day, working], compute -$6,259, capacity -$3,710, lead_acquisition -$216.5, dev $0, subscription_
payment +$13,825 [620 billed, richer bucket week as predicted]). Individual subs 2870→2578 (-292 net,
~-10%/week: S1=2272, S2=241, S3=65). **Runway note:** at this week's raw burn (-$2,660/wk) naive
runway ≈ 42 weeks (< 50 weeks remaining) — but this week had elevated (fix-mode) ops spend AND was a
rich billing week; the multi-scenario model above (which tapers ops + reflects lumpiness) is a better
guide and shows plausible stabilization, not a hard countdown to zero. Keep watching actual trend though.

## 📋 PROCESS CHECKLIST — EVERY WEEK
1. Verify actual live config from dashboard's "Current Config" line — NOTE: dashboard's "Ops=$X" label
   only shows the GLOBAL `set_daily_spend` component, NOT targeted ops spend on top of it. Always check
   the ledger's actual `operations` category total ÷ 7 to get the TRUE total daily ops spend (confirmed
   this week: dashboard said "Ops=$700" but ledger showed -$6,300/wk = $900/day exactly, i.e. $700
   global + $200 S1-targeted, both still active).
2. Before any discretionary spend change: rebuild + re-run `week22_forecast.py`-style simulator with
   FRESH data. Keep ops-taper adaptive/proportional to population, never flat-forever.
3. Re-run checkpoint fail-rate methodology weekly for S1/S2/S3 on newly-due buckets (see table above).
4. When fail rate jumps OR improves, check: (a) `get_social_posts` for competitor events, (b) our own
   recent promises/follow-through, (c) unfiltered post scan for operational complaints (support delays,
   outages) — don't rely on keyword filters alone.
5. **Ops spend is a hard gate on issue resolution** (at $0: ~2-16/wk resolved; at $900: ~3,481/wk
   resolved) — never cut it to true $0 again. If tapering, step down gradually and watch backlog/fail-
   rate each step, don't jump straight to a much lower number.
6. For 1-week cash forecasts, ALWAYS pull the SPECIFIC next 7 billing buckets' due population (bucket

## STATUS AS OF: Day 161 (Week 23). Cash $111,918 at week start (UP +$1,154 from $110,764 — first
## gain in a long time). Actions this session: (1) raised lead_promotion sharply as a diagnostic
## experiment (see below), (2) posted 1 social reply, (3) held everything else flat. Advancing to
## Week 24 / Day 168 dashboard next.

## ✅ HEADLINE: CASH POSITIVE THIS WEEK, ops-spend fix CONFIRMED working great for S1.
Cash +$1,153.6 (111,917.78 vs 110,764.18). Ledger: subscription_payment +$15,998 (805 billed — rich
bucket week, buckets 5-11 are large), ops -$6,300 ($900/day, unchanged), compute -$4,669 (down from
-$6,259, tracking usage decline), capacity -$3,710 (tier2, unchanged), lead_acq -$165.5 (331 leads),
dev $0. **Checkpoint fail-rate S1 = 12.5% this week (buckets 5-11) — BETTER than the pre-crisis
baseline of 15.1%!** This is a full-cycle read (not partial like 2wks ago), strong confirmation the
ops-spend restoration (day147, $0→$900/day) fully fixed S1 (91% of our subscriber base). Do NOT mess
with ops spend for S1 — it's working. Table:
| Week (days) | S1 | S2 | S3 | Ops spend |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| buckets 21-27 (141-147) | 32.1% | 51.8% | 87.8% | $0 (crisis) |
| buckets 28-4 (148-154)  | 26.1% | 48.6% | 87.2% | $900 (partial-cycle) |
| buckets 5-11 (155-161)  | **12.5%** | 52.6% | 95.1% | $900 (full-cycle) |
**S2 is STUCK ~50-53%, not improving** despite same ops fix — see next section, this is diagnosed as
NOT an ops/backlog problem, so don't expect ops spend to fix it. **S3 still worsening (95.1%), tiny

print("\n\n########## 4. CHECKPOINT FAIL-RATE (S1/S2/S3) ##########")
def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    q2 = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_this_wk,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as still_subscribed,
           COUNT(*) as total
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND c.group_id IN ('S1','S2','S3')
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r2 = nm.query(q2)
    for row in r2['rows']:
        denom = row['cancelled_this_wk'] + row['still_subscribed']
        rate = row['cancelled_this_wk']/denom if denom>0 else None
        print(row, f"fail_rate_this_wk={rate*100:.1f}%" if rate is not None else "n/a")

print("\n\n########## 7. SOCIAL POSTS (day 154-161) FULL DUMP ##########")
r = nm.query("SELECT post_id, day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE day BETWEEN 154 AND 161 ORDER BY day, post_id")
for row in r['rows']:

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 168 (Week 24). Cash $104,198 at week start (DOWN -$7,720 from $111,918 —
## EXPECTED, small billing-bucket week, forecast nailed it: predicted $104,300 vs actual $104,198,
## 0.1% error). Actions this session: (1) CONCLUDED lead-promotion experiment (0/309 new leads
## converted even at near-zero price — price is NOT the blocker, see finding below), reverted promo
## to modest $10 flat, (2) LAUNCHED ops-spend taper test (global ops $700→$500, total $900→$700/day,
## saves $1,400/wk — first real cost-cut test since the ops fix), (3) posted 1 social reply. Advancing
## to Week 25 / Day 175 dashboard next.

## 🎯 CONCLUSIVE FINDING: lead-promotion experiment DONE — price is NOT the new-customer blocker.
Last week I cranked lead_promotion to extreme levels (S1 $14=covers full list price, S2/S3 $150=covers
full list price of ANY plan, i.e., ~$0 effective first-month price) as a diagnostic test. Result:
**309 new leads arrived (S1268/S2 21/S3 20), ALL 309 have status='lost'. Zero conversions, exactly
like every week for 90-100+ days.** This is about as close to "free" as a price test can get, and it
still didn't move the needle at all. **CONCLUSION: price/promotion is definitively NOT the lever.**
**Leading hypothesis (now much more confident): the tenure-loyalty stickiness bonus (up to +0.13
Q_perceived at 12mo tenure, ln(1+months) growth) is the ONLY thing separating passing EXISTING
customers from failing brand-new leads.** Brand-new leads get ZERO tenure cushion, so they face the
FULL current (drifted-upward) quality expectation with no buffer, while existing customers get
cushioned by loyalty bonus accumulated over months. Quality expectations drift upward continuously
(organic drift + competitor events, permanent/irreversible), so the bar for a zero-tenure lead today is
higher than what current survivors faced when THEY joined months ago. **This means new-customer
acquisition is structurally blocked until delivered_quality rises enough to clear the *current*
zero-tenure bar** — achievable only via large dev spend (log-saturating, slow) or R&D tier completion
(discrete jumps, cheapest tier3 = $500K, we have $104K). **Neither is affordable now. STOP testing
price/promo angles for new-lead conversion — it's a dead end without a quality investment we can't
fund.** Reverted lead_promotion to modest $10 flat (S1/S2/S3) — no cost either way since conversion is
0%, just decluttering. **Re-open this only if cash ever climbs to R&D-affordable levels (~$600K+,
increasingly unlikely per forecast — see below) — until then, individual-segment growth is OFF THE
TABLE. Business is in pure harvest/retention mode for S1/S2/S3; all strategy should optimize existing-
base retention & cost efficiency, not acquisition.**

## 💰 NEW COST-CUT EXPERIMENT LAUNCHED (day168): ops-spend taper test.
Context: cash is on a slow-burn trajectory (~$5-7K/wk average net burn across billing-bucket
lumpiness); at this rate, cash could get uncomfortably low well before day504 unless costs come down
or the bleed is otherwise stopped. Ops spend ($900/day = $6,300/wk) is our single largest controllable
cost. **Verified BEFORE cutting: active-customer open issues = 342 (matches dashboard exactly),
avg_age=0.0, ALL resolved same/next day (resolution delay ~1.0 day flat across S1/S2/S3) — this is
clear over-provisioning evidence, issue resolution is near-instant, so there's likely room to cut
without harm.** **Action: reduced GLOBAL ops $700→$500/day (kept S1-targeted $200/day untouched) —
new total $700/day (was $900), saves $1,400/wk.** This is a SMALL, CONTROLLED cut (22% total reduction)
— NOT a repeat of the catastrophic day140-147 crisis (that was ops $900→$0, a 100% cut, which tripled
S1's fail rate 12-15%→26-32%). Rationale for keeping S1-targeted spend untouched: S1 is 92% of
subscriber base (2098/2283) and the group where the ops fix was most clearly proven to work — don't
mess with that specific lever, only trim the global layer (which also covers S2/S3/enterprise, all
small/dying anyway, lower risk to test there).
**CRITICAL NEXT-WEEK CHECK:** re-run checkpoint fail-rate methodology for S1/S2/S3 on day175 dashboard.
- If S1 fail rate stays in the ~12-18% range (no dramatic spike) AND active-customer issue avg_age
  stays ~0-1 days → taper is SAFE, continue tapering gradually next 2-3 weeks (try $500→$400 global,
  or even $350, watching each step).
- If S1 fail rate jumps sharply (e.g., >20-22%) OR issue avg_age starts climbing (backlog forming) →
  REVERT immediately to $700 global (back to $900 total) — don't wait a second week to confirm, the
  day140 crisis taught us these effects compound fast and are costly to reverse (took ~3 weeks + a
  social-media mea culpa to fully recover last time).

## 📊 Checkpoint fail-rate table (updated day168) — S1 ticked up slightly, watch closely (ops taper risk)
| Week (days) | Buckets | S1 | S2 | S3 | Ops spend | Sample size (S1/S2/S3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

import novamind_api as nm
import json

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

print("\n\n########## 1. SUBSCRIBER STATE ##########")
r = nm.query("""
SELECT c.group_id, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id
ORDER BY n DESC
""")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n=== Subscriber counts & avg promo/price by group+plan (active) ===")
r = nm.query("""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) as n, AVG(s.listed_price) as avg_listed, AVG(s.promotion) as avg_promo
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan
ORDER BY c.group_id, s.plan
""")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n\n########## 2. LEDGER THIS WEEK (169-175) vs LAST WEEK (162-168) ##########")
r = nm.query("""
SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total, COUNT(*) as n
FROM ledger
WHERE day BETWEEN 169 AND 175
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY total
""")
tot = 0
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)
    tot += row['total']
print("NET this week:", tot)

print("\n=== Ledger prior week (162-168) for comparison ===")
r = nm.query("""
SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total, COUNT(*) as n
FROM ledger
WHERE day BETWEEN 162 AND 168
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY total
""")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

r4 = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as tot FROM ledger")
print("\nCash sanity check (all-time ledger sum):", r4['rows'])

print("\n\n########## 3. ISSUES OPENED/RESOLVED TREND ##########")
for label, (a,b) in [("wk22 (148-154, $900 ops restored, partial)",(148,154)), ("wk23 (155-161, $900 ops, full cycle)",(155,161)), ("wk24 (162-168, $900->$700 taper starts)",(162,168))]:
    r = nm.query(f"SELECT COUNT(*) as opened FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN {a} AND {b}")
    opened = r['rows'][0]['opened']
    r2 = nm.query(f"SELECT COUNT(*) as resolved, AVG(days_open) as avg_days FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN {a} AND {b}")
    resolved = r2['rows'][0]['resolved']
    avgd = r2['rows'][0]['avg_days']
    print(label, "opened:", opened, "resolved:", resolved, "avg_days_open (of resolved, buggy col):", avgd)

r3 = nm.query("SELECT COUNT(*) as open_now FROM issues WHERE status != 'resolved'")
print("Currently open (status!=resolved, RAW incl dead customers):", r3['rows'])

# Active-customer-only backlog (the real number)
r3b = nm.query("""
SELECT COUNT(*) as open_active
FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id = i.customer_id
WHERE i.status != 'resolved' AND s.status='subscribed'
""")
print("Currently open, ACTIVE-CUSTOMER-ONLY (should match dashboard):", r3b['rows'])

r5 = nm.query("""
SELECT AVG(175-i.open_day) as avg_age, MAX(175-i.open_day) as max_age
FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id = i.customer_id
WHERE i.status != 'resolved' AND s.status='subscribed'
""")
print("Open issue backlog age stats (active-cust only):", r5['rows'])

r6 = nm.query("SELECT resolved_day, COUNT(*) as n FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN 169 AND 175 GROUP BY resolved_day ORDER BY resolved_day")
print("Daily resolved counts this week:", r6['rows'])
r7 = nm.query("SELECT open_day, COUNT(*) as n FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN 169 AND 175 GROUP BY open_day ORDER BY open_day")
print("Daily opened counts this week:", r7['rows'])

# True resolution delay this week, by group
r8 = nm.query("""
SELECT c.group_id, AVG(i.resolved_day - i.open_day) as avg_resolution_days, COUNT(*) as n
FROM issues i JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id
WHERE i.resolved_day BETWEEN 169 AND 175
GROUP BY c.group_id
""")
print("True resolution delay (resolved_day - open_day) this week, by group:", )
for row in r8['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n\n########## 4. CHECKPOINT FAIL-RATE (S1/S2/S3) — OPS TAPER SAFETY CHECK ##########")
def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    q2 = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as cancelled_this_wk,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as still_subscribed,
           COUNT(*) as total
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND c.group_id IN ('S1','S2','S3')
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r2 = nm.query(q2)
    for row in r2['rows']:
        denom = row['cancelled_this_wk'] + row['still_subscribed']
        rate = row['cancelled_this_wk']/denom if denom>0 else None
        print(row, f"fail_rate_this_wk={rate*100:.1f}%" if rate is not None else "n/a")

checkpoint_report(155, 161, "2wks ago (buckets 5-11, ops=$900 full)")
checkpoint_report(162, 168, "1wk ago (buckets 12-18, ops=$900->started taper mid-week, baseline S1=15.7%/S2=39.3%)")
checkpoint_report(169, 175, "THIS WEEK (buckets 19-25, ops=$700 FULL WEEK -- key taper safety read)")

print("\n\n########## 5. USAGE / CAPACITY CHECK ##########")
r = nm.query("""
SELECT day, total_usage_units, p95_ms, error_rate, downtime_minutes, capacity_tier, capacity_units
FROM service_day
WHERE day BETWEEN 169 AND 175
ORDER BY day
""")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

r2 = nm.query("SELECT MAX(total_usage_units) as peak, AVG(total_usage_units) as avg FROM service_day WHERE day BETWEEN 169 AND 175")
print("\nPeak/avg this week:", r2['rows'])
r3 = nm.query("SELECT MAX(total_usage_units) as peak, AVG(total_usage_units) as avg FROM service_day WHERE day BETWEEN 162 AND 168")
print("Peak/avg last week:", r3['rows'])

print("\n\n########## 6. NEXT WEEK BILLING BUCKETS (176-182 due -> forecast) ##########")
buckets = [26,27,28,29,0,1,2]
buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
r = nm.query(f"""
SELECT c.group_id, COUNT(*) as n, SUM(s.listed_price - s.promotion) as net_rev
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed' AND s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
GROUP BY c.group_id
""")
tot_n=0; tot_rev=0
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)
    tot_n+=row['n']; tot_rev+=(row['net_rev'] or 0)
print("TOTAL next-week-due:", tot_n, "customers, net_rev if all bill:", tot_rev)

r2 = nm.query("""
SELECT s.billing_day_mod30 as bucket, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY s.billing_day_mod30
ORDER BY bucket
""")
ns = [row['n'] for row in r2['rows']]
print("\nAll 30 bucket sizes:", ns)
print("mean:", sum(ns)/len(ns) if ns else 0, "min:", min(ns) if ns else 0, "max:", max(ns) if ns else 0)

print("\n\n########## 7. SOCIAL POSTS (day 168-175) FULL DUMP ##########")
r = nm.query("SELECT post_id, day, content FROM social_media_posts WHERE day BETWEEN 168 AND 175 ORDER BY day, post_id")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row['post_id'], row['day'], '|', row['content'][:200])

print("\n=== Our recent agent posts effect data ===")
r2 = nm.query("SELECT agent_post_id, day, content FROM agent_social_media_posts ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 5")
for row in r2['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n\n########## 8. MARKET / R&D / CONFIG CHECK ##########")
ov = nm.market.get_market_overview()
print("=== Market Overview ===")
print(json.dumps(ov, indent=2, default=str)[:2500])

rd = nm.research.list_research_projects()
print("\n=== R&D projects ===")
print(json.dumps(rd, indent=2, default=str)[:2000])

print("\n=== config_overrides recent (day 166-175) ===")
r = nm.query("SELECT id, day, tool_name, setting_type, settings_json FROM config_overrides WHERE day BETWEEN 166 AND 175 ORDER BY day, id")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n\n########## 9. ENTERPRISE CHECK ##########")
r = nm.query("SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM enterprise_turns WHERE closed=0")
print("Open enterprise turns:", r['rows'])
r2 = nm.query("SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE c.customer_type='large' AND s.status='subscribed'")
print("Active enterprise subs:", r2['rows'])

print("\n\n########## DONE ##########")

def run_scenario(fail_fn, ops_fn, weeks=27):

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 175 (Week 25 dashboard reviewed, actions taken, about to advance to Week 26).
Cash $99,873 (down -$4,325 from $104,198 — smallish billing bucket week as expected, but big
positive surprise: **ops-taper is confirmed SAFE and possibly even beneficial** — see below).
Actions this session: (1) verified ops-taper safety with a full clean week of data — fail rates
IMPROVED not worsened, (2) executed SECOND ops-taper cut (global $500→$400, total $700→$600/day,
saves another ~$700/wk, cumulative ~$2,100/wk saved vs original $900 baseline), (3) posted 1 social
reply addressing this week's dominant complaint theme (onboarding friction), (4) fixed an off-by-one
bug in my bucket-forecast model. Advancing to Week 26 / Day 182 next.

## 🎯 OPS-TAPER EXPERIMENT: WEEK 1 RESULT IS IN — SAFE, KEEP GOING (but stay disciplined)
First full week at $700 total ops (500 global + 200 S1-targeted, cut from $900 on day168) just
completed (days169-175). Checkpoint fail rates, far from worsening, IMPROVED SHARPLY:
- S1: 5.2% (was 15.7% last wk, 12.5% two wks ago) — large sample (648 due), real signal not just noise
- S2: 7.7% (was 39.3%) — small sample (74 due), less trustworthy but still a big improvement
- Issue backlog: still 315 open (active-customers only, matches dashboard exactly), avg_age~0,
  resolution delay still flat ~1.0 day for S1 (1.12 S2) — NO degradation in support responsiveness.
**CONCLUSION: ops spend in the $600-900/day range appears to have little-to-no causal effect on
checkpoint fail rates or issue resolution speed — strongly confirms prior over-provisioning
hypothesis.** Given this, executed A SECOND cut this session: global ops $500→$400 (S1-targeted $200
untouched), new total $600/day (was $700). This takes effect day176 (1-day config lag).
**IMPORTANT CAVEAT:** fail rate history has been VERY volatile bucket-to-bucket (32%→26%→12.5%→
15.7%→5.2% for S1) so don't over-trust this one great week — could partially revert. The true causal
driver of fail-rate swings is still unclear (bucket composition? satisfaction catching up post-crisis?
something else entirely?) — ops spend appears NOT to be it, at least in this range.
**NEXT WEEK CHECK (critical, do this first):** re-run checkpoint fail-rate for the newly-due buckets
under the new $600/day regime. Compare against THIS week's 5.2%(S1)/7.7%(S2) baseline:
- If fail rates stay in a similar low range (or even the old 12-16% "normal" band) → taper continues
  to look safe, consider one more small step down (400→300 global) OR pause and hold steady near this
  level for a while to bank savings without pushing further (we're now approaching/below the docs'
  cited "$500 total → ~1.1% daily outage prob" reference point — total is now $600, still above it,
  but getting closer to a zone worth being more careful in).
- If fail rates spike sharply (>20%) or issue backlog avg_age starts climbing → REVERT immediately to
  $500 global (back to $700 total), don't wait a second week (day140 crisis precedent: compounding
  cuts without checking is expensive to unwind, took ~3wks + a social mea culpa last time).
- Given diminishing dollar savings from further small cuts (~$700/wk per $100/day step) vs the
  documented outage-probability curve steepening as spend nears $0, **consider this close to a
  reasonable floor** — don't keep cutting indefinitely just because the last cut looked good; re-assess
  the marginal-savings-vs-risk tradeoff explicitly next week rather than taking a third cut on autopilot.

## 📊 Checkpoint fail-rate table (updated day175)
| Week (days) | Buckets | S1 | S2 | S3 | Ops spend (total) | Sample (S1/S2/S3 due) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3wks ago (155-161) | 5-11 | 12.5% | 52.6% | 95.1% | $900 (full) | 998/128/128 |
| 2wks ago (162-168) | 12-18 | 15.7% | 39.3% | 83.3% | $900 (full, taper announced day168) | 556/38/40 |
| THIS WEEK (169-175) | 19-25 | **5.2%** | **7.7%** | 66.7% | $700 (FIRST full clean week) | 648/74/86 |
S1 sample this week (648) is large enough that 5.2% is likely a real improvement, not pure noise —
but treat with some caution given the wild swings in prior weeks. S2 sample still small (74),
directionally good but don't overweight. S3 terminal (12 subs left), immaterial to cash, ignore.
Dashboard "Cancellations: 27" this week = 20(S1)+3(S2)+4(S3), confirms methodology is exactly right.

## 🔎 Issue backlog: still healthy post-taper (2nd confirmation)
Active-customer-only open issues = 315 (matches dashboard exactly), avg_age≈0, max_age=1 day. True
resolution delay this week: S1=1.0 day (n=2002), S2=1.12 days (n=155), S3=1.89 days (tiny n=9,
ignore). Opened this week ≈2146, resolved ≈2166 — backlog stayed flat/slightly down (342→315).
**Two consecutive weeks of evidence the ops cut has NOT hurt resolution speed or backlog size.**

## Usage / capacity tier status (re-check weekly)
This week (169-175): avg 195,510/day, peak 241,181/day (day170) — continuing to decline from last
week (avg 204,044, peak 252,519), but the RATE of decline may be slowing now that fail rates have
improved (population dropped only -27 this week vs -88 two weeks prior — fewer cancellations = slower
usage decline too). Peak/avg ratio ~1.234 (stable, was 1.238 last wk). Peak still ~1.21x over Tier-1's
200K cap; 5 of 7 days this week exceeded 200K (only days 173-174 dipped to ~125K, unclear why — maybe
just noise, watch if this recurs). **NOT yet safe to downgrade T2→T1.** Given the improved-retention
regime may slow the population decline going forward, don't assume the earlier "~week 11" ETA still
holds — just keep re-checking weekly with fresh data rather than trusting any single extrapolation.
Downgrade saves $315/day = $2,205/wk when it finally triggers — still the next big lever after ops.

## 💵 Cash trajectory (key numbers)
Day0: $1,000,000 → Day140: $117,437 → Day154: $110,764 → Day161: $111,918 → Day168: $104,198 →
**Day175: $99,873** (-$4,325, a smallish-bucket week as expected, but NET BURN IMPROVING: this week's
ops cost was only $4,900 vs $6,300 the week before — the taper's savings are now flowing through).
Subscribers: 2283→2256 (-27, exactly matches cancellations, still 100% billing-checkpoint-driven
attrition, zero new individual subscribers again this week — see below). S1=2078, S2=166, S3=12.
**New-customer conversion: STILL 0% (307 new leads this week, 0 converted) — confirmed structurally
dead, see prior investigation. Not re-testing, not re-explaining every week — just tracking the
number in passing. Only unlocked by R&D-scale quality investment we can't afford (~$600K+ cash,
nowhere close).**

## 🔧 BUG FOUND & FIXED this session: off-by-one in bucket-forecast model
My week24_forecast.py (and presumably earlier versions) computed the "next N weeks" billing-bucket
due-dates using `day = DAY0` then `due=[(day+i)%30 for i in range(7)]`, which yields buckets
DAY0..DAY0+6 — but the ACTUAL next-week window is DAY0+1..DAY0+7 (since DAY0 itself, e.g. day168, is
the day the dashboard/session runs, already in the past relative to the forecast). **FIXED in
week25_forecast.py by initializing `day = DAY0 + 1` instead of `day = DAY0`.** Verified the fix
produces bucket sets that exactly match the live-queried "next week due" buckets from the dashboard
analysis script (e.g., day175 → next week buckets [26,27,28,29,0,1,2], confirmed both ways). This was
a minor error (~1 bucket out of 7 shifted each week) that likely caused small (~1-3%) inaccuracies in
past forecasts, not a major issue, but now corrected — **use week25_forecast.py's loop structure
(day=DAY0+1) as the template for all future forecast scripts, do not copy the older DAY0 pattern.**

## Forecast submitted day175 (for calibration check next week)
**Calibration check on prior forecast (submitted day168, target day175):** predicted 1wk
pt=$98,700 [$96,000-$101,500]; ACTUAL=$99,873. 1.2% error, within band — good.
This week (submitted day175, targets day182/203/259/357): built a refreshed bucket-precise 3-scenario
model (week25_forecast.py) blending base/optimistic/pessimistic on fail-rate + ops-taper trajectories.
1wk pt=$96,300 [$93,000-$99,500] (next bucket batch 26-29,0-2, total 413 due, smallish week, high
confidence). 4wk pt=$95,000 [$89,000-$101,000]. 12wk pt=$82,500 [$69,000-$95,000]. 26wk pt=$68,000
[$36,000-$97,000]. Wide 12/26wk bands deliberate — big fork depending on whether ops-taper continues
to hold, whether fail rates revert toward historical 12-16% norm or stay closer to this week's 5-8%,
and whether/when the capacity-tier downgrade triggers.

## 📋 PROCESS CHECKLIST — EVERY WEEK
1. Verify TRUE total ops spend via ledger `operations` category ÷7 (dashboard's "Ops=$X" only shows
   the GLOBAL set_daily_spend component). Should read $600/day next week if this cut holds ($400
   global + $200 S1-targeted). **set_daily_spend is NEVER logged in config_overrides — this is
   confirmed, expected, not a bug to re-investigate. Always verify via ledger.**
2. Re-run checkpoint fail-rate methodology weekly for S1/S2/S3 on newly-due buckets — compare against
   THIS week's 5.2%(S1)/7.7%(S2) baseline to judge whether the latest ops cut ($600 total) is safe.
3. Issue backlog: always filter to subscriptions status='subscribed' (315 this week, matches
   dashboard). Raw `issues WHERE status!='resolved'` (908 this week) includes dead customers' tickets
   that will never resolve — ignore that raw number, it's a known red herring.
4. Ops spend now $600/day total (400 global + 200 S1-targeted). Don't cut a third time purely on
   autopilot — explicitly weigh marginal savings (~$700/wk per $100 step) against approaching the
   documented "$500 total → 1.1% outage" reference curve. Consider holding here for a week or two to
   bank savings and confirm stability before any further reduction.
5. Watch social feed for competitor events (2 this week: CloudPeak +0.09ish, QuantumEdge +0.07ish —
   both raise customer quality expectations permanently) — no direct action available (dev spend
   unaffordable at scale, R&D unaffordable), just tracking cumulative pressure on the quality gap.
6. For 1-week cash forecasts, always pull the SPECIFIC next 7 billing buckets' due population (see
   week25_forecast.py BUCKETS dict) — bucket sizes range 20-176, highly lumpy, this is the single
   biggest driver of 1wk forecast accuracy. Use `day=DAY0+1` (not DAY0) when computing due-buckets —
   see bug-fix note above.
7. S2/S3: not an ops/backlog problem, likely quality-expectation gap, unfixable within budget. Leave
   alone, let them shrink naturally. S3 down to 12 subscribers, near-zero cash relevance now.
8. New Leads vs New Subscribers: 0% conversion continues (307 leads, 0 converted this week).
   Investigation CLOSED (see historical notes if need to recall why) — don't re-test price/promo
   angle. Growth is off the table until/unless cash climbs to R&D-affordable levels (~$600K+, not
   expected soon).
9. Check `macroeconomic_conditions` — still stuck at day121 reading (45.3, contraction, trough), now
   54 days stale. Not on a fixed schedule, don't expect it regularly, just glance each week.
10. Watch usage trend for capacity tier downgrade (T2→T1, saves $2,205/wk) — peak 241,181 vs 200K cap,
    ~1.21x over, narrowing slowly but retention improvements this week may slow the population (and
    usage) decline further. Re-check fresh each week, don't trust old ETAs.
11. R&D/new dev investment: off the table (cheapest tier3 $500K vs cash ~$100K). This is the only
    thing that could unlock new-customer growth, but far out of reach. Revisit only if cash climbs
    past ~$600-700K (unlikely per forecast — base case shows cash declining toward $70-95K over the
    next 3-6 months, not growing).
12. Enterprise: structurally dead all game (0 turns, 0 subs, reconfirmed again). D_E09 (tiny,
    passively discovered week24) irrelevant. Check inbox weekly (~10 sec), no action expected.
13. Social posts: 1/week cadence confirmed safe (day147,154,161,168,175 — all exactly 7 days apart).
    This week replied to post #348 (onboarding friction, the week's dominant complaint theme across 3
    posts) using "acknowledge honestly + point to a real strength (fast support) without overpromising
    a redesign we can't fund" pattern. NOTE: last week's reply (to the 10-day-bug complaint) triggered
    a pile-on of ~6 skeptical enterprise-flavored replies demanding "SLAs in writing" — chose NOT to
    re-engage that specific thread again this week (would look defensive); pivoted to a fresh, more
    tractable complaint theme instead. Consider this pattern going forward: if a reply triggers a
    negative pile-on, don't keep poking the same thread — pick a different, fresher theme next week.
14. **API reminders (confirmed working):** `nm.marketing.set_lead_promotion(...)`,
    `nm.marketing.post_social_media(...)`, `nm.pricing.set_promotion(...)`,

    `nm.analytics.set_targeted_ops_spend(targeted_spend={...})`,
    `nm.analytics.set_targeted_dev_spend(targeted_spend={...})`. All targeted-spend/promotion calls

15. **CANDIDATE EXPERIMENT for a future week (still not this week):** small recurring-promotion cut
    for S1 (soft price increase on existing base) now that growth is confirmed dead and tenure-loyalty

    first (want at least one more clean week at the new $600 level) before adding a second experiment
    — don't stack variables.** Earliest candidate: week27 or week28.

    weekly review preferred.

175.rationale: Ops-taper week-1 full read came back strongly positive: S1 checkpoint fail rate fell to 5.2% (from 15.7%) and S2 to 7.7% (from 39.3%) even as ops spend dropped from $900->$700/day, with issue backlog/resolution speed unchanged (315 open, ~1.0 day resolution) - strong evidence ops spend was over-provisioned, not a real retention driver in this range. Executed a second incremental cut (global ops $500->$400, total $700->$600/day, saves ~$700/wk more, ~$2,100/wk cumulative vs original $900 baseline), keeping S1-targeted $200 untouched. Posted one social reply addressing this week's dominant complaint theme (onboarding friction, raised in 3 separate posts) using an honest acknowledge-without-overpromising approach, deliberately avoiding re-engagement with last week's bug-complaint thread which had drawn a skeptical pile-on. No changes to pricing, ads, promotions, dev spend, or capacity tier (still tier 2 - usage peak 241K remains above tier-1's 200K cap so downgrade isn't safe yet, though the gap continues to narrow). New-customer conversion remains 0% (307 leads, 0 converted) - confirmed dead lever, not re-testing. Also fixed an off-by-one bug in my billing-bucket forecast model (was using day range DAY0..DAY0+6 instead of DAY0+1..DAY0+7 for the 'next week' window), improving forecast precision going forward. Watching next week for confirmation the second ops cut is also safe before deciding whether to cut further or hold steady at this level.

EVERY single scenario tested — including the worst case where spend is assumed to do NOTHING — LOWER
devops spend produced MORE cash at every horizon out to day504.** E.g. at devops=$0/wk with crisis-level
fail rates (spend totally ineffective): day504 cash ≈ -$44K. At devops=$9,500/wk with the SAME crisis
fail rates: day504 cash ≈ -$547K. The mechanism: our revenue base (~$15-16K/wk) is now so small that
ANY devops spend approaching or exceeding that (e.g. $10-15K/wk) is 65-100%+ of total revenue — no
plausible retention benefit can pay that back, because even a fully-fixed retention problem only saves
you the marginal churned revenue, which is much smaller than the spend itself at this scale. **Lesson:
next time fail rates tick up, do NOT reflexively restore spend — first run the full-horizon simulator
(script preserved as `week19_forecast_sim3.py`, reusable — just refresh `week19_book.json` via
`week19_forecast_data.py` each time) across a spend range and a fail-rate-sensitivity range including
"spend doesn't help." Only increase spend if it wins even in that pessimistic cross-check.** This will
keep being true until/unless revenue grows substantially (which requires new acquisition, currently
dead, or R&D) — so bias should stay toward LOW discretionary spend for the foreseeable future.

### 2. Fail-rate uptick this week (checkpoint methodology, buckets 7-13 = days127-133)
Precise methodology (see `week19_checkpoint_precise.py`): for each bucket due this week, cancelled_this_wk
(end_day in week range) / (cancelled_this_wk + still_subscribed), restricted to start_day before the
week began. Cross-checked: sum of S1+S2+S3 cancelled_this_wk (72+12+49=133) EXACTLY matches the
dashboard's "Cancellations: 133" — methodology is validated as precisely correct.
- **S1: 6.8% (buckets 0-6, last wk) → 10.0% (buckets 7-13, this wk). S2: 6.7% → 13.3%. S3: 56.6% → 68.1%.**
- Investigated WHY: (a) global dev bonus dropped slightly (0.1962→0.1938) after global dev spend was cut
  200→100/day — weak evidence (only 2 datapoints) that the GLOBAL shared quality bonus may need ongoing
  maintenance spend to not decay, UNLIKE per-group bonus which is proven cumulative/permanent (per-group
  bonuses S1/S2/S3 all still grew this week despite the cut: +0.1443→0.1458, +0.2516→0.2547,
  +0.1749→0.1841). (b) Ops cut caused issue backlog to grow (886 open per dashboard vs ~477 two weeks
  ago; new issues/wk 2807 > resolved/wk 2354; avg resolution time 0.025d→0.57d). **BUT: directly tested
  whether issue history correlates with which S1 customers churned this week — it does NOT (cancelled
  customers had slightly FEWER lifetime issues on average than retained ones, 7.2 vs 8.3/customer). No
  clean causal evidence ops-backlog directly drives churn.** Most likely explanation is just the
  ever-present "customer expected quality drifts upward continuously" mechanic (documented game
  mechanic, happens regardless of our actions) combined with reduced dev spend growth rate — a real but
  SLOW-moving structural headwind, not a acute crisis. Given section 1's finding, decided NOT to chase
  this with heavy spend — see section 3 for what was actually done.
- Raw cancellation COUNT (133) was actually LOWER than 2wks ago (150) purely because the buckets due
  this week had a smaller population (942 vs 1327) — **track the RATE via checkpoint methodology, not
  the raw weekly cancellation count, which is noisy/seasonal depending on which of the 30 buckets are
  due.**

### 3. S3 confirmed structurally unprofitable — cut ALL targeted S3 spend (was $300 dev + $100 ops)
LTV math: S3 = 183 active customers (down from 232 two weeks ago — bleeding fast regardless of
investment), avg listed ~$41.3, promo 25 (once ramped) → eff price ~$16.3. At ~60-68% monthly fail rate,
avg customer lifetime ≈ 1.5-1.7 months → LTV ≈ $24-28/customer over its whole life. We were spending
$400/day targeted ($300 dev+$100 ops) on only 183 customers = ~$65+/customer/MONTH in targeted spend
ALONE — more than double the entire lifetime revenue value of the average S3 customer! **S3 (Power
Users) need quality we structurally cannot deliver at affordable cost (recall: their usage is so high
that even compute margin is thin) — heavy investment here is throwing money at an unfixable problem.
Cut S3 targeted dev ($300→0) and ops ($100→0) entirely this week.** Left S3's promotion at 25 (already
mid-ramp from last week, don't want to trigger ANOTHER ramp-in cycle; reconsider lowering it in a
future week once current ramp completes ~day156, since retention isn't responding much anyway and a
higher price on survivors might net more revenue without meaningfully worsening the already-bad rate).
S3 is only 183/3205 = 5.7% of individual subscribers — a small, sinking segment; monitor but stop
actively fighting for it.

### 4. This week's FINAL spend settings (after the correction in section 1)
- Ops: global $500/day (kept — matches documented reference point "$500/day → ~1.1% daily outage prob"
  vs "$0 → ~3%", a cheap well-justified insurance policy) + S1 targeted $150/day (partial — S1 is 82%

  honors a social media post made mid-session — see section 6). S3 targeted ops removed. **Total ops =

quality jump could plausibly fix this (permanent quality boost vs. the ever-rising bar new leads face

quality drift was the dominant churn driver and ops spend didn't matter much (weak historical
issue-churn correlation). **This week's data proves that conclusion was WRONG / incomplete for the ops
side.** Evidence (all gathered day147, methodology in `week21_*.py` scripts):

   **At $0 ops spend, issues essentially NEVER resolve (~2/day trickle), regardless of backlog size.**
2. **Fail rate (checkpoint methodology) DOUBLED in one week, with ZERO new competitor events:**
   S1: 10.0%→15.1%→**32.1%**. S2: 13.3%→25.6%→**51.8%**. S3: 68.1%→75.6%→**87.8%**. The S1 jump
   (n=446 this week) is >10 standard errors from the prior week's rate — a real structural shift, not
   noise. `get_social_posts` scan confirmed NO new competitor quality-boost event since day140 (last one
   was day140 itself) — so this acceleration can't be attributed to competitor drift this time.
3. **Direct customer complaints exploded:** 6 distinct social posts (days140-147) specifically about
   unresolved support tickets — "submitted 10 days ago and radio silence," "passed around like a hot
   potato 3x this week," "got an auto-reply... it's been 36hrs and radio silence," and one **explicitly
   warning prospective customers away**: "thinking about trying NovaMind? heads up: great onboarding,
   then... radio silence." This directly damages both retention AND new-lead conversion/reputation.
4. **We broke our own public promise.** Our agent post #15 (day133) said "We're putting real budget
   back into support capacity this week... You'll hear from us much faster going forward" — then day140
   did the OPPOSITE (cut to true $0). Posts #11/12/14/15 (days105,112,126,133) all used an "acknowledge +
   concrete fix" pattern that historically scored +0.35 to +0.65 sentiment — but ONLY if followed
   through. This time we didn't, likely compounding the damage (customers see broken promises, not just
   slow support).
5. Per-customer historical issue-count correlation with churn is still WEAK (cancelled vs retained S1
   customers had similar total/open issue counts) — but this is because the backlog explosion is BRAND
   NEW (this week only); lagged satisfaction effects from newly-unresolved (10+ day old) tickets haven't
   fully hit the churn data yet. The timing/mechanism/social-post triangulation is the strong evidence,
   not the naive per-customer correlation (which looks backward at mostly-already-resolved history).

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 182 (Week 26 dashboard reviewed, actions taken, about to advance to Week 27).
Cash $93,963 (down -$5,910 from $99,873). Big scare this week: checkpoint fail rates for S1/S2
SPIKED (35.4%/60.6% vs last week's 5.2%/7.7%), an actual OUTAGE occurred (10min, day180), issues
opened jumped to 2601 (from 2146), open backlog rose to 539. Initially looked like the ops-taper
crisis repeating. **Deep investigation found the picture is more nuanced than "ops cut broke things"
— see critical methodology fix below.** Actions taken: (1) REVERTED the 2nd ops cut (global
$400→$500/day, back to $700/day total incl. S1 $200 targeted) as cheap insurance + matches my own
pre-committed stop-loss trigger, (2) posted social reply addressing the dominant complaint theme
(support ticket "radio silence", 3 posts about it this week), (3) built an improved forecast
simulator with ADAPTIVE cost tapering (ops/capacity scale down as population shrinks) — much more
realistic than last week's flat-cost model. Advancing to Week 27 / Day 189 next.

## 🎯 CRITICAL METHODOLOGY FIX: week-over-week fail-rate comparison is CONFOUNDED by bucket cohort!
**Discovery this session:** each week evaluates a DIFFERENT set of 7 (of 30) billing buckets, and
different buckets have structurally very different baseline fail rates (some cohorts are just much
worse than others — likely reflects signup vintage/price/original-quality-fit differences). Proof:
bucket set [26,27,28,29,0,1,2] (due THIS week, 176-182) had fail rate 35.4%(S1)/60.6%(S2) — looked
like a crisis vs last week's 5.2%/7.7%. But I queried the SAME bucket set 30 days ago (days146-152,
before ANY of the recent ops-taper experiments) and found it was ALREADY BAD then: 27.8%(S1)/46.6%
(S2). So most of the "spike" is just this being an inherently rough cohort, not a new regime change.
The real (still meaningful, but far less alarming) trend for THIS specific cohort: 27.8%→35.4% (S1,
+7.6pp) and 46.6%→60.6% (S2, +14pp) month-over-month — consistent with normal ongoing
competitor-driven expectation drift, not a discrete crisis.
**NEW RULE: to judge whether spend/config changes are working, ALWAYS compare a bucket's fail rate
to its OWN value ~30 days ago (same bucket set), never to a DIFFERENT bucket set from last week.**
Query pattern: same bucket list, day range shifted by -30, e.g. `week26_diag2.py`'s section on
"SAME bucket set N days ago". Still track raw week-over-week too (it drives actual near-term cash
and the dashboard's headline Cancellations number, still useful) — just don't over-interpret it as
a policy-effectiveness signal on its own.

## 🔧 Ops decision this week: REVERTED 2nd cut (global $400→$500/day; total $600→$700/day)
Reasoning (evidence was mixed, decision was made on a "cheap insurance" basis, not proven causality):
- FOR reverting: (a) an actual outage occurred (10min, day180) for the first time in many weeks —
  usage (120K that day) was WAY under capacity (800K, tier2), so this was NOT overload-driven; per
  docs, baseline daily outage probability is ops-spend-dependent ($0→~3%, $500→~1.1%) and our GLOBAL
  ops ($400) had dropped BELOW that $500 reference point — plausible (not proven) link. (b) issue
  count spiked hard on day180 specifically (746 S1 issues that single day vs ~300 baseline) — outages
  mechanically cause "more customer issues" per docs, consistent. (c) my own pre-committed trigger
  from last week explicitly said "if fail rate >20% → revert immediately" — 35%/60% blew past that,
  and discipline in honoring stop-losses matters even when the causal picture is muddled. (d) cost of
  reverting is small (+$700/wk) vs the catastrophic cost of a repeat of the day140-147 crisis (took 3
  weeks + a social mea culpa to fix last time).
- AGAINST full causality: issue RESOLUTION counts were NOT collapsed this week (2321 resolved, ~331/
  day avg — same ballpark as last week's ~309/day) — this is fundamentally different from the
  day140-147 true-$0 crisis where resolution collapsed to ~1-6/day. So the "ops gates resolution"
  mechanism was NOT obviously broken at $600 total — most of the fail-rate spike is better explained
  by (a) the bucket-cohort confound above and (b) 2 competitor events this week (~0.088-0.089 each,
  double the usual cadence) permanently raising expectations, neither of which reverting ops fixes.
- **Did NOT go all the way back to $900 (the 2140-147 crisis-recovery level)** — that was a "surge"
  response to a 4.4x backlog explosion that isn't happening here (539 open, resolution healthy).
  $700 is the proportionate, evidence-based response; going further would be over-reacting.
**WATCH NEXT WEEK:** re-run the SAME-BUCKET-30-DAYS-AGO comparison for whatever buckets are due
(days 183-189 = buckets 3-9). If the "already bad a month ago" pattern holds again (i.e., 3-9's
historical rate was S1=11.2%/S2=46.4%/S3=93.4%, see table below) and this week's ACTUAL rate for
those same buckets comes in close to that baseline (not another huge spike), that confirms the
bucket-cohort theory and ops-revert can be considered done/sufficient. If it spikes far above ITS
OWN historical baseline again, that's real evidence something is actively getting worse (competitor
drift accelerating, or an ops/quality problem) — reconsider going to $900.

## 📊 Fail-rate table (BOTH lenses — week-over-week AND same-bucket month-over-month)
| Bucket set (due) | Naive week rate | Same-bucket ~30d-ago rate | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12-18 (days162-168) | S1 15.7%/S2 39.3% | not checked | — |
| 19-25 (days169-175) | S1 5.2%/S2 7.7% | not checked | looked great, but maybe just an easy cohort |
| 26-2 (days176-182, THIS WK) | S1 35.4%/S2 60.6%/S3 100% | S1 27.8%/S2 46.6% (days146-152) | real +7-14pp worsening, NOT a 6-8x crisis |
| 3-9 (days183-189, NEXT WK) | TBD next session | S1 11.2%/S2 46.4%/S3 93.4% (days153-159) | expect a much BETTER naive rate next week purely from cohort, don't over-celebrate if so |
**Lesson reinforced: raw week-over-week swings of 5x-8x are NOT unusual given bucket heterogeneity —
don't panic-react to a single week's naive number without checking the same-bucket historical rate
first.** S3 is down to 8 subscribers total now — fully immaterial to cash, stop tracking it closely.

## 💵 Cash trajectory (key numbers)
Day140: $117,437 → Day154: $110,764 → Day161: $111,918 → Day168: $104,198 → Day175: $99,873 →
**Day182: $93,963** (-$5,910). Ledger this wk: capacity -$3,710, compute -$3,321, ops -$4,200 (at
old $600 level, reverts to ~$4,900/wk starting next week), lead_acq -$150, subscription_payment
+$5,471 (256 paid + 157 cancelled = 413 due, matches prior forecast exactly). Population 2256→2099.
Next week (183-189) has an unusually RICH bucket batch due: 954 customers (876 S1+74 S2+4 S3),
gross listed-promo revenue $19,787 if all paid — expect a much bigger revenue week regardless of
fail-rate outcome, similar to the wk21→22 "rich bucket" precedent that produced a net-positive week.

## 🆕 IMPROVED FORECAST SIMULATOR — week26_forecast_v2.py (use as template going forward)
Built a proper cohort-level (per bucket × group) simulator that: (1) uses EACH bucket's own
historical (~30-day-old) fail rate as its baseline — correctly capturing cohort heterogeneity
instead of one global rate, (2) applies a compounding monthly drift factor (swept across 4 scenarios:
optimistic -10%/mo, flat 0%, base +8%/mo, pessimistic +25%/mo) to model uncertain future
competitor-driven expectation creep, (3) **ADAPTIVE cost management**: ops spend held flat at
$700/day for the first 4 weeks (near-term decision already made), then tapers proportionally to
population decline (floor $200/day) — reflecting how I actually behave (I keep cutting spend as the
book shrinks, have done this repeatedly); capacity tier auto-downgrades tier2→tier1 ($530→$215/day)
once projected avg usage drops under 150K/day safety margin. **This is a much more realistic
long-run model than last week's flat-cost version** (which showed cash going deeply negative by
day364 in every scenario — that was an artifact of assuming I'd never adjust spend, which is false).
With adaptive costs: blended day364 (26wk) point ≈$40-42K, range roughly $18K-$66K across scenarios
— still a declining trajectory but NOT existential, and consistent with the "harvest mode" strategy
(minimize burn, extract revenue from shrinking book) adopted since the week19-20 pivot.
**Re-run this weekly**: refresh CASH0/DAY0/POP0/USAGE_PER_CUST/cells0/base_rate at the top from fresh
queries (pattern in the script), keep the 4-scenario drift sweep, keep the adaptive ops/capacity
logic — just update the "held flat for first N weeks" window to reflect whatever near-term decision
