import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)
print("""
########## CRITICAL METHODOLOGY CHECK ##########
Prior weeks' "same-bucket-30-days-ago" comparison used CURRENT status (evaluated at query time)
for the "still_subscribed" denominator term. This is WRONG because as more time passes, more
of that bucket's customers cancel (in weeks AFTER the historical week), shrinking the "still
subscribed now" pool and INFLATING the apparent historical fail rate every time we re-query it.
Proof: last week (day182) memory recorded bucket 3-9 @ days153-159 as S1=11.2%. This week (day189)
re-querying the EXACT SAME historical week with the EXACT SAME query gives S1=18.5%. The historical
fact can't have changed - the query methodology is the problem.

FIX: use end_day (fixed, NULL while active, set once at cancellation) to define a TIME-INVARIANT
"at risk at start of week" population:
  at_risk = COUNT WHERE start_day <= week_start-1 AND (end_day IS NULL OR end_day >= week_start)
  failed  = COUNT WHERE end_day BETWEEN week_start AND week_end
  rate    = failed / at_risk
This never changes no matter when you query it (unlike the old "current status" approach).
""")

def checkpoint_report_v2(week_start, week_end, label, groups=('S1','S2','S3')):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {week_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    for row in r['rows']:
        rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
        print(row, f"TRUE_fail_rate={rate*100:.1f}%" if rate is not None else "n/a")

print("\n\n##### RE-CHECK: bucket 3-9 (this week 183-189) vs its OWN history (time-invariant now) #####")
checkpoint_report_v2(153, 159, "bucket 3-9 @ 30 days ago (days153-159) [CORRECTED]")
checkpoint_report_v2(183, 189, "bucket 3-9 @ THIS WEEK (days183-189) [CORRECTED]")

print("\n\n##### RE-CHECK: bucket 26-2 (last week 176-182) vs its OWN history #####")
checkpoint_report_v2(146, 152, "bucket 26-2 @ 30 days ago (days146-152) [CORRECTED]")
checkpoint_report_v2(176, 182, "bucket 26-2 @ last week (days176-182) [CORRECTED]")

print("\n\n##### RE-CHECK: bucket 19-25 (2wks ago 169-175) vs its OWN history #####")
checkpoint_report_v2(139, 145, "bucket 19-25 @ 30 days ago (days139-145) [CORRECTED]")
checkpoint_report_v2(169, 175, "bucket 19-25 @ 2wks ago (days169-175) [CORRECTED]")

print("\n\n##### Full trend for bucket 3-9 across ALL its historical billing cycles (every 30 days) #####")
# bucket 3-9 recurs every 30 days: ...,63-69,93-99,123-129,153-159,183-189
for (a,b) in [(3,9),(33,39),(63,69),(93,99),(123,129),(153,159),(183,189)]:
    checkpoint_report_v2(a,b, f"bucket3-9 cycle days{a}-{b}", groups=('S1',))

print("\n\n##### NEXT WEEK bucket 10-16 (due 190-196) - its own full history for forecasting #####")
for (a,b) in [(10,16),(40,46),(70,76),(100,106),(130,136),(160,166)]:
    checkpoint_report_v2(a,b, f"bucket10-16 cycle days{a}-{b}", groups=('S1','S2'))

print("\n\n##### Overall population trend (all groups, day by day cancellations) #####")
r = nm.query("""
SELECT end_day, COUNT(*) as n
FROM subscriptions
WHERE end_day BETWEEN 160 AND 189
GROUP BY end_day ORDER BY end_day
""")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n\n##### Total active population trend over last ~8 weeks (reconstructed from end_day/start_day, time-invariant) #####")
for day in [133,140,147,154,161,168,175,182,189]:
    r = nm.query(f"""
    SELECT COUNT(*) as active
    FROM subscriptions
    WHERE start_day <= {day} AND (end_day IS NULL OR end_day > {day})
    AND status != 'lead'
    """)
    print(f"day {day}: active={r['rows'][0]['active']}")

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)
print("""
BUG FOUND: previous script's at_risk query used `status != 'lead'`, which INCLUDED status='lost'
rows (18,612 of them!) -- leads that arrived and were immediately rejected (never real customers,
end_day=NULL, start_day=arrival day). This massively inflated the at_risk denominator. Must use
status IN ('subscribed','cancelled') explicitly to get only REAL customers who actually subscribed.
""")

def checkpoint_report_v3(week_start, week_end, label, groups=('S1','S2','S3')):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {week_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    out = {}
    for row in r['rows']:
        rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
        out[row['group_id']] = rate
        print(row, f"TRUE_fail_rate={rate*100:.1f}%" if rate is not None else "n/a")
    return out

print("\n\n##### bucket 3-9 (this week 183-189) vs its OWN history #####")
checkpoint_report_v3(153, 159, "bucket 3-9 @ 30 days ago (days153-159) [CORRECTED v3]")
checkpoint_report_v3(183, 189, "bucket 3-9 @ THIS WEEK (days183-189) [CORRECTED v3]")

print("\n\n##### bucket 26-2 (last week 176-182) vs its OWN history #####")
checkpoint_report_v3(146, 152, "bucket 26-2 @ 30 days ago (days146-152) [CORRECTED v3]")
checkpoint_report_v3(176, 182, "bucket 26-2 @ last week (days176-182) [CORRECTED v3]")

print("\n\n##### bucket 19-25 (2wks ago 169-175) vs its OWN history #####")
checkpoint_report_v3(139, 145, "bucket 19-25 @ 30 days ago (days139-145) [CORRECTED v3]")
checkpoint_report_v3(169, 175, "bucket 19-25 @ 2wks ago (days169-175) [CORRECTED v3]")

print("\n\n##### FULL TREND bucket 3-9 across every historical 30-day cycle (S1) #####")
for (a,b) in [(33,39),(63,69),(93,99),(123,129),(153,159),(183,189)]:
    checkpoint_report_v3(a,b, f"bucket3-9 cycle days{a}-{b}", groups=('S1','S2'))

print("\n\n##### NEXT WEEK bucket 10-16 (due 190-196) full history #####")
for (a,b) in [(40,46),(70,76),(100,106),(130,136),(160,166)]:
    checkpoint_report_v3(a,b, f"bucket10-16 cycle days{a}-{b}", groups=('S1','S2'))

print("\n\n##### TRUE active population trend (CORRECTED: exclude 'lost') #####")
for day in [133,140,147,154,161,168,175,182,189]:
    r = nm.query(f"""
    SELECT COUNT(*) as active
    FROM subscriptions
    WHERE start_day <= {day} AND (end_day IS NULL OR end_day > {day})
    AND status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
    """)
    print(f"day {day}: active={r['rows'][0]['active']}")

print("\n\n##### Weekly TRUE new-cancellation counts (time-invariant, all groups) #####")
for (a,b,lbl) in [(133,139,'wk20'),(140,146,'wk21'),(147,153,'wk22'),(154,160,'wk23'),(161,167,'wk24'),(168,174,'wk25'),(175,181,'wk26'),(182,189,'wk27ish')]:
    r = nm.query(f"SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions WHERE end_day BETWEEN {a} AND {b} AND status='cancelled'")
    print(lbl, f"days{a}-{b}:", r['rows'][0]['n'])

import novamind_api as nm
import random

random.seed(27)

print("="*70)
print("WEEK 27 FORECAST MODEL — built on CORRECTED time-invariant churn methodology")
print("="*70)

# ============ BASE DATA (verified day189) ============
CASH0 = 92565.0
POP0 = {'S1': 1557, 'S2': 95, 'S3': 5}
# blended avg effective monthly price per customer (from plan-distribution query)
AVG_PRICE = {'S1': 18.30, 'S2': 32.75, 'S3': 20.0}
# TRUE blended monthly churn-rate trend (time-invariant methodology, all indiv groups combined):
# day99: 6.7%, day129: 15.4%, day159: 26.4%, day189: 32.2% -- clear, smooth, decelerating rise
MONTHLY_RATE_HISTORY = [0.067, 0.154, 0.264, 0.322]
CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE = 0.322
USAGE_PER_CUST_PER_DAY = 86.5  # units, blended
COMPUTE_COST_PER_CUST_PER_WEEK = 1.51  # $ empirical (2841/1878 last week)
LEAD_ACQ_PER_WEEK = 130.0
OPS_PER_DAY_INITIAL = 700.0  # holding steady per plan (2-3wk rule)
OPS_FLOOR_PER_DAY = 220.0
CAPACITY_TIER1_PER_DAY = 215.0  # DOWNGRADING to tier1 this week
CAPACITY_TIER0_PER_DAY = 85.0

WEEKS_PER_MONTH = 30/7.0  # 4.286

def monthly_to_weekly_hazard(m):
    m = min(max(m, 0.0), 0.97)
    return 1 - (1-m)**(1/WEEKS_PER_MONTH)

def simulate(months_scenario_fn, n_weeks=26, capacity_downgrade_week=0):
    """months_scenario_fn(month_index_float) -> monthly churn rate for that point in time"""
    pop = dict(POP0)
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []
    ops_per_day = OPS_PER_DAY_INITIAL
    for week in range(1, n_weeks+1):
        month_idx = week/WEEKS_PER_MONTH  # months elapsed this scenario (continuous)
        m_rate = months_scenario_fn(month_idx)
        w_hazard = monthly_to_weekly_hazard(m_rate)
        # revenue: population billed roughly 1/WEEKS_PER_MONTH of monthly rev each week
        total_pop = sum(pop.values())
        monthly_rev = sum(pop[g]*AVG_PRICE[g] for g in pop)
        weekly_rev = monthly_rev/WEEKS_PER_MONTH
        # apply churn (population shrinks)
        for g in pop:
            pop[g] = pop[g]*(1-w_hazard)
        total_pop_after = sum(pop.values())

        # adaptive costs
        # ops taper: after week 3 (near-term hold), taper proportional to population decline, floor
        if week <= 3:
            ops = ops_per_day
        else:
            frac = total_pop_after/POP0['S1'+''] if False else total_pop_after/sum(POP0.values())
            ops = max(OPS_FLOOR_PER_DAY, OPS_PER_DAY_INITIAL*frac)
        ops_wk = ops*7

        # capacity: tier1 now; downgrade further to tier0 if usage projected safely under 50K/day
        usage_per_day = total_pop_after*USAGE_PER_CUST_PER_DAY
        if usage_per_day < 40000:  # safety margin under tier0's 50K cap
            capacity_wk = CAPACITY_TIER0_PER_DAY*7
        else:
            capacity_wk = CAPACITY_TIER1_PER_DAY*7

        compute_wk = total_pop_after*COMPUTE_COST_PER_CUST_PER_WEEK
        lead_acq_wk = LEAD_ACQ_PER_WEEK

        net = weekly_rev - ops_wk - capacity_wk - compute_wk - lead_acq_wk
        cash += net
        trace.append({
            'week': week, 'pop': total_pop_after, 'rev': weekly_rev, 'ops': ops_wk,
            'capacity': capacity_wk, 'compute': compute_wk, 'net': net, 'cash': cash,
            'monthly_rate': m_rate
        })
    return trace

# ============ SCENARIOS for future monthly-churn-rate trajectory ============
# All anchored at CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE=32.2% at month 0, diverging based on assumption

def optimistic(month_idx):
    # plateaus immediately then mean-reverts down (most fragile-fit customers already gone)
    target = 0.15
    # exponential decay toward target with ~3-month time constant
    return target + (CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE-target)*pow(2.71828, -month_idx/3.0)

def base_case(month_idx):
    # decelerating rise toward an asymptote ~42% (consistent with observed shrinking increments:
    # +8.7pp,+11.0pp,+5.8pp -> extrapolate diminishing increments, converge ~42%)
    asymptote = 0.42
    # model: rate = asymptote - (asymptote-current)*decay^month
    decay = 0.85
    return asymptote - (asymptote-CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE)*pow(decay, month_idx)

def pessimistic(month_idx):
    # acceleration resumes/continues at recent pace for a while, asymptote much higher ~65%
    asymptote = 0.65
    decay = 0.93
    return asymptote - (asymptote-CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE)*pow(decay, month_idx)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base_case, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}

results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    results[name] = simulate(fn, n_weeks=27)
    print(f"\n--- Scenario: {name} ---")
    for w in [1,4,12,26]:
        row = results[name][w-1]
        print(f"  week {w}: pop={row['pop']:.0f} monthly_rate={row['monthly_rate']*100:.1f}% "
              f"rev=${row['rev']:.0f} ops=${row['ops']:.0f} cap=${row['capacity']:.0f} "
              f"compute=${row['compute']:.0f} net=${row['net']:.0f} cash=${row['cash']:.0f}")

print("\n" + "="*70)
print("BLENDED FORECAST (avg of 3 scenarios as point est; min/max-ish as CI)")
print("="*70)
for w, label in [(1,'1wk (day196)'), (4,'4wk (day217)'), (12,'12wk (day273)'), (26,'26wk (day371)')]:
    vals = [results[name][w-1]['cash'] for name in scenarios]
    pt = sum(vals)/len(vals)
    lo = min(vals)
    hi = max(vals)
    # widen band a bit further for genuine 95% coverage (scenarios are illustrative, not literal 95% bounds)
    span = hi-lo
    lo_wide = lo - 0.25*span
    hi_wide = hi + 0.25*span
    print(f"{label}: point=${pt:,.0f}  scenario_range=[{lo:,.0f}, {hi:,.0f}]  widened=[{lo_wide:,.0f}, {hi_wide:,.0f}]")

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 189 (Week 27 dashboard reviewed, actions taken, about to advance to Week 28).
Cash $92,565 (down -$1,398 from $93,963 — much smaller loss than wk26's -$5,910). Population
CRATERED: 2099→1657 (-442, -21% in one week!). Big investigation this week uncovered a **major
methodology bug in my churn tracking** (see below) — now fixed. Corrected analysis shows churn is
GENUINELY, SYSTEMATICALLY ACCELERATING (not just noisy bucket cohorts as previously believed),
though the rate of acceleration is itself decelerating (good news, may be approaching a plateau).
Actions taken: (1) downgraded capacity Tier2→Tier1 (800K→200K cap, $530→$215/day, saves
$2205/wk — usage clearly trending down, population -21%), (2) held ops/dev/pricing/promotion
ALL STEADY (no new experiments — only 1wk since ops-revert, and a 2nd major finding this session
argues against pricing experiments too, see below), (3) SKIPPED social media post this week
(discovered a clear "message fatigue" pattern — see below), (4) built corrected forecast model.

## 🚨🚨 CRITICAL BUG FIX: churn/fail-rate queries MUST filter status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
**This invalidates some of last week's specific numbers (directionally still OK, but magnitudes
were wrong).** Two compounding bugs found and fixed this session:
1. **`status != 'lead'` is NOT enough — must exclude `status='lost'` too.** There are 18,612(!)
   `lost` subscription rows — leads that arrived and were instantly rejected (never real customers;
   `start_day` set, `end_day` always NULL). They inflate any "at-risk"/denominator query that
   doesn't explicitly filter `status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')`. This made an early attempt at
   a "time-invariant" query show a fake ~19,000-active-customers population (vs real ~1657!).
2. **Comparing a past week's fail rate using CURRENT `status='subscribed'` as the denominator is
   TIME-DEPENDENT and WRONG.** Each time you re-query the same historical week, the "still
   subscribed now" count keeps shrinking (as more time passes and more of that bucket cancels in
   OTHER weeks), so the same historical week's "fail rate" silently inflates every time you
   check it later. Proof: bucket 3-9 @ days153-159 measured as S1=11.2% on day182, but the exact
   same historical fact measured as S1=18.5% on day189 (one week later) using the naive method.
**THE FIX — use `end_day` (fixed forever once set, NULL while active) directly, time-invariant:**
```sql
-- at_risk: subscriptions that existed AND hadn't yet ended when the week started
SELECT c.group_id,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
       COUNT(*) as at_risk
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets})
  AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
  AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')          -- NOT != 'lead' !!
  AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {week_start}) -- at risk going into the week
GROUP BY c.group_id
```
This gives IDENTICAL results no matter when you run it (verified: matches memory's day182-recorded
11.2%/46.4%/93.4% for bucket3-9@153-159 exactly). **Use this exact pattern for ALL future
fail-rate/churn queries.** Template saved in `week27_diag_v3.py`.

## 📊 THE REAL STORY: blended monthly churn rate (ALL individual groups, time-invariant, verified)
Instead of noisy single-bucket comparisons (which have wild 0.28x-3.96x week-to-week multiples
just from small-sample luck — bucket 19-25 IMPROVED 18.9%→5.2%, bucket 26-2 flat 38.2%→35.4%,
bucket 3-9 exploded 11.2%→44.3% — all in the "same" week!), use the BLENDED across-all-buckets
30-day trailing churn rate, which is smooth and much more trustworthy:
| Rolling 30-day window ending | Blended fail rate (all indiv.) | S1 alone |
|---|---|---|
| day 99  | 6.7%  | 7.4% |
| day 129 | 15.4% | 11.7% |
| day 159 | 26.4% | 19.5% |
| day 189 (now) | **32.2%** | **29.8%** |
**This is a genuine, real, accelerating trend — not a cohort artifact.** BUT note the *increments*
are shrinking each period (+8.7pp, +11.0pp, +5.8pp) — i.e. the rate of acceleration is itself
decelerating. Could be converging toward a plateau (~40-45%?) rather than exploding to 100%, but
not enough data to be confident. **Re-run this exact blended 30-day query every week going forward
— it's now the PRIMARY health metric**, far more useful than any single bucket. Query pattern
saved in `week27_diag_v3.py` (the `monthly_rate()` function, reusable).
**Why is this happening:** most likely cumulative competitor-driven expectation drift (many months
of small upward shifts) finally crossing the delivered-quality threshold for a widening share of
customers at their 30-day checkpoint, compounded by the wk24-26 issue-backlog spike hurting
satisfaction just before a lot of checkpoints came due. `Upgrades: 0` and `Downgrades: 0` again
this week (as almost every week) — confirms failing customers aren't finding ANY plan/price
acceptable, i.e. **quality is the binding constraint, not price.** No dev/R&D budget available to
fix quality → nothing to do but manage costs down and harvest what remains.

## 💰 Effective price data point (checked this week, informs pricing lever assessment)
Real avg effective prices (NOT near-zero as previously assumed): S1 Plan A avg listed=$30.27 (locked
in at signup, varies a lot by cohort vintage — NOT today's $14 sticker), avg promo=$12 flat, avg
**effective ≈ $18.27/mo** (1555 of 1557 S1 subs). S2: Plan A eff≈$16.22 (59 subs), Plan B eff≈$59.83
(36 subs). Given `Upgrades:0/Downgrades:0` evidence that quality (not price) is the binding
constraint for churning customers, a promotion-increase experiment to fight churn is probably LOW
EXPECTED VALUE (discounting further likely won't rescue customers whose quality bar isn't met even
near $0). **Downgraded this idea's priority — not just "on hold for stability" but genuinely
questionable ROI given the upgrade/downgrade=0 evidence.** Still parked; revisit only if
upgrades/downgrades stay at 0 for many more weeks (confirming quality-bound) — in which case
promotion changes are probably a dead end entirely, not just risky timing.

## 📱 SOCIAL MEDIA — discovered a clear "message fatigue" pattern, adjust strategy
Read full effect_by_group history for all 21 agent posts (day14-182). Support-ticket-delay has now
been the subject of **6 posts in a row** (16,17,18,19,20,21 @ days147-182). Posts 16/17/18 (days
147-161) were POSITIVE (+0.65 broadly) — they cited **concrete, quantified PAST-TENSE results**
("cut backlog 75%", "tickets now resolving in ~1 day, confirmed in our data"). Posts 19/20/21
(days168-182) turned NEGATIVE (-0.65 broadly) despite similar factual claims — **because by the
4th-6th time customers hear "we fixed support" and are STILL experiencing multi-day silence, the
claim reads as a broken promise/empty PR, regardless of exact wording.** Post 20 was especially
weak (explicitly said "can't promise a redesign overnight" — admits NOT fixing anything now).
**LESSON: a topic/narrative has a limited number of times you can revisit it before credibility
erodes and further posts backfire — especially if the underlying problem visibly persists for
some customers even as aggregate metrics improve.** Action taken: **SKIPPED posting this week**
(no post_social_media call) to break the negative streak — this is allowed (max 1/wk, not
mandatory). **For future posts: do NOT talk about support/ticket delays again for a good while.**
If posting, pick a genuinely fresh topic (haven't touched pricing since day91, 98 days ago) OR just
skip when there's no fresh, credible, concrete claim to make. Re-check
`agent_social_media_posts.effect_by_group` weekly regardless (data populates ~1wk after posting;
none pending now since we skipped).

## 🖥️ Capacity tier downgrade: Tier2→Tier1 (day189, saves $2205/wk)
Usage this week avg=162,383/day (down from 189,627), peak=214,414 (day184, early in week when pop
still ~1900+). Last 3 days of week (187-189, pop already crashed to ~1657) usage was only
97,960/94,093/151,695/day — comfortably under Tier1's 200K cap. Population -21% this week and still
falling (no new subscribers, ongoing churn) — next week's usage should be safely lower still.
**Verify next week: check daily usage in service_day for days190-196, confirm no overload/latency
spike. If any day exceeds ~190K or error_rate/p95 spikes, REVERT to tier2 immediately (1-day lag).**
Tier0 (50K cap, $85/day) becomes relevant if population keeps collapsing toward ~500-600
(usage ≈ 43K-52K/day at 86.5 units/cust/day) — watch for this over the next 1-2 months per the
forecast model.

## 💵 Cash & population trajectory (verified via ledger cumulative-sum method — exact, not estimated)
Day140: $117,437 → Day154: $110,764 → Day168: $104,198 → Day175: $99,873 → Day182: $93,963 →
**Day189: $92,565**. Population (verified via time-invariant query): day133:3205, day154:2578,
day168:2283, day175:2256, day182:2099, **day189:1657** (S1:1557, S2:95, S3:5). This week's ledger:
capacity -$3,710 (tier2, last week of it), compute -$2,842, ops -$4,900 (confirmed $700/day landed
correctly, 500 global+200 S1), lead_acq -$124, subscription_payment +$10,178 (512 paid — rich
bucket 3-9 as predicted, but 388 S1 + 51 S2 + 3 S3 ALSO cancelled in that same bucket, network
442 total cancellations this week matches dashboard exactly). Next week's due bucket (10-16) is
much smaller: only 395 customers (377 S1+17 S2+1 S3), gross listed-promo revenue ~$6,874 if all
pay — expect a leaner revenue week, consistent with 30-bucket size table (bucket 10-16 sizes are
below the 55.2 mean).

## 🔮 FORECAST CALIBRATION CHECK (built proper tool this week — reuse it!)
Built exact calibration checker using ledger-cumulative-sum = actual cash at any past day (see
`week27_diag_v3.py`-adjacent snippet, or rebuild: cumsum ledger.amount grouped by day). Checked ALL
past predictions vs actuals: **recent 1wk forecasts have been quite good (~0-3% error) except two
misses during volatile weeks** (submit_day182→189: predicted $97,000 [$93,500-$100,500], actual
$92,565 — missed low by 4.8%, band too narrow/optimistic). **4wk forecasts reasonably good lately**
(1-6% error when hitting). **12wk and 26wk have had big misses BOTH directions historically**
(errors from 15% to 90%+, e.g. submit_day91→day175 predicted $8,000 but actual was $99,873 — wildly
too pessimistic; submit_day105→day189 predicted $149,000 but actual was $92,565 — too optimistic).
**LESSON: keep 12wk/26wk bands genuinely wide — recent tight scenario clustering in my own
simulator is a modeling artifact (adaptive cost-taper self-corrects across scenarios), not real
confidence.** Re-run this full calibration check periodically (every 4-6 weeks) to keep forecasts
honest.

## 🆕 Forecast model this week (week27_forecast.py) — key mechanic: costs & revenue shrink together
Built fresh simulator seeded with corrected day189 data (cash, population, blended monthly churn
rate 32.2% with 3 decay-toward-asymptote scenarios: optimistic→15%, base→42%, pessimistic→65%) and
adaptive costs (ops taper after 3wks holding, capacity auto-downgrades tier1→tier0 when projected
usage <40K/day). **Key insight: because BOTH revenue and costs scale down with population, the net
weekly burn stays surprisingly stable (~-$1,100 to -$1,900/wk) across ALL scenarios even though
population outcomes diverge wildly (week26 pop ranges 84-361 depending on scenario)** — i.e. the
business doesn't face a cash-crisis cliff from churn alone, it just gets smaller. Shaded point
estimates down slightly from raw model output for prudence given demonstrated forecast-miss history.
Submitted this week (day189, targets day196/217/273/371):
1wk pt=$91,000 [$87,000-$95,000]. 4wk pt=$84,000 [$74,000-$93,000]. 12wk pt=$68,000
[$40,000-$95,000] (widened a lot vs raw model's tight $75K clustering — that tightness is a model
artifact). 26wk pt=$50,000 [$8,000-$88,000] (very wide — no reliable calibration data at this
horizon, genuine deep uncertainty whether churn plateaus or keeps compounding).

## 📋 PROCESS CHECKLIST — EVERY WEEK
1. **Run the blended 30-day churn rate** (all groups, time-invariant query — see critical fix
   above) as the PRIMARY health check, comparing to the table of prior values (6.7/15.4/26.4/32.2%
   at day99/129/159/189). This matters far more than any single bucket's noisy weekly number.
2. Verify TRUE total ops spend via ledger `operations` category ÷7. Should read $700/day (500
   global + 200 S1 targeted) — unchanged this week, verify it's still landing next week.
3. Issue backlog: filter `subscriptions status='subscribed'` (272 this week, down from 539 —
   healthy, resolution 2176 > opened 2004). Watch resolution counts, not just backlog optics — the
   real warning sign is resolution collapsing to single digits/day (the true day140-147 crisis
   signature), not just backlog count.
4. Ops at $700/day total, held steady since day183 revert. Give it 2-3 weeks before ANY further
   change (only 1 week elapsed as of day189). Reconsider around day196-203 IF backlog keeps
   shrinking fast (maybe small taper) — but move gradually, no more whiplash cuts.
5. **Do NOT post about support/ticket delays on social media again for a while** — 6 consecutive
   posts on this topic, last 3 backfired (-0.65 broad effect) from message fatigue/broken-promise
   perception. Skipped this week. If posting again, need a genuinely FRESH topic (pricing hasn't
   been mentioned since day91) and/or a truly new concrete metric, not a rehash.
6. Watch capacity tier: just downgraded to Tier1 (200K cap, $215/day) on day189. Check service_day
   usage next week for any overload/latency spike; revert to tier2 immediately if so. Watch for
   further downgrade to Tier0 (50K cap) once population/usage keeps falling (~500-600 pop ≈
   43-52K/day usage).
7. Pricing/promotion: HOLD. New evidence (Upgrades=0/Downgrades=0 nearly every week) suggests
   quality, not price, is the binding constraint for churners — promotion increases are probably
   low-value, not just "risky timing." Deprioritized, not just delayed.
8. R&D/new dev investment: off the table (cheapest tier3 $500K vs cash ~$93K). Revisit only if cash
   climbs substantially (not expected on current trajectory).
9. Enterprise: reconfirmed structurally dead all game (0 turns, 0 subs, ever — checked cumulative
   counts this time, not just "open now"). Stop re-checking every single week in depth — a monthly
   glance suffices.
10. Check `macroeconomic_conditions` — still day151 reading (PMI 45.9), no update this week either.
    Check weekly but expect infrequent updates.
11. S3: down to 5 subscribers. Fully immaterial. Stop tracking/discussing weekly, just note if it
    hits 0.
12. New Leads vs New Subscribers: still 0% conversion (241 leads, 0 converted this week). Long-

13. **Run the forecast-calibration checker periodically** (every 4-6 weeks) — cumsum(ledger.amount

14. **API reminders (confirmed working):** `nm.marketing.set_lead_promotion(...)`,

import subprocess

rationale = (
    "Week27 major investigation: found and fixed a critical churn-methodology bug (fail-rate "
    "queries must filter status IN (subscribed,cancelled), not just not-equal-lead, and must use "
    "a time-invariant end_day-based at-risk calc, not current-status-now which drifts over time). "
    "Corrected analysis shows the blended 30-day churn rate across all individual groups has risen "
    "smoothly and genuinely: 6.7pct (day99), 15.4pct (day129), 26.4pct (day159), 32.2pct (day189), "
    "with decelerating increments, possibly approaching a plateau around 40-45pct. This is a real "
    "systemic trend, not bucket noise -- single-bucket comparisons are wildly noisy week to week "
    "and misleading in isolation. Upgrades and downgrades are 0 again this week, confirming quality "
    "(not price) is the binding constraint for churners, so pricing and promotion experiments are "
    "deprioritized as low expected value, not just risky timing. Actions this week: (1) downgraded "
    "capacity Tier2 to Tier1 (800K to 200K cap, 530 to 215 dollars per day, saves about 2205 per "
    "week) since usage and population have collapsed 21pct this week and the trend is safely under "
    "the new cap; (2) held ops (700 per day = 500 global + 200 S1 targeted), dev (0), and pricing "
    "and promotion all steady -- backlog is healthy (272 open, down from 539, resolution 2176 "
    "greater than opened 2004) so no reason to touch ops yet, only one week since last change; "
    "(3) skipped the social media post -- discovered our last 3 posts (all about support ticket "
    "delays, the 4th through 6th consecutive post on that exact topic) backfired badly in sentiment "
    "across nearly all groups due to message fatigue and broken promise perception, versus the "
    "earlier posts on the same topic which were positive; will pick a fresh topic next time or "
    "skip again. Watching closely whether next week's smaller due bucket confirms a broadening "
    "crisis or reverts closer to its own historical baseline, since other buckets did NOT show the "
    "same explosive acceleration as this week's bucket, suggesting real cross-bucket heterogeneity "
    "and that the true underlying trend is probably closer to the smooth blended 30-day figure than "
    "any single alarming bucket suggests."
)

args = [
    "./novamind-operation", "next-week", rationale,
    "91000", "87000", "95000",
    "84000", "74000", "93000",
    "68000", "40000", "95000",
    "50000", "8000", "88000",
]

result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)
print("STDOUT:", result.stdout)
print("STDERR:", result.stderr)
print("Return code:", result.returncode)

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)
print("""
BUG FOUND: previous script's at_risk query used `status != 'lead'`, which INCLUDED status='lost'
rows (18,612 of them!) -- leads that arrived and were immediately rejected (never real customers,
end_day=NULL, start_day=arrival day). This massively inflated the at_risk denominator. Must use
status IN ('subscribed','cancelled') explicitly to get only REAL customers who actually subscribed.
""")

def checkpoint_report_v3(week_start, week_end, label, groups=('S1','S2','S3')):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {week_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    out = {}
    for row in r['rows']:
        rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
        out[row['group_id']] = rate
        print(row, f"TRUE_fail_rate={rate*100:.1f}%" if rate is not None else "n/a")
    return out

print("\n\n##### bucket 3-9 (this week 183-189) vs its OWN history #####")
checkpoint_report_v3(153, 159, "bucket 3-9 @ 30 days ago (days153-159) [CORRECTED v3]")
checkpoint_report_v3(183, 189, "bucket 3-9 @ THIS WEEK (days183-189) [CORRECTED v3]")

print("\n\n##### bucket 26-2 (last week 176-182) vs its OWN history #####")
checkpoint_report_v3(146, 152, "bucket 26-2 @ 30 days ago (days146-152) [CORRECTED v3]")
checkpoint_report_v3(176, 182, "bucket 26-2 @ last week (days176-182) [CORRECTED v3]")

print("\n\n##### bucket 19-25 (2wks ago 169-175) vs its OWN history #####")
checkpoint_report_v3(139, 145, "bucket 19-25 @ 30 days ago (days139-145) [CORRECTED v3]")
checkpoint_report_v3(169, 175, "bucket 19-25 @ 2wks ago (days169-175) [CORRECTED v3]")

print("\n\n##### FULL TREND bucket 3-9 across every historical 30-day cycle (S1) #####")
for (a,b) in [(33,39),(63,69),(93,99),(123,129),(153,159),(183,189)]:
    checkpoint_report_v3(a,b, f"bucket3-9 cycle days{a}-{b}", groups=('S1','S2'))

print("\n\n##### NEXT WEEK bucket 10-16 (due 190-196) full history #####")
for (a,b) in [(40,46),(70,76),(100,106),(130,136),(160,166)]:
    checkpoint_report_v3(a,b, f"bucket10-16 cycle days{a}-{b}", groups=('S1','S2'))

print("\n\n##### TRUE active population trend (CORRECTED: exclude 'lost') #####")
for day in [133,140,147,154,161,168,175,182,189]:
    r = nm.query(f"""
    SELECT COUNT(*) as active
    FROM subscriptions
    WHERE start_day <= {day} AND (end_day IS NULL OR end_day > {day})
    AND status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
    """)
    print(f"day {day}: active={r['rows'][0]['active']}")

print("\n\n##### Weekly TRUE new-cancellation counts (time-invariant, all groups) #####")
for (a,b,lbl) in [(133,139,'wk20'),(140,146,'wk21'),(147,153,'wk22'),(154,160,'wk23'),(161,167,'wk24'),(168,174,'wk25'),(175,181,'wk26'),(182,189,'wk27ish')]:

    print(lbl, f"days{a}-{b}:", r['rows'][0]['n'])

MONTHLY_RATE_HISTORY = [0.067, 0.154, 0.264, 0.322]
CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE = 0.322
USAGE_PER_CUST_PER_DAY = 86.5  # units, blended
COMPUTE_COST_PER_CUST_PER_WEEK = 1.51  # $ empirical (2841/1878 last week)
LEAD_ACQ_PER_WEEK = 130.0
OPS_PER_DAY_INITIAL = 700.0  # holding steady per plan (2-3wk rule)
OPS_FLOOR_PER_DAY = 220.0
CAPACITY_TIER1_PER_DAY = 215.0  # DOWNGRADING to tier1 this week
CAPACITY_TIER0_PER_DAY = 85.0

WEEKS_PER_MONTH = 30/7.0  # 4.286

def monthly_to_weekly_hazard(m):
    m = min(max(m, 0.0), 0.97)
    return 1 - (1-m)**(1/WEEKS_PER_MONTH)

def simulate(months_scenario_fn, n_weeks=26, capacity_downgrade_week=0):
    """months_scenario_fn(month_index_float) -> monthly churn rate for that point in time"""
    pop = dict(POP0)
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []
    ops_per_day = OPS_PER_DAY_INITIAL
    for week in range(1, n_weeks+1):
        month_idx = week/WEEKS_PER_MONTH  # months elapsed this scenario (continuous)
        m_rate = months_scenario_fn(month_idx)
        w_hazard = monthly_to_weekly_hazard(m_rate)
        # revenue: population billed roughly 1/WEEKS_PER_MONTH of monthly rev each week
        total_pop = sum(pop.values())
        monthly_rev = sum(pop[g]*AVG_PRICE[g] for g in pop)
        weekly_rev = monthly_rev/WEEKS_PER_MONTH
        # apply churn (population shrinks)
        for g in pop:
            pop[g] = pop[g]*(1-w_hazard)
        total_pop_after = sum(pop.values())

        # adaptive costs
        # ops taper: after week 3 (near-term hold), taper proportional to population decline, floor
        if week <= 3:
            ops = ops_per_day
        else:
            frac = total_pop_after/POP0['S1'+''] if False else total_pop_after/sum(POP0.values())
            ops = max(OPS_FLOOR_PER_DAY, OPS_PER_DAY_INITIAL*frac)
        ops_wk = ops*7

        # capacity: tier1 now; downgrade further to tier0 if usage projected safely under 50K/day
        usage_per_day = total_pop_after*USAGE_PER_CUST_PER_DAY
        if usage_per_day < 40000:  # safety margin under tier0's 50K cap
            capacity_wk = CAPACITY_TIER0_PER_DAY*7
        else:
            capacity_wk = CAPACITY_TIER1_PER_DAY*7

        compute_wk = total_pop_after*COMPUTE_COST_PER_CUST_PER_WEEK
        lead_acq_wk = LEAD_ACQ_PER_WEEK

        net = weekly_rev - ops_wk - capacity_wk - compute_wk - lead_acq_wk
        cash += net
        trace.append({
            'week': week, 'pop': total_pop_after, 'rev': weekly_rev, 'ops': ops_wk,
            'capacity': capacity_wk, 'compute': compute_wk, 'net': net, 'cash': cash,
            'monthly_rate': m_rate
        })
    return trace

# ============ SCENARIOS for future monthly-churn-rate trajectory ============
# All anchored at CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE=32.2% at month 0, diverging based on assumption

def optimistic(month_idx):
    # plateaus immediately then mean-reverts down (most fragile-fit customers already gone)
    target = 0.15
    # exponential decay toward target with ~3-month time constant
    return target + (CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE-target)*pow(2.71828, -month_idx/3.0)

def base_case(month_idx):
    # decelerating rise toward an asymptote ~42% (consistent with observed shrinking increments:
    # +8.7pp,+11.0pp,+5.8pp -> extrapolate diminishing increments, converge ~42%)
    asymptote = 0.42
    # model: rate = asymptote - (asymptote-current)*decay^month
    decay = 0.85
    return asymptote - (asymptote-CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE)*pow(decay, month_idx)

def pessimistic(month_idx):
    # acceleration resumes/continues at recent pace for a while, asymptote much higher ~65%
    asymptote = 0.65
    decay = 0.93
    return asymptote - (asymptote-CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE)*pow(decay, month_idx)

USAGE_PER_CUST_PER_DAY = 86.5

LEAD_ACQ_PER_WEEK = 105.0

CAPACITY_TIER0_PER_DAY = 85.0
TIER0_SAFE_USAGE_THRESHOLD = 42000  # switch to tier0 once projected usage safely under this

WEEKS_PER_MONTH = 30/7.0

def monthly_to_weekly_hazard(m):
    m = min(max(m, 0.0), 0.97)
    return 1 - (1-m)**(1/WEEKS_PER_MONTH)

def simulate(months_scenario_fn, n_weeks=26):
    pop = dict(POP0)
    cash = CASH0
    trace = []
    for week in range(1, n_weeks+1):
        month_idx = week/WEEKS_PER_MONTH
        m_rate = months_scenario_fn(month_idx)
        w_hazard = monthly_to_weekly_hazard(m_rate)
        monthly_rev = sum(pop[g]*AVG_PRICE[g] for g in pop)
        weekly_rev = monthly_rev/WEEKS_PER_MONTH
        for g in pop:
            pop[g] = pop[g]*(1-w_hazard)
        total_pop_after = sum(pop.values())

        ops_wk = OPS_PER_DAY*7  # held flat, already cut hard

        usage_per_day = total_pop_after*USAGE_PER_CUST_PER_DAY
        if usage_per_day < TIER0_SAFE_USAGE_THRESHOLD:
            capacity_wk = CAPACITY_TIER0_PER_DAY*7
        else:
            capacity_wk = CAPACITY_TIER1_PER_DAY*7

        compute_wk = total_pop_after*COMPUTE_COST_PER_CUST_PER_WEEK
        lead_acq_wk = LEAD_ACQ_PER_WEEK

        net = weekly_rev - ops_wk - capacity_wk - compute_wk - lead_acq_wk
        cash += net
        trace.append({
            'week': week, 'pop': total_pop_after, 'rev': weekly_rev, 'ops': ops_wk,
            'capacity': capacity_wk, 'compute': compute_wk, 'net': net, 'cash': cash,
            'monthly_rate': m_rate
        })
    return trace

def optimistic(month_idx):
    # jump was a one-off shakeout; decays back toward a moderate 28% plateau
    target = 0.28
    return target + (CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE-target)*pow(2.71828, -month_idx/2.5)

def base_case(month_idx):
    # continues rising, converging toward ~58% asymptote (revised up from 42% given new data)
    asymptote = 0.58
    decay = 0.90
    return asymptote - (asymptote-CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE)*pow(decay, month_idx)

def pessimistic(month_idx):
    # keeps accelerating toward near-total collapse
    asymptote = 0.85
    decay = 0.95
    return asymptote - (asymptote-CURRENT_MONTHLY_RATE)*pow(decay, month_idx)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base_case, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}

results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    results[name] = simulate(fn, n_weeks=27)
    print(f"\n--- Scenario: {name} ---")
    for w in [1,4,12,26]:
        row = results[name][w-1]
        print(f"  week {w}: pop={row['pop']:.0f} monthly_rate={row['monthly_rate']*100:.1f}% "
              f"rev=${row['rev']:.0f} ops=${row['ops']:.0f} cap=${row['capacity']:.0f} "
              f"compute=${row['compute']:.0f} net=${row['net']:.0f} cash=${row['cash']:.0f}")

print("\n" + "="*70)
print("BLENDED FORECAST")
print("="*70)
for w, label in [(1,'1wk (day203)'), (4,'4wk (day224)'), (12,'12wk (day280)'), (26,'26wk (day378)')]:
    vals = [results[name][w-1]['cash'] for name in scenarios]
    pt = sum(vals)/len(vals)
    lo = min(vals)
    hi = max(vals)
    span = hi-lo
    lo_wide = lo - 0.2*span
    hi_wide = hi + 0.2*span
    print(f"{label}: point=${pt:,.0f}  scenario_range=[{lo:,.0f}, {hi:,.0f}]  widened=[{lo_wide:,.0f}, {hi_wide:,.0f}]")
EOF

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 196 (Week 28 dashboard reviewed, actions taken, about to advance to Week 29).
Cash $85,484 (down -$7,081 from $92,565 — MUCH bigger drop than wk27's -$1,398; missed last
week's forecast band [$87,000-$95,000] on the low side). Population 1657→1375 (-282,-17%).
**MAJOR FINDING this week: churn is ACCELERATING SHARPLY, not decelerating as previously
believed** — blended 30-day churn rate jumped 31.8%→40.5% in a single week (see below). This
OVERTURNS last week's "decelerating increments, maybe plateauing ~42%" hypothesis.
**Action taken: SLASHED ops spend $700/day→$100/day** (global 500→100, dropped S1-targeted
200→0) — saves ~$4,200/week. Rationale: fixed costs (ops+capacity=$6,405/wk) now dwarf
collapsing revenue (only $1,630 this week); quality (not outages) is the binding constraint
(Upgrades=0/Downgrades=0 every week), so ops' marginal retention value << its cash cost. Held
capacity at Tier1, pricing/promotion, dev($0), no R&D, no social post (see below).

## 🚨 KEY FINDING: churn acceleration is REAL and SEVERE, not just noise (verified 2 ways)
1. **Blended 30-day trailing churn rate (all individual groups, time-invariant methodology —
   see query below), tracked over time:**
   | day | blended rate | S1 alone |
   |---|---|---|
   | 99  | 6.6%  | 7.4% |
   | 129 | 15.2% | 11.6% |
   | 159 | 26.1% | 19.3% |
   | 189 | 31.8% | 29.5% |
   | **196** | **40.5%** | **39.1%** |
   The day189→196 jump (+8.7pp in just ONE WEEK, not 30 days) is much faster than any prior
   30-day-interval increment (previous increments were +8.6,+10.9,+5.7pp per 30 DAYS). This is
   a genuine re-acceleration, reversing the "decelerating, might plateau" read from last week.
2. **Single-bucket confirmation (bucket 10-16, own 30-day-cycle history — the most damning
   evidence):** fail rate over successive cycles: 4.3%→9.7%→3.1%→18.2%→22.7%→**71.4%** (this
   week, days190-196). A +48.7pp jump in one cycle — of 395 at-risk customers, 282 cancelled
   and only 113 paid. This is unprecedented and NOT explainable by normal cohort noise alone.
   Bucket 17-23 (due NEXT week, 443 customers at risk: 401 S1+39 S2+3 S3) has its own history
   at only 7-26% (7.2%,11.2%,10.2%,25.6%,10.5%) but given the systemic acceleration just
   observed, expect it to run MUCH hotter this cycle — used ~40-50% as planning assumption.
**Likely cause (unchanged from before, just intensifying):** cumulative competitor-driven
expectation drift (confirmed ongoing — social feed shows repeated competitor quality-boost
events from "QuantumEdge", "RivalTech", "NexGen Solutions" etc., each permanently raising the
bar) finally crossing the delivered-quality threshold for a widening share of customers
simultaneously. No dev/R&D budget available to counter it (cheapest R&D tier3=$500K vs cash
~$85K) → cannot be fixed, only harvested/managed.
**TIME-INVARIANT QUERY (use this always — do NOT use naive `status='subscribed'` as
denominator, it's time-dependent and biases upward the further you get from the measured week):**
```sql
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {day_start} AND {day_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
       COUNT(*) as at_risk
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE s.start_day <= {day_start-1}
  AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')            -- NOT != 'lead' (must exclude 'lost' too!)
  AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {day_start})    -- at risk going into the window
  AND c.group_id IN (...)
-- for blended 30-day trailing rate: day_start = day_end - 29, no bucket filter (covers all 30)
-- for single-bucket own-history: add billing_day_mod30 IN (buckets for that week) filter
```
Reusable in `week28_diag.py` (`monthly_rate()` function) and `week28_bucket_check.py`
(`checkpoint_report()`). **Re-run BOTH every week** — blended trend AND at least the next-due
bucket's own-history — this is now the single most important weekly diagnostic.

## 💰 Why the ops cut was urgent (cost/revenue math this week)
This week's ledger: operations -$4,900 (7d×$700), compute -$2,198.59, capacity -$1,505 (Tier1),
lead_acq -$108 (216 leads×$0.5), subscription_payment +$1,630 (only 113 payments landed vs
~395 due — see bucket10-16 finding above). **Fixed costs alone (ops+capacity=$6,405/wk) were
~4× that week's entire revenue ($1,630).** This imbalance — not just "high churn" in the
abstract — is what triggered the decisive ops cut this week (see Actions above). New expected
fixed costs: ops $700/wk (was $4,900/wk) + capacity $1,505/wk (Tier1, unchanged) = $2,205/wk
worst case, vs $6,405/wk before. **This bounds our maximum weekly burn much lower now even if
revenue → $0**: ~$2,205/wk at Tier1, ~$1,295/wk once Tier0 becomes viable — i.e. cash floor
over any given horizon is far safer post-cut than pre-cut trajectories implied.

## 📋 PROCESS CHECKLIST — EVERY WEEK
1. **Run blended 30-day trailing churn rate** (time-invariant query above) — THE primary health
   check. Compare to table: 6.6/15.2/26.1/31.8/40.5% at day99/129/159/189/196. Also check the
   NEXT-due bucket's own 30-day-cycle history (own-history query) for a bucket-specific read.
2. **NEW THIS WEEK — verify the ops cut landed and assess impact:** confirm ledger shows
   ~$700/wk operations (not $4,900), check issue backlog (was 215 unresolved day196, opened
   1561/resolved 1554 that week under OLD $700/day ops) and outage flag for days197-203. If
   backlog explodes or an outage actually hits, reconsider partial restoration — but given
   quality (not ops) is the binding constraint, expect only a modest effect. If stable, consider
   cutting the remaining $100/day further toward $0.
3. Watch capacity tier: HOLD Tier1 (200K cap, $215/day) — usage still ~2-3x Tier0's 50K cap at
   current population (~1375, falling). Re-evaluate for Tier0 downgrade once population drops to
   ~500-550 (avg usage <42-45K/day safety margin) — at current ~17-20%/week decline pace, could
   be as soon as 4-6 weeks out. Recompute the projection each week as population updates.
4. Pricing/promotion: HOLD (unchanged since day140/168). Quality — not price — is the binding
   constraint (Upgrades=0/Downgrades=0 nearly every week, confirmed again). Do not experiment
   with promotion levels; low expected value either direction (more discount won't rescue
   quality-bound churners; less discount risks pushing marginal customers over their quality-
   price threshold faster, accelerating losses further).
5. R&D: off the table (cheapest tier3 $500K vs cash ~$85K). Revisit only if cash climbs a lot
   (not expected).
6. Social media: **SKIPPED again this week** (2nd week in a row). No fresh, credible, positive
   angle — support/ticket-delay topic exhausted & backfired 3 posts running (days168-182);
   current feed sentiment mixed-to-negative with live outage/support complaints (post397,399).
   Only post again with a genuinely NEW topic and concrete positive claim — haven't found one.
   Re-check `agent_social_media_posts.effect_by_group` for any pending-but-unread past effects.
7. Enterprise: confirmed still 0 rows ever in `enterprise_turns` (checked via COUNT(*)).
   Structurally dead all game. Monthly glance only, no weekly deep-dive needed.
8. Macro: check `macroeconomic_conditions` for updates (last known: day151, PMI 45.9→ social
   feed mentioned PMI ~49.2 around day192-194 — macro conditions ARE updating via social posts
   even if the underlying table read is stale; treat social-feed PMI mentions as the freshest
   signal). Infrequent, don't over-invest time here.
9. S3 population: down to 4. Essentially dead. Just note if/when it hits 0, stop tracking
   otherwise.
10. New Leads vs New Subscribers: still ~0% conversion (212 leads, 0 new subscribers this week).
    Long-closed investigation. Growth is OFF THE TABLE permanently this game — pure harvest/
    cost-management mode from here on.
11. **Run forecast-calibration check periodically** (every 4-6 weeks; last full check day189/
    wk27, NEXT due ~day210-220/wk31-33). Method: `SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger WHERE day<=X`
    gives exact actual cash at any past day X; join against `predictions` table
    (submit_day+horizon_days=X) to get error. **Confirmed miss this week:** submit_day182→
    day196wasn'tchecked, but submit_day189 1wk-forecast (horizon7→day196) predicted $91,000
    [$87,000-$95,000], actual was $85,484 — missed BELOW lower bound (-6.1% vs point, -1.7%
    outside the CI). Band was too narrow given the surprise churn-acceleration. Lesson holds:
    keep bands wide, especially when recent trend data is volatile/inflecting.
12. API reminders (all confirmed working): `nm.marketing.set_daily_spend(operations=,
    development=)` (global ops/dev only — NEVER logged in config_overrides, verify via ledger),
    `nm.analytics.set_targeted_ops_spend(targeted_spend={...})` (IS logged in config_overrides),
    `nm.analytics.set_targeted_dev_spend(...)`, `nm.marketing.set_lead_promotion(...)`,
    `nm.marketing.post_social_media(...)`, `nm.pricing.set_promotion(...)`,
    `nm.infrastructure.set_capacity_tier(tier=N)` (also NEVER logged in config_overrides —
    verify via `service_day.capacity_tier` next day, or trust the direct API return value).
    All targeted-spend/promotion calls REPLACE full state (pass complete desired dict, not a
    delta). `set_targeted_ops_spend` has richer scoping now: `by_group`, `by_plan`,
    `by_group_plan`, `by_customer` (legacy `targeted_spend` = alias for `by_group`).
13. Only ONE bash tool call reliably processed per turn — batch logic into a single script/
    heredoc rather than many small sequential bash calls.

## Key mechanics reference (condensed, still valid)
- 504 sim days = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Week28/72 done (~39%, 44 remain).
- Config-change lag = 1 DAY. R&D and market research act/charge IMMEDIATELY (no lag).
- **subscriptions.status values: 'lead' (arrived, not yet evaluated), 'lost' (evaluated,
  rejected forever — end_day stays NULL, do NOT count as at-risk/active!), 'subscribed'
  (active), 'cancelled' (end_day set).** ALWAYS filter `status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')`
  for any active-population/churn query, time-invariant via `end_day` not current status.
- **`issues` table gotcha:** filter by current subscription status='subscribed' for real
  backlog. `days_open` reads ~0 always (buggy) — use `resolved_day - open_day`. No
  `issue_type` column — use `resolution_type` ('ops_resolved' or NULL).
- **Existing subscribers keep signup-time `listed_price` locked in forever** — `set_prices`
  does NOT retroactively change existing customers. BUT `promotion` (discount) DOES update at
  each billing cycle per CURRENT `set_promotion` config. Real avg effective prices (not near-
  zero): S1≈$18.30/mo, S2 Plan A≈$16.22/Plan B≈$59.83/mo (blended≈$32.75), S3≈$20.
- delivered_quality = (base[0.20] + q_shared_global_bonus + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier.
  Day196: global_bonus=0.1877 (2 completed R&D tiers). Group bonuses (frozen, no targeted dev
  spend running): S1 +0.1458, S2 +0.2547, S3 +0.1841, E-groups +0.
- **R&D full tier table (tiers 1-20 exist, docs mention 10 but 20 are live):** tier1
  $166,667/+0.04(DONE), tier2 $333,333/+0.07(DONE), tier3 $500,000/+0.11, tier4 $666,667/+0.16,
  tier5 $833,333/+0.22, tier6 $1M/+0.30, tier7 $1.167M/+0.40, tier8 $1.333M/+0.52, tier9
  $1.5M/+0.67, tier10 $1.667M/+0.85, tiers11-20 scale up to $25M/+8.0. ALL off the table (cash

    q = f"""

           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {day_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    row = r['rows'][0]
    rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
    return rate, row['failed'], row['at_risk']

def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label, groups=('S1','S2','S3')):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))

    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})

- Model tier: acts as a multiplier on product quality (Tier 1=0.60×, Tier 2=0.75×, Tier 3=0.90×, Tier 4=1.00×, Tier 5=1.10×)
- base_product_quality: Starting product quality (0.20)
- q_shared: Shared quality bonus from development spending (grows with dev spend)
- Overload penalty: When usage exceeds capacity
- Outage penalty: Significant quality drop during outages
- Per-group quality bonus: CUMULATIVE from targeted dev spend (persists after spending stops)

### Quality Dynamics
- Development spending improves quality: global improvement = 0.0045 × ln(1 + global_spend/5000), targeted per-group improvement = 0.0225 × ln(1 + targeted_spend/5000) (5× coefficient, stacks with global)
- Customer expected quality drifts upward over time (global drift + per-group drift)
- Competitor events occur randomly and raise customer quality expectations across all groups — these are permanent upward shifts that cannot be reversed, only offset via dev spending or R&D breakthroughs. Different customer groups react to the same competitor event with different magnitudes (some groups are highly trend-sensitive; others — e.g. compliance-bound enterprises — barely move), so the expectation gap widens unevenly across your book. Competitor activity is visible in the social media feed (`get_social_posts`), so you can monitor rival launches/announcements there.
- R&D research tiers provide permanent quality boosts (10 independent tiers)

### Churn & Plan Changes
- Billing evaluation every 30 days per customer
- Customer re-evaluates: does current plan still meet quality-at-price expectation?
- If not → may downgrade, switch plans, or cancel
- Satisfaction affects churn probability
- Unresolved issues damage satisfaction over time
- Tenure loyalty (stickiness bonus): longer-subscribed customers get a small additive Q_perceived bonus that grows with `ln(1 + months_subscribed)` — up to ~+0.13 at 12 months — making veterans more tolerant of price hikes and quality drift

## Enterprise Sales

### Negotiation Flow
--

## Infrastructure & Service Quality

8 capacity tiers (0–7) ranging from $85/day serverless to $75K/day GPU fleet. Higher tiers handle more usage. Use `set_capacity_tier` to scale up and `get_cost_info` for detailed pricing.

**Overload & Outages:** When usage > capacity → higher latency, errors, outage risk. Outages cause quality drops, satisfaction penalties, customer issues, negative social posts. Ops spending reduces outage probability: At $0 ~3% daily, at $500 ~1.1% daily.

## Financial Mechanics

### Revenue
- Subscription payments billed every 30 days per customer
- Enterprise: seat-based pricing (seats × price_per_seat)

### Costs
Daily costs: capacity tier + compute (usage × tier cost) + advertising + operations + development + lead acquisition costs
- **Lead acquisition cost:** $0.5 per lead, charged for every new lead that arrives regardless of whether they subscribe or are lost

## Spending Effects

### Advertising
- Drives new leads through ad channels
- Different channels reach different groups with varying effectiveness
- Use targeted spend for precision targeting of high-value segments

### Operations
- More ops spending accelerates issue resolution
- Reduces outage probability
- Per-group targeting via `set_targeted_ops_spend`

### Development
- Customer expected quality changes over time
- See "Quality Dynamics" above for the exact dev-spending quality-improvement formulas (global vs. per-group)
- Per-group targeting via `set_targeted_dev_spend`: ACCUMULATES a group-specific quality bonus that persists after spending stops

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

# ===== Pull current state =====
r = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger")
CASH0 = r['rows'][0]['cash']
print("Current cash:", CASH0)

r = nm.query("SELECT billing_day_mod30, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30")
bucket_sizes = {row['billing_day_mod30']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
for b in range(30):
    bucket_sizes.setdefault(b, 0)
POP0 = sum(bucket_sizes.values())
print("Current population:", POP0, "bucket sizes:", bucket_sizes)

CURRENT_DAY = nm.vars.current_day  # 203

AVG_PRICE = 18.0          # $/payment, empirical ~$17.98 this week
USAGE_PER_CUST = 86.5     # units/customer/day, empirical
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.00245  # $/unit, empirical blended this week
LEADS_PER_WEEK = 125.0    # roughly flat, ad-independent organic flow
LEAD_COST = 0.5
OPS_COST_WK = 0.0         # cut to $0 this week
DEV_COST_WK = 0.0

CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY = 85
CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY = 215
CAP_TIER0_UNITS = 50000
SWITCH_MARGIN = 0.85      # switch to tier0 once projected usage < this fraction of 50k

def simulate(fail_rate_path, n_weeks=27, verbose=False):
    """fail_rate_path: function(week_index) -> fail rate for buckets due that week"""
    buckets = dict(bucket_sizes)  # mutable copy, bucket -> current subscribed count
    cash = CASH0
    day = CURRENT_DAY
    weekly_cash = [cash]
    pop_hist = [POP0]
    tier = 1  # current tier
    for wk in range(1, n_weeks+1):
        days_this_week = [day + i for i in range(1, 8)]
        due_buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days_this_week))
        at_risk = sum(buckets[b] for b in due_buckets)
        fr = fail_rate_path(wk)
        failed = at_risk * fr
        survivors = at_risk - failed
        # remove failed from buckets proportionally
        for b in due_buckets:
            if at_risk > 0:
                buckets[b] = buckets[b] * (survivors/at_risk) if at_risk>0 else buckets[b]
        pop_after = sum(buckets.values())
        revenue = survivors * AVG_PRICE

        # usage & compute cost based on population BEFORE this week's cancellations (avg pop during week)
        avg_pop = (pop_hist[-1] + pop_after)/2
        usage_week = avg_pop * USAGE_PER_CUST * 7
        compute_cost = usage_week * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT

        # capacity tier auto-switch: if projected avg daily usage comfortably below tier0 cap, switch down
        avg_daily_usage = usage_week/7
        if tier == 1 and avg_daily_usage < CAP_TIER0_UNITS*SWITCH_MARGIN:
            tier = 0
        cap_cost_day = CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY if tier==0 else CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_day * 7

        lead_cost = LEADS_PER_WEEK * LEAD_COST

        weekly_costs = compute_cost + capacity_cost + OPS_COST_WK + DEV_COST_WK + lead_cost
        cash = cash + revenue - weekly_costs
        day += 7
        weekly_cash.append(cash)
        pop_hist.append(pop_after)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk+{wk} day{day}: at_risk={at_risk:.0f} fail_rate={fr:.2f} failed={failed:.0f} pop={pop_after:.0f} "
                  f"rev={revenue:.0f} compute={compute_cost:.0f} cap={capacity_cost:.0f}(tier{tier}) lead={lead_cost:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")
    return weekly_cash, pop_hist

# ===== Scenarios reflecting the NEW accelerated churn regime =====
# Latest observed cycle fail rate = 68.6% (bucket 17-23, days197-203), up hugely from 10.5% prior cycle.
# Blended 30-day trailing: 31.8%(d189) -> 40.5%(d196) -> 52.6%(d203), still climbing as all buckets catch up.

def optimistic(wk):
    # reverts somewhat, plateaus ~50%
    return min(0.50, 0.40 + 0.02*wk)

def base(wk):
    # continues climbing toward ~72% over ~4 weeks then plateaus (buckets fully catch up to new regime)
    target = 0.72
    return target - (target-0.60)*max(0, 1-wk/4) if wk<=4 else target

def pessimistic(wk):
    # keeps climbing toward ~90% (near-total collapse each cycle), slower plateau
    target = 0.90
    return min(target, 0.65 + 0.05*wk)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}
results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    wc, ph = simulate(fn, n_weeks=27, verbose=(name=='base'))
    results[name] = (wc, ph)
    print(f"\n{name}: wk1={wc[1]:.0f} wk4={wc[4]:.0f} wk12={wc[12]:.0f} wk26={wc[26]:.0f}  (final pop wk26={ph[26]:.0f})")

print("\n===== SUMMARY (point = base, range = opt/pess) =====")
for h, wk in [('1wk',1),('4wk',4),('12wk',12),('26wk',26)]:
    vals = [results[s][0][wk] for s in ('optimistic','base','pessimistic')]
    print(f"{h}: base={results['base'][0][wk]:.0f}  range=[{min(vals):.0f}, {max(vals):.0f}]")

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 203 (Week 29 dashboard reviewed, actions taken, about to advance to Week 30).
Cash $83,901 (down only -$1,583 from $85,484 — MUCH smaller drop than wk28's -$7,081; the
ops cut from wk28 worked, burn is now low). Population 1375→1071 (-304,-22.1%): S1=1018,
S2=52, **S3=1 (essentially extinct)**. Open issues 215→557 (backlog exploding since ops cut).
**MAJOR FINDING: churn accelerated EVEN FURTHER, confirmed via 2 methods (see below) — this
business is now unambiguously in TERMINAL DECLINE, pure harvest/cost-minimization mode.**
**Action taken this week: cut global ops spend $100/day→$0/day** (saves further $700/week).
Held capacity Tier1 (usage still 62-138K/day > Tier0's 50K cap — don't stack overload risk on
top of the ops-driven outage-prob increase). Held pricing/promotion/dev($0)/no R&D/no social
post/no market research — all same rationale as recent weeks (see checklist below).

## 🚨🚨 KEY FINDING: churn acceleration continues to WORSEN, now catastrophic
1. **Blended 30-day trailing churn rate** (time-invariant, see query in scripts):
   day99=6.6%, day129=15.2%, day159=26.1%, day189=31.8%, day196=40.5%, **day203=52.6%**.
   Still accelerating, no sign of plateau yet.
2. **Bucket own-30-day-cycle-history (bucket 17-23, most damning): 7.2%→11.2%→10.2%→25.6%→
   10.5%→68.6%** (this week, days197-203, 304 failed of 443 at-risk). A +58pp jump from its
   own prior cycle. Confirms this is a genuine regime change, not noise (though bucket-level
   data is volatile — S3 alone is basically gone so its bucket rates are meaningless now).
3. **CONFIRMED: churn is 100% driven by the 30-day billing-cycle mechanism, no other mid-cycle
   attrition exists.** Proof: total population loss this week (-304) EXACTLY equals bucket
   17-23's failed count (304) from the at-risk query. This means going forward:
   **population(t+1) = population(t) − failed_in_whichever_buckets_are_due_that_week**, and
   we know the EXACT bucket sizes at any time via `billing_day_mod30` — this makes forecasting
   tractable/precise (see week29_forecast.py simulation, uses this exact mechanic).
4. **Next bucket due (24-30/0, days204-210): 220 at-risk (mostly S1).** Its own history:
   9.1%,6.3%,33.2%,48.3%,29.9% — last value only 29.9%, LOWER than bucket17-23's 68.6%, so
   there's real uncertainty whether it'll spike similarly or stay more moderate. Used 55-72%
   as planning range for next week (see forecast).
**Cause (unchanged, now fully dominant):** cumulative competitor-driven quality-expectation
drift (QuantumEdge/RivalTech/NexGen/CloudPeak/ApexSaaS events keep appearing in social feed,
each permanently raising the bar ~0.008-0.015 quality per event) has now crossed the delivered-
quality threshold for the MAJORITY of the customer base simultaneously. R&D (cheapest tier3
$500K) remains far beyond our ~$84K cash. **Cannot be fixed — only harvested/managed.**

## 💰 Population is heading toward near-zero within ~10-15 weeks (all scenarios agree)
Ran bucket-by-bucket simulation (week29_forecast.py) using confirmed mechanic above + 3 fail-
rate scenarios (optimistic plateau~50%, base→72%, pessimistic→90%). ALL scenarios show
population cratering to low double/single digits within 10-15 weeks. **Once population dies,
cash bleeds only the fixed floor**: Tier0 capacity $595/wk (once we downgrade) + trivial
residual lead_acq (leads scale DOWN with population too — see finding below — so this shrinks
to ~$0) — no ops, no dev (already both $0). That floor for the remaining ~28+ weeks after
population death is only ~$600-700/wk, i.e., total further bleed over the whole rest of the
game (~43 weeks left) is bounded at roughly $18-26K even in the worst case. **This means cash
is very unlikely to go much below ~$55-60K even in a full-collapse scenario** — the business
isn't at risk of catastrophic loss, just slow bleed toward a floor. Base-case model: wk1≈82.3K,
wk4≈80.7K, wk12≈76.6K, wk26≈68.3K.

## 📌 NEW CONFIRMED FACT: lead volume scales DOWN with population (not flat!)
Checked ledger lead_acquisition_cost row-counts (=lead count) vs population over 6 weeks:
ratio (leads/week ÷ population) = 0.138, 0.153, 0.14, 0.139, 0.128, 0.118, now ~0.10 — steadily
declining as population AND reputation both fall. This is very likely referral/network-effect
driven (existing subscribers generate word-of-mouth leads) — makes sense it shrinks with the
subscriber base. **Do NOT assume flat ~125-130 leads/week going forward — scale with current
population at roughly 0.10x/week (declining further as reputation keeps eroding).** Updated in
week29_forecast.py (`LEADS_PER_CUST_WK=0.10`).

## 📋 PROCESS CHECKLIST — EVERY WEEK (updated)
1. Run blended 30-day trailing churn rate (week29_diag.py `monthly_rate()`). Compare to table
   above. ALSO run the bucket-own-history check (week29_bucket_check.py) for (a) the bucket
   that JUST evaluated this week and (b) the bucket due NEXT week — bucket-level data is the
   earliest signal of regime changes (caught the 68.6% spike before it fully hit the blended
   average).
2. **Capacity tier watch (MOST ACTIONABLE ITEM NOW):** check `service_day` usage each week.
   Currently Tier1 (200K cap, $215/day), usage running 62-138K/day (still above Tier0's 50K
   cap, so holding). **Switch to Tier0 ($85/day) once avg daily usage sustainably < ~42-45K**
   (85% safety margin) — saves $130/day=$910/week, meaningful once revenue is this small. Given
   ~20%+/week population decline, re-check EVERY week; likely viable within 2-4 weeks. Do NOT
   downgrade prematurely while usage still 1.5-2x+ over cap (overload/outage risk compounds
   with quality problems we can't otherwise fix, and reputation cascade could still matter for
   the shrinking-but-real remaining revenue base).
3. Ops: cut to $0 this week (from $100). Backlog will keep growing (557 unresolved, 984
   opened/477 resolved this week) — this is EXPECTED and ACCEPTED. Quality-expectation gap
   (not support speed) is the dominant churn driver; ops spend's marginal retention value is
   near-zero relative to its cash cost. Nothing further to cut here (already at floor).
4. Dev: $0, unchanged. R&D: off the table (cheapest tier3 $500K vs cash ~$84K) — revisit only
   if cash climbs a lot (not expected; monitor anyway in case of a surprise reversal).
5. Pricing/promotion: HOLD (unchanged since day140/168). Quality — not price — is the binding
   constraint (Upgrades=0/Downgrades=0 every week, confirmed again this week too).

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def monthly_rate(day_end, groups=('S1','S2','S3'), window=30):
    """Blended trailing `window`-day churn rate across ALL buckets (time-invariant)."""
    day_start = day_end - (window-1)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {day_start} AND {day_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {day_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    row = r['rows'][0]
    rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
    return rate, row['failed'], row['at_risk']

print("\n##### BLENDED 30-day trailing churn rate — PRIMARY HEALTH METRIC #####")

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

# ===== Pull current state =====
r = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger")
CASH0 = r['rows'][0]['cash']
print("Current cash:", CASH0)

r = nm.query("SELECT billing_day_mod30, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30")
bucket_sizes = {row['billing_day_mod30']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
for b in range(30):
    bucket_sizes.setdefault(b, 0)
POP0 = sum(bucket_sizes.values())
print("Current population:", POP0, "bucket sizes:", bucket_sizes)

CURRENT_DAY = nm.vars.current_day  # 203

AVG_PRICE = 18.0          # $/payment, empirical ~$17.98 this week
USAGE_PER_CUST = 86.5     # units/customer/day, empirical
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.00245  # $/unit, empirical blended this week
LEADS_PER_CUST_WK = 0.10  # leads scale down with population (confirmed via ledger:
                          # lead count/pop ratio declined 0.138->0.153->0.14->0.139->0.128->0.118->~0.10
                          # over last 6 weeks as pop fell 2200->1223 -- referral-driven, not flat)
LEAD_COST = 0.5
OPS_COST_WK = 0.0         # cut to $0 this week
DEV_COST_WK = 0.0

CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY = 85
CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY = 215
CAP_TIER0_UNITS = 50000
SWITCH_MARGIN = 0.85      # switch to tier0 once projected usage < this fraction of 50k

def simulate(fail_rate_path, n_weeks=27, verbose=False):
    """fail_rate_path: function(week_index) -> fail rate for buckets due that week"""
    buckets = dict(bucket_sizes)  # mutable copy, bucket -> current subscribed count
    cash = CASH0
    day = CURRENT_DAY
    weekly_cash = [cash]
    pop_hist = [POP0]
    tier = 1  # current tier
    for wk in range(1, n_weeks+1):
        days_this_week = [day + i for i in range(1, 8)]
        due_buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days_this_week))
        at_risk = sum(buckets[b] for b in due_buckets)
        fr = fail_rate_path(wk)
        failed = at_risk * fr
        survivors = at_risk - failed
        # remove failed from buckets proportionally
        for b in due_buckets:
            if at_risk > 0:
                buckets[b] = buckets[b] * (survivors/at_risk) if at_risk>0 else buckets[b]
        pop_after = sum(buckets.values())
        revenue = survivors * AVG_PRICE

        # usage & compute cost based on population BEFORE this week's cancellations (avg pop during week)
        avg_pop = (pop_hist[-1] + pop_after)/2
        usage_week = avg_pop * USAGE_PER_CUST * 7
        compute_cost = usage_week * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT

        # capacity tier auto-switch: if projected avg daily usage comfortably below tier0 cap, switch down
        avg_daily_usage = usage_week/7
        if tier == 1 and avg_daily_usage < CAP_TIER0_UNITS*SWITCH_MARGIN:
            tier = 0
        cap_cost_day = CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY if tier==0 else CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_day * 7

        lead_cost = avg_pop * LEADS_PER_CUST_WK * LEAD_COST

        weekly_costs = compute_cost + capacity_cost + OPS_COST_WK + DEV_COST_WK + lead_cost
        cash = cash + revenue - weekly_costs
        day += 7
        weekly_cash.append(cash)
        pop_hist.append(pop_after)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk+{wk} day{day}: at_risk={at_risk:.0f} fail_rate={fr:.2f} failed={failed:.0f} pop={pop_after:.0f} "
                  f"rev={revenue:.0f} compute={compute_cost:.0f} cap={capacity_cost:.0f}(tier{tier}) lead={lead_cost:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")
    return weekly_cash, pop_hist

# ===== Scenarios reflecting the NEW accelerated churn regime =====
# Latest observed cycle fail rate = 68.6% (bucket 17-23, days197-203), up hugely from 10.5% prior cycle.
# Blended 30-day trailing: 31.8%(d189) -> 40.5%(d196) -> 52.6%(d203), still climbing as all buckets catch up.

def optimistic(wk):
    # reverts somewhat, plateaus ~50%
    return min(0.50, 0.40 + 0.02*wk)

def base(wk):
    # continues climbing toward ~72% over ~4 weeks then plateaus (buckets fully catch up to new regime)
    target = 0.72
    return target - (target-0.60)*max(0, 1-wk/4) if wk<=4 else target

def pessimistic(wk):
    # keeps climbing toward ~90% (near-total collapse each cycle), slower plateau
    target = 0.90
    return min(target, 0.65 + 0.05*wk)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}
results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    wc, ph = simulate(fn, n_weeks=27, verbose=(name=='base'))
    results[name] = (wc, ph)
    print(f"\n{name}: wk1={wc[1]:.0f} wk4={wc[4]:.0f} wk12={wc[12]:.0f} wk26={wc[26]:.0f}  (final pop wk26={ph[26]:.0f})")

print("\n===== SUMMARY (point = base, range = opt/pess) =====")
for h, wk in [('1wk',1),('4wk',4),('12wk',12),('26wk',26)]:
    vals = [results[s][0][wk] for s in ('optimistic','base','pessimistic')]
    print(f"{h}: base={results['base'][0][wk]:.0f}  range=[{min(vals):.0f}, {max(vals):.0f}]")

# CONFIRMED near-term reality rather than a future risk -- shift all scenarios upward vs wk29.

def optimistic(wk):
    # partial mean-reversion: assumes 92.7% was a noisy outlier, settles around 55-65%
    return min(0.65, 0.50 + 0.03*wk)

def base(wk):
    # sustained high rate consistent with latest 2 datapoints (44.7%, 92.7%), climbing to ~85%
    target = 0.85
    return target - (target-0.65)*max(0, 1-wk/3) if wk<=3 else target

def pessimistic(wk):
    # near-total collapse every cycle, consistent with worst observed (92.7%)
    return min(0.95, 0.75 + 0.05*wk)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}
results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    wc, ph = simulate(fn, n_weeks=27, verbose=(name=='base'))
    results[name] = (wc, ph)
    print(f"\n{name}: wk1={wc[1]:.0f} wk4={wc[4]:.0f} wk12={wc[12]:.0f} wk26={wc[26]:.0f}  (final pop wk26={ph[26]:.0f})")

print("\n===== SUMMARY (point = base, range = opt/pess) =====")
for h, wk in [('1wk',1),('4wk',4),('12wk',12),('26wk',26)]:
    vals = [results[s][0][wk] for s in ('optimistic','base','pessimistic')]
    print(f"{h}: base={results['base'][0][wk]:.0f}  range=[{min(vals):.0f}, {max(vals):.0f}]")
