# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 210 (Week 30 dashboard reviewed, actions taken, about to advance to Week 31).
Cash $81,237 (down -$2,663 from $83,901 — burn increased vs wk29's -$1,583 drop, despite ops
already at $0 both weeks; driven by terminal-decline mechanics/revenue collapse, not spending
changes). Population 1071→867 (-204,-19.0%): S1=824, S2=42, **S3=1 (unchanged, still
essentially extinct)**. Open issues 557→717 (backlog still growing but opened-count way down:
355 opened vs 984 last week, consistent with shrinking population generating fewer new issues).
**MAJOR NEW FINDING: bucket-level churn hit a NEW EXTREME — 92.7% fail rate for the bucket
that just cycled (204 of 220 at-risk churned, S1 alone 194/208=93.3%). Highest single-cycle
fail rate observed all game, up from 29.9% just ONE cycle (30 days) earlier for the SAME
bucket-group.** No settings changes made this week (pure hold, nothing new to cut — ops/dev
already at $0 floor). Capacity held at Tier1; model predicts safe to downgrade to Tier0 NEXT
week (day224/wk32) — re-verify before switching.

## 🚨🚨 KEY FINDING: bucket-level churn now hitting NEAR-TOTAL-COLLAPSE levels
1. **Blended 30-day trailing churn rate**: day159=26.1%, day189=31.8%, day196=40.5%,
   day203=52.6%, **day210=60.0%**. Still climbing but INCREMENT shrinking (+12.1pp then
   +7.4pp) — math artifact of approaching a high plateau (can't exceed 100%), NOT a sign of
   recovery.
2. **Bucket-own-30-day-cycle-history, bucket24-0 (just evaluated, days204-210): 9.1%→6.3%→
   33.2%→48.3%→29.9%→92.7%**. Near-total wipeout of that cohort. This bucket-group (buckets
   24-29/0) is now almost entirely gone (1-5 subscribers left each, ~16 total).
3. **Bucket1-7 (due NEXT week, days211-217) own-history: 6.8%→4.0%→12.6%→21.6%→44.7%** (last
   obs, roughly DOUBLING each cycle recently — if that continues, next value could be 70-90%+).
   This is the LARGEST remaining cohort (490 at-risk = 56% of total remaining population 867)
   — next week is the single biggest churn event remaining in the game. Watch closely.
4. **Population(t+1) = population(t) − failed_in_due_buckets mechanic CONFIRMED AGAIN**
   (204 total loss = 204 bucket24-0 failures exactly, 5th consecutive week matching exactly).
   Fully deterministic once fail-rate is known; only the fail-rate itself is uncertain now.
**Cause (unchanged):** cumulative competitor-driven quality-expectation drift has crossed the
delivered-quality threshold for the vast majority of remaining customers. Confirmed via social
feed: constant stream of competitor micro-update posts (QuantumEdge/RivalTech/NexGen/CloudPeak/
ApexSaaS, each +0.01-0.02 quality, permanent) plus ongoing "support radio silence" complaints
(structural now — ops spend at $0, backlog 717, won't be resolved). **Nothing to be done — R&D
(cheapest tier3 $500K) still ~6x unaffordable vs $81K cash. Pure harvest continues.**

## 💰 Updated cash forecast model (week30_forecast.py, refreshed data + scenarios)
Bucket-by-bucket simulation using confirmed mechanic + 3 fail-rate scenarios reflecting the NEW
higher-churn regime (optimistic plateau~55-65%, base→85%, pessimistic→95%). Population now
modeled to hit ~0 within 10-14 weeks (base case), slightly FASTER than wk29's model (was
10-15wk) — consistent with observed acceleration. **Cash floor mechanics unchanged: once
population dies, only fixed cost floor remains** = Tier0 capacity $595/wk (auto-switch modeled
once avg daily usage < 42.5K, projected day224/wk32) + near-zero residual lead-acquisition
(scales with population → ~$0). Base-case model: wk1≈$81.5K, wk4≈$79.5K, wk12≈$74.8K,
wk26≈$66.5K. Scenario spread narrows at 26wk ($65.2K-$70.3K) because by then ALL scenarios have
long since crossed into "population≈0, pure floor cost" territory — exact fail-rate path
mostly affects HOW FAST we get there, not the ultimate cash level. **Confirms: cash unlikely to
fall much below ~$58-65K even in worst case — slow bleed to a floor, not catastrophic risk.**
This week's submitted forecast (widened beyond pure model range for safety margin): 1wk point
$81,450 [$79,000-$84,500]; 4wk point $79,500 [$75,500-$83,500]; 12wk point $75,000
[$69,000-$81,000]; 26wk point $67,000 [$60,000-$75,000].

## 📋 PROCESS CHECKLIST — EVERY WEEK (unchanged from wk29, still valid)
1. Run blended 30-day trailing churn rate + bucket-own-history check (both just-evaluated AND
   next-due buckets) — use week30_diag.py / week30_bucket_check.py as templates, bump day
   ranges by +7 (blended rate) or +30 per bucket-history-entry (bucket cycles) each week.
2. **Capacity tier watch:** Tier1 usage this week averaged ~82.3K/day (576,365/7), still above
   Tier0's 50K cap most days (only day208-209 dipped below; day210 popped back to 80.6K —
   volatile day-to-day). Model predicts safe switch NEXT week (day224/wk32) once population
   drops to ~516 and avg daily usage falls under ~42.5K. **Re-verify with fresh data before
   switching — a downgrade-triggered overload/outage right as the largest remaining cohort
   (490, bucket1-7) hits its billing decision this week would be a bad trade for saving
   ~$910/wk.**
3. Ops/Dev: $0/$0, unchanged, at floor. R&D: still unaffordable (cheapest tier3 $500K vs cash
   ~$81K) — revisit only if cash climbs a lot (not expected).
4. Pricing/promotion: HOLD (unchanged since day140/168). Upgrades=0/Downgrades=0 again this
   week — quality (not price) remains the binding constraint.
5. Social media: SKIPPED again (4th week running). Feed still 100% support complaints +
   routine competitor micro-update posts. No genuine positive angle; past posts about support
   backfire (-0.65 typical effect in most groups). Don't force a post without a real angle.
6. Enterprise: still confirmed 0 rows ever in `enterprise_turns`, 0 active enterprise subs.
   Structurally dead all game.
7. Market research: still not worth $25K (>30% of current cash) — skip permanently unless cash
   grows substantially.
8. S3 population: still 1 (essentially extinct) — unchanged from last week.
9. New Leads vs New Subscribers: 131 leads, 0 new subscribers this week — still 0% conversion,
   confirmed AGAIN. Growth permanently off the table.
10. **Forecast-calibration check** — last full check day189, NEXT due ~day224-230 (do it in
    the next 1-3 weeks: pull `predictions` table joined with actual ledger cumsum cash at the
    target day).
11. Only ONE bash tool call reliably processed per turn — batch logic into a single
    script/heredoc rather than many small sequential bash calls.

## Key mechanics reference (condensed, unchanged from wk29 — all still verified working)
- 504 sim days = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Week30/72 done (~42%, 42 remain).
- Config-change lag = 1 DAY. R&D and market research act/charge IMMEDIATELY (no lag).
- subscriptions.status values: 'lead','lost','subscribed','cancelled'. Filter
  `status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')` for active-population/churn queries.
- churn = 100% driven by 30-day billing-cycle evaluation (confirmed 5 weeks running, exact
  match each time). `population(t+1) = population(t) − failed_in_due_buckets_that_week`.
- lead volume scales with population but NOISILY — don't assume clean monotonic decline. This
  week's ratio (134 leads / 1071 start-pop = 0.125) actually ticked UP from last week's ~0.10.
  Use ~0.13 as working estimate, revisit weekly.
- `issues` table: filter by subscription status='subscribed' for real backlog. `days_open`
  buggy (~0 always) — use `resolved_day - open_day`. No `issue_type` col — use
  `resolution_type` ('ops_resolved' or NULL).
- Existing subscribers keep signup-time `listed_price` locked in forever. Real avg effective
  price per payment this week ≈ $20.25 (empirical: $324/16 payments — small sample, noisy).
- delivered_quality = (base[0.20] + q_shared_global_bonus + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier.
  Day210: global_bonus=0.1907 (2 completed R&D tiers, unchanged). Group bonuses (frozen): S1
  +0.1458, S2 +0.2547, S3 +0.1841, E-groups +0.
- R&D tiers 1-20 exist: tier1 $166,667/+0.04(DONE), tier2 $333,333/+0.07(DONE), tier3 $500,000/
  +0.11 (cheapest available, still unaffordable at $81K cash), tiers 4-20 scale up to $25M/+8.0.
- Compute cost/unit by MODEL tier (1-5): T1 $0.0003, T2 $0.002, T3 $0.006, T4 $0.012, T5 $0.03.
  Quality mult: T1 .60×, T2 .75×, T3 .90×, T4 1.00×, T5 1.10×. Current model tiers: A=2,B=4,C=5.
  CAPACITY tiers (0-7): T0=50K/day $85, **T1=200K/day $215 (CURRENT)**, T2=800K/day $530, T3=
  2.5M/day $1330, T4=8M/day $4000, T5=25M/day $10000, T6=80M/day $28000, T7=300M/day $75000.
  $85/day (=$595/wk) is the fixed floor forever once on Tier0. Usage/customer/day empirical ≈
  85 units (consistent). Compute cost/unit blended empirical ≈ $0.00246/unit this week.
- Ops spend impact: GLOBAL ops (`set_daily_spend(operations=)`) reduces outage prob AND speeds
  resolution (global pool). TARGETED ops only adds per-scope issue-resolution pools, no outage
  effect.
- `nm.query()` read-only SQL, max 5000 rows. `billing_day_mod30` = start_day%30 billing bucket.
  `config_overrides` columns: `id, day, tool_name, setting_type, settings_json`. NOTE:
  `set_daily_spend` (ops/dev) and `set_capacity_tier` NEVER logged in config_overrides — verify
  via dashboard "Daily Spend" line / ledger / `service_day.capacity_tier` instead.
- CLI binaries: `./novamind-operation` (main sim control) vs `novamind` (daily-script mgmt,
  unused).

## Reusable scripts in working directory (USE THESE, avoid re-deriving from scratch)
- `week30_diag.py` — latest comprehensive weekly diagnostic (run FIRST each week, update day
  ranges by +7). Supersedes week29_diag.py (identical methodology).
- `week30_bucket_check.py` — per-bucket own-30-day-cycle-history checker for BOTH just-
  evaluated and next-due buckets, plus full 30-bucket size snapshot. Update day-range tuples by
  +30 each week (bucket history) and bucket-ID window by +7 mod 30. **Earliest-signal
  diagnostic** — caught the 92.7% spike this week before the blended average fully reflected it.
- `week30_forecast.py` — bucket-by-bucket cash/population simulation, refreshed empirical

  query — no manual refresh needed, just update the empirical constants + scenario shapes each
  week based on freshest bucket-history data.
- Older week00-29_* scripts are historical/superseded — kept for reference only.

## Current live settings snapshot (day210, VERIFY on next dashboard!)
Prices: A=$14, B=$79, C=$150 (frozen listed prices for new signups only). Model tiers: A=2,
B=4, C=5. Quotas: A=1000,B=1200,C=1500. Promotion (recurring, unchanged since day140): S1=$12,
S2=$15, S3: by_group_plan A=$25. Lead promotion: global=0, S1=$10, S2=$10, S3=$10 (irrelevant,
0% conversion). Ads strength: 0.0. Targeted ad spend: {} (all zero).
**Ops: $0/day global, $0 targeted. Dev: $0 global/targeted (unchanged 2 weeks now).**
**Capacity: Tier 1 (unchanged, 200K cap $215/day) — model predicts safe to downgrade next week
(day224/wk32), re-verify with fresh usage data before switching.**

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

# ===== Pull current state =====
r = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger")
CASH0 = r['rows'][0]['cash']
print("Current cash:", CASH0)

r = nm.query("SELECT billing_day_mod30, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30")
bucket_sizes = {row['billing_day_mod30']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
for b in range(30):
    bucket_sizes.setdefault(b, 0)
POP0 = sum(bucket_sizes.values())
print("Current population:", POP0, "bucket sizes:", bucket_sizes)

CURRENT_DAY = nm.vars.current_day  # 210

AVG_PRICE = 20.0          # $/payment, empirical $324/16=$20.25 this week (204-210)
USAGE_PER_CUST = 85.0     # units/customer/day, empirical 576365/7/969avg=84.96 this week
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.00246  # $/unit, empirical 1415.39/576365 this week
LEADS_PER_CUST_WK = 0.13  # leads/start-of-week-population, empirical 134/1071=0.125 this week
                          # (NOTE: prior weeks trend was declining 0.138->0.10, but this week
                          # ticked back UP to 0.125-0.15 range -- noisy, not a clean monotonic
                          # decline. Use recent empirical value, revisit next week.)
LEAD_COST = 0.5
OPS_COST_WK = 0.0         # $0 since wk29, unchanged
DEV_COST_WK = 0.0

CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY = 85
CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY = 215
CAP_TIER0_UNITS = 50000
SWITCH_MARGIN = 0.85      # switch to tier0 once projected avg daily usage < this fraction of 50k

def simulate(fail_rate_path, n_weeks=27, verbose=False):
    """fail_rate_path: function(week_index) -> fail rate for buckets due that week"""
    buckets = dict(bucket_sizes)  # mutable copy, bucket -> current subscribed count
    cash = CASH0
    day = CURRENT_DAY
    weekly_cash = [cash]
    pop_hist = [POP0]
    tier = 1  # current tier (still Tier1 as of day210; usage 204-210 averaged ~58-82K/day at various points)
    for wk in range(1, n_weeks+1):
        days_this_week = [day + i for i in range(1, 8)]
        due_buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days_this_week))
        at_risk = sum(buckets[b] for b in due_buckets)
        fr = fail_rate_path(wk)
        failed = at_risk * fr
        survivors = at_risk - failed
        for b in due_buckets:
            if at_risk > 0:
                buckets[b] = buckets[b] * (survivors/at_risk)
        pop_after = sum(buckets.values())
        revenue = survivors * AVG_PRICE  # only surviving/renewing customers pay (rough approx)
        # actually should apply to ALL subscribers billed this week, but non-due buckets don't bill this week

        avg_pop = (pop_hist[-1] + pop_after)/2
        usage_week = avg_pop * USAGE_PER_CUST * 7
        compute_cost = usage_week * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT

        avg_daily_usage = usage_week/7
        if tier == 1 and avg_daily_usage < CAP_TIER0_UNITS*SWITCH_MARGIN:
            tier = 0
        cap_cost_day = CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY if tier==0 else CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_day * 7

        lead_cost = avg_pop * LEADS_PER_CUST_WK * LEAD_COST

        weekly_costs = compute_cost + capacity_cost + OPS_COST_WK + DEV_COST_WK + lead_cost
        cash = cash + revenue - weekly_costs
        day += 7
        weekly_cash.append(cash)
        pop_hist.append(pop_after)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk+{wk} day{day}: at_risk={at_risk:.0f} fail_rate={fr:.2f} failed={failed:.0f} pop={pop_after:.0f} "
                  f"rev={revenue:.0f} compute={compute_cost:.0f} cap={capacity_cost:.0f}(tier{tier}) lead={lead_cost:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")
    return weekly_cash, pop_hist

# ===== Scenarios reflecting the LATEST regime data =====
# bucket24-0 own-cycle-history (days204-210, JUST evaluated): 9.1,6.3,33.2,48.3,29.9 -> 92.7% !!
#   (huge spike, near-total collapse for that cohort: 204 failed of 220 at-risk)
# bucket1-7 own-cycle-history (due NEXT week days211-217): 6.8,4.0,12.6,21.6 -> 44.7% (last obs)
#   roughly doubling each cycle recently (21.6->44.7 ~2.07x) -- if that continues, next ~70-92%
# Blended 30-day trailing: 31.8%(d189)->40.5%(d196)->52.6%(d203)->60.0%(d210), deceleration in
#   the INCREMENT (+12.1pp then +7.4pp) even as level keeps rising -- consistent with the level
#   approaching a high plateau (as more buckets "catch up" to the new bad regime, the marginal
#   pp increase per week shrinks even while absolute level keeps climbing toward ~75-90%).
# Given day204-210's actual observed rate hit 92.7%, we now treat "near-total collapse" as a
# CONFIRMED near-term reality rather than a future risk -- shift all scenarios upward vs wk29.

def optimistic(wk):
    # partial mean-reversion: assumes 92.7% was a noisy outlier, settles around 55-65%
    return min(0.65, 0.50 + 0.03*wk)

def base(wk):
    # sustained high rate consistent with latest 2 datapoints (44.7%, 92.7%), climbing to ~85%
    target = 0.85
    return target - (target-0.65)*max(0, 1-wk/3) if wk<=3 else target

def pessimistic(wk):
    # near-total collapse every cycle, consistent with worst observed (92.7%)
    return min(0.95, 0.75 + 0.05*wk)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}
results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    wc, ph = simulate(fn, n_weeks=27, verbose=(name=='base'))
    results[name] = (wc, ph)
    print(f"\n{name}: wk1={wc[1]:.0f} wk4={wc[4]:.0f} wk12={wc[12]:.0f} wk26={wc[26]:.0f}  (final pop wk26={ph[26]:.0f})")

print("\n===== SUMMARY (point = base, range = opt/pess) =====")
for h, wk in [('1wk',1),('4wk',4),('12wk',12),('26wk',26)]:
    vals = [results[s][0][wk] for s in ('optimistic','base','pessimistic')]
    print(f"{h}: base={results['base'][0][wk]:.0f}  range=[{min(vals):.0f}, {max(vals):.0f}]")

import novamind_api as nm

def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label, groups=('S1','S2','S3')):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {week_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    tot_f, tot_r = 0,0
    for row in r['rows']:
        rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
        tot_f += row['failed']; tot_r += row['at_risk']
        print(row, f"TRUE_fail_rate={rate*100:.1f}%" if rate is not None else "n/a")
    if tot_r:
        print(f"  TOTAL: failed={tot_f} at_risk={tot_r} rate={100*tot_f/tot_r:.1f}%")

print("##### bucket 1-7 (THIS week that just happened, days211-217) full own-history #####")
for (a,b) in [(61,67),(91,97),(121,127),(151,157),(181,187),(211,217)]:
    checkpoint_report(a,b, f"bucket1-7 cycle days{a}-{b}")

sizes = {row['billing_day_mod30']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

r = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger")
CASH0 = r['rows'][0]['cash']
print("Current cash:", CASH0)

r = nm.query("SELECT billing_day_mod30, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30")
bucket_sizes = {row['billing_day_mod30']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
for b in range(30):
    bucket_sizes.setdefault(b, 0)
POP0 = sum(bucket_sizes.values())
print("Current population:", POP0, "bucket sizes:", bucket_sizes)

CURRENT_DAY = nm.vars.current_day  # 217

AVG_PRICE = 20.0
USAGE_PER_CUST = 95.0     # units/customer/day, empirical ~90-105 most days this week (210-214), noisy 59-104 range
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.00246
LEADS_PER_CUST_WK = 0.13
LEAD_COST = 0.5
OPS_COST_WK = 0.0
DEV_COST_WK = 0.0

CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY = 85
CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY = 215
CAP_TIER0_UNITS = 50000

def simulate(fail_rate_path, n_weeks=27, verbose=False, start_tier=0):
    buckets = dict(bucket_sizes)
    cash = CASH0
    day = CURRENT_DAY
    weekly_cash = [cash]
    pop_hist = [POP0]
    tier = start_tier  # switching to Tier0 THIS week (day218 effective)
    for wk in range(1, n_weeks+1):
        days_this_week = [day + i for i in range(1, 8)]
        due_buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days_this_week))
        at_risk = sum(buckets[b] for b in due_buckets)
        fr = fail_rate_path(wk)
        failed = at_risk * fr
        survivors = at_risk - failed
        for b in due_buckets:
            if at_risk > 0:
                buckets[b] = buckets[b] * (survivors/at_risk)
        pop_after = sum(buckets.values())
        revenue = survivors * AVG_PRICE

        avg_pop = (pop_hist[-1] + pop_after)/2
        usage_week = avg_pop * USAGE_PER_CUST * 7
        compute_cost = usage_week * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT

        avg_daily_usage = usage_week/7
        if tier == 1 and avg_daily_usage < CAP_TIER0_UNITS*0.85:
            tier = 0
        cap_cost_day = CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY if tier==0 else CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_day * 7

        lead_cost = avg_pop * LEADS_PER_CUST_WK * LEAD_COST

        weekly_costs = compute_cost + capacity_cost + OPS_COST_WK + DEV_COST_WK + lead_cost
        cash = cash + revenue - weekly_costs
        day += 7
        weekly_cash.append(cash)
        pop_hist.append(pop_after)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk+{wk} day{day}: at_risk={at_risk:.0f} fail_rate={fr:.2f} failed={failed:.0f} pop={pop_after:.0f} "
                  f"rev={revenue:.0f} compute={compute_cost:.0f} cap={capacity_cost:.0f}(tier{tier}) lead={lead_cost:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")
    return weekly_cash, pop_hist

# Scenarios: bucket1-7 own-history just hit 98.2% (from 44.7% two cycles ago -- effectively
# total collapse). bucket8-14 (due this coming week) last obs was 63.7%, trending same direction.
# Given the trajectory, treat near-total collapse (90-99%) as the base case going forward for
# ALL remaining buckets -- the quality gap is now so wide that almost nobody re-qualifies.

def optimistic(wk):
    # some mean reversion -- assume most-collapsed cohorts already gone, remaining tail is
    # slightly stickier (newer signups, higher tenure-loyalty bonus); settle at ~70-80%
    return min(0.80, 0.55 + 0.05*wk)

def base(wk):
    return min(0.97, 0.75 + 0.06*wk)

def pessimistic(wk):
    return min(0.99, 0.90 + 0.03*wk)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}
results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    wc, ph = simulate(fn, n_weeks=27, verbose=(name=='base'))
    results[name] = (wc, ph)
    print(f"\n{name}: wk1={wc[1]:.0f} wk4={wc[4]:.0f} wk12={wc[12]:.0f} wk26={wc[26]:.0f}  (final pop wk26={ph[26]:.0f}, pop_wk4={ph[4]:.0f})")

print("\n===== SUMMARY (point = base, range = opt/pess) =====")
for h, wk in [('1wk',1),('4wk',4),('12wk',12),('26wk',26)]:
    vals = [results[s][0][wk] for s in ('optimistic','base','pessimistic')]
    print(f"{h}: base={results['base'][0][wk]:.0f}  range=[{min(vals):.0f}, {max(vals):.0f}]")

# Sanity floor check: once population ~0, pure floor burn = tier0 cost/week = 595/wk
print("\nFloor burn check: Tier0 $85/day =", 85*7, "/wk;", 85*84, "/12wk (84d);", 85*182,"/26wk(182d)")

week vs 115 opened). Outage YES (30min, day213) but Overload=None — random outage, not
capacity-driven (ops=$0 → baseline ~3%/day risk, unavoidable without spend we can't justify).

day218. Saves $130/day (~$910/wk) for remainder of game.** Verified safe: usage/day already

   **day217=78.2%**. Still climbing, no sign of plateau yet.
2. **Bucket1-7 own-30-day-cycle-history (just evaluated, days211-217): 6.8%→4.0%→12.6%→
   21.6%→44.7%→98.2%**. Went from "large but survivable" to "near-total collapse" in ONE
   cycle (44.7%→98.2%, +53.5pp / ~2.2x). S1=98.3% fail, S2=95.5%, S3=100% (last S3 customer
   gone). This bucket-group is now down to residual survivors only (11 total across buckets
   0,2-7).
3. **Bucket8-14 (due THIS COMING week, days218-224) own-history: 10.7%→3.3%→16.4%→22.1%→
   63.7%** (last obs, days188-194). Same trajectory shape as bucket1-7 had one cycle prior
   (21.6%→44.7%→98.2%) — expect bucket8-14's next value (this week) to jump sharply, plausibly
   70-99%. This bucket is the largest remaining cohort at **178 at-risk (46% of total
   population)** — single biggest churn event upcoming. Watch closely next week.
4. **Population(t+1) = population(t) − failed_in_due_buckets mechanic CONFIRMED AGAIN** (6th
   consecutive week exact match: 481 failed = 481 population lost).
5. Remaining bucket schedule (current snapshot, 386 total): buckets8-14=178 (due wk32,
   day218-224), buckets15-21=143 (due wk33, day225-231), buckets22-28=52 (due wk34,
   day232-238), buckets29+0-5=12 (due wk35, day239-245), residual bucket6-7=3 (wk36+).
   **Extinction of entire individual population plausible within 3-5 more weeks** given the
   fail-rate trajectory — much faster than any prior estimate.

delivered-quality threshold for nearly the entire book. R&D tier3 ($500K) still ~6.3x
unaffordable vs $78,879 cash. Dev spend at $0. Nothing to reverse this — pure harvest mode.

## 💰 Updated cash forecast model (week31_forecast.py — MAJOR revision, extinction now ~2-3x faster)
Bucket-by-bucket simulation, forced Tier0 from day218, fail-rate scenarios re-tuned upward given
98.2%/63.7% observations (optimistic 55%→80% ramp, base 75%→97% ramp, pessimistic 90%→99%).
**Population now modeled to hit ~0 within 8-10 weeks (~day287-294)**, vs wk30's estimate of
10-14 weeks — confirms acceleration. Once population=0, pure floor burn = Tier0 $85/day=$595/wk
for remainder of game (no revenue, no compute, no leads). Model output: wk1=$78,427
range[78018,79143]; wk4=$76,519 range[75958,77790]; wk12=$71,663 range[71162,73157];
wk26=$63,333 range[62832,64828]. Spread is narrow because once extinct, trajectory is
deterministic (floor burn only) — the fail-rate uncertainty mostly affects TIMING not the
ultimate 26wk level. Submitted forecast widened beyond pure model range for safety margin
(unknown-unknowns: faster/slower extinction, any surprise mechanic): 1wk point $78,400
[$77,300-$79,600]; 4wk point $76,500 [$74,500-$78,700]; 12wk point $71,700 [$68,500-$75,000];
26wk point $63,300 [$58,000-$69,000].

1. Run blended 30-day trailing churn rate + bucket-own-history check (both just-evaluated AND
   next-due buckets) — use week31_diag.py / week31_bucket_check.py as templates, bump day
   ranges by +7 (blended rate) or +30 per bucket-history-entry (bucket cycles) each week.

- 504 sim days = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Week31/72 done (~43%, 41 remain).

- subscriptions.status values: 'lead','lost','subscribed','cancelled'. Filter
  `status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')` for active-population/churn queries.
- churn = 100% driven by 30-day billing-cycle evaluation (confirmed 6 weeks running, exact
  match each time). `population(t+1) = population(t) − failed_in_due_buckets_that_week`.
- lead volume scales with population but noisily — ~0.10-0.15 leads per start-of-week
  population per week; conversion to subscriber is now 0% (has been for many weeks).
- `issues` table: filter by subscription status='subscribed' for real backlog. `days_open`
  buggy (~0 always) — use `resolved_day - open_day`. No `issue_type` col — use
  `resolution_type` ('ops_resolved' or NULL).
- Existing subscribers keep signup-time `listed_price` locked in forever. Avg effective price
  per payment ≈ $20 (empirical: $181/9=$20.11 this week, consistent with prior weeks).

  bonuses remain exactly frozen as expected/documented: S1 +0.1458, S2 +0.2547 (S3 n/a, extinct).

  cash), tiers 4-20 scale up to $25M/+8.0.
- Compute cost/unit by MODEL tier (1-5): T1 $0.0003, T2 $0.002, T3 $0.006, T4 $0.012, T5 $0.03.
  Quality mult: T1 .60×, T2 .75×, T3 .90×, T4 1.00×, T5 1.10×. Current model tiers: A=2,B=4,C=5.
  CAPACITY tiers (0-7): **T0=50K/day $85/day (CURRENT, switched day217/218)**, T1=200K/day
  $215, T2=800K/day $530, T3=2.5M/day $1330, T4=8M/day $4000, T5=25M/day $10000, T6=80M/day
  $28000, T7=300M/day $75000. $85/day (=$595/wk) is the fixed floor forever now — no further
  downgrade possible. Usage/customer/day empirical ≈ 90-105 (noisy, occasionally dips to

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def monthly_rate(day_end, groups=('S1','S2','S3'), window=30):
    day_start = day_end - (window-1)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {day_start} AND {day_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {day_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    row = r['rows'][0]
    rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
    return rate, row['failed'], row['at_risk']

print("\n##### BLENDED 30-day trailing churn rate — PRIMARY HEALTH METRIC #####")

def checkpoint_report(week_start, week_end, label, groups=('S1','S2','S3')):
    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))

    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)

      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {week_start})

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

r = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger")
CASH0 = r['rows'][0]['cash']
print("Current cash:", CASH0)

r = nm.query("SELECT billing_day_mod30, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30")
bucket_sizes = {row['billing_day_mod30']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
for b in range(30):
    bucket_sizes.setdefault(b, 0)
POP0 = sum(bucket_sizes.values())
print("Current population:", POP0, "bucket sizes:", bucket_sizes)

CURRENT_DAY = nm.vars.current_day  # 217

AVG_PRICE = 20.0
USAGE_PER_CUST = 95.0     # units/customer/day, empirical ~90-105 most days this week (210-214), noisy 59-104 range
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.00246
LEADS_PER_CUST_WK = 0.13
LEAD_COST = 0.5
OPS_COST_WK = 0.0
DEV_COST_WK = 0.0

CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY = 85
CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY = 215
CAP_TIER0_UNITS = 50000

def simulate(fail_rate_path, n_weeks=27, verbose=False, start_tier=0):
    buckets = dict(bucket_sizes)
    cash = CASH0
    day = CURRENT_DAY
    weekly_cash = [cash]
    pop_hist = [POP0]
    tier = start_tier  # switching to Tier0 THIS week (day218 effective)
    for wk in range(1, n_weeks+1):
        days_this_week = [day + i for i in range(1, 8)]
        due_buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days_this_week))
        at_risk = sum(buckets[b] for b in due_buckets)
        fr = fail_rate_path(wk)
        failed = at_risk * fr
        survivors = at_risk - failed
        for b in due_buckets:
            if at_risk > 0:
                buckets[b] = buckets[b] * (survivors/at_risk)
        pop_after = sum(buckets.values())
        revenue = survivors * AVG_PRICE

        avg_pop = (pop_hist[-1] + pop_after)/2
        usage_week = avg_pop * USAGE_PER_CUST * 7
        compute_cost = usage_week * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT

        avg_daily_usage = usage_week/7
        if tier == 1 and avg_daily_usage < CAP_TIER0_UNITS*0.85:
            tier = 0
        cap_cost_day = CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY if tier==0 else CAP_TIER1_COST_DAY
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_day * 7

        lead_cost = avg_pop * LEADS_PER_CUST_WK * LEAD_COST

        weekly_costs = compute_cost + capacity_cost + OPS_COST_WK + DEV_COST_WK + lead_cost
        cash = cash + revenue - weekly_costs
        day += 7
        weekly_cash.append(cash)
        pop_hist.append(pop_after)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk+{wk} day{day}: at_risk={at_risk:.0f} fail_rate={fr:.2f} failed={failed:.0f} pop={pop_after:.0f} "
                  f"rev={revenue:.0f} compute={compute_cost:.0f} cap={capacity_cost:.0f}(tier{tier}) lead={lead_cost:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")
    return weekly_cash, pop_hist

# Scenarios: bucket1-7 own-history just hit 98.2% (from 44.7% two cycles ago -- effectively
# total collapse). bucket8-14 (due this coming week) last obs was 63.7%, trending same direction.
# Given the trajectory, treat near-total collapse (90-99%) as the base case going forward for
# ALL remaining buckets -- the quality gap is now so wide that almost nobody re-qualifies.

def optimistic(wk):
    # some mean reversion -- assume most-collapsed cohorts already gone, remaining tail is
    # slightly stickier (newer signups, higher tenure-loyalty bonus); settle at ~70-80%
    return min(0.80, 0.55 + 0.05*wk)

def base(wk):
    return min(0.97, 0.75 + 0.06*wk)

def pessimistic(wk):
    return min(0.99, 0.90 + 0.03*wk)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}
results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    wc, ph = simulate(fn, n_weeks=27, verbose=(name=='base'))
    results[name] = (wc, ph)

print("\n===== SUMMARY (point = base, range = opt/pess) =====")
for h, wk in [('1wk',1),('4wk',4),('12wk',12),('26wk',26)]:
    vals = [results[s][0][wk] for s in ('optimistic','base','pessimistic')]
    print(f"{h}: base={results['base'][0][wk]:.0f}  range=[{min(vals):.0f}, {max(vals):.0f}]")

# Sanity floor check: once population ~0, pure floor burn = tier0 cost/week = 595/wk

        at_risk = sum(buckets[b] for b in due_buckets)
        fr = fail_rate_path(wk)
        failed = at_risk * fr
        survivors = at_risk - failed
        for b in due_buckets:
            if at_risk > 0:
                buckets[b] = buckets[b] * (survivors/at_risk)
        pop_after = sum(buckets.values())
        revenue = survivors * AVG_PRICE

        avg_pop = (pop_hist[-1] + pop_after)/2
        usage_week = avg_pop * USAGE_PER_CUST * 7
        compute_cost = usage_week * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT

        cap_cost_day = CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY  # floor forever, pop only shrinking
        capacity_cost = cap_cost_day * 7

        lead_cost = avg_pop * LEADS_PER_CUST_WK * LEAD_COST

        weekly_costs = compute_cost + capacity_cost + OPS_COST_WK + DEV_COST_WK + lead_cost
        cash = cash + revenue - weekly_costs
        day += 7
        weekly_cash.append(cash)
        pop_hist.append(pop_after)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk+{wk} day{day}: at_risk={at_risk:.0f} fail_rate={fr:.2f} failed={failed:.0f} pop={pop_after:.1f} "
                  f"rev={revenue:.0f} compute={compute_cost:.0f} cap={capacity_cost:.0f}(tier{tier}) lead={lead_cost:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")
    return weekly_cash, pop_hist

# bucket8-14 showed right before ITS final 99.4% wipeout. Expect bucket15-21 to also largely
# wipe out this cycle (85-99%). Remaining bucket22-28 (52) and bucket29+0-6 (14) will likely
# follow the same total-collapse pattern within 2-3 more weeks. Population is on track to hit
# ~single digits / zero within 3-4 weeks (day238-245), MUCH faster than prior (8-10wk) estimate.

def optimistic(wk):
    # slower collapse -- newer/stickier cohorts resist a bit longer
    return min(0.95, 0.75 + 0.06*wk)

def base(wk):
    # matches observed acceleration pattern (66.9% -> ~95%+ in one cycle)
    return min(0.98, 0.85 + 0.05*wk)

def pessimistic(wk):
    # near-total wipeout every remaining cycle, same as bucket8-14's 99.4%
    return min(0.995, 0.95 + 0.02*wk)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}
results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    wc, ph = simulate(fn, n_weeks=26, verbose=(name=='base'))
    results[name] = (wc, ph)
    print(f"\n{name}: wk1={wc[1]:.0f} wk4={wc[4]:.0f} wk12={wc[12]:.0f} wk26={wc[26]:.0f}  (pop wk1={ph[1]:.0f} wk4={ph[4]:.0f} wk12={ph[12]:.0f} wk26={ph[26]:.0f})")

print("\n===== SUMMARY (point = base, range = opt/pess) =====")
for h, wk in [('1wk',1),('4wk',4),('12wk',12),('26wk',26)]:
    vals = [results[s][0][wk] for s in ('optimistic','base','pessimistic')]
    print(f"{h}: base={results['base'][0][wk]:.0f}  range=[{min(vals):.0f}, {max(vals):.0f}]")

print("\nFloor burn check: Tier0 $85/day =", 85*7, "/wk;", 85*84, "/12wk (84d);", 85*182,"/26wk(182d)")

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def monthly_rate(day_end, groups=('S1','S2','S3'), window=30):
    day_start = day_end - (window-1)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {day_start} AND {day_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {day_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    row = r['rows'][0]
    rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
    return rate, row['failed'], row['at_risk']

print("\n##### BLENDED 30-day trailing churn rate — PRIMARY HEALTH METRIC #####")
print("(history: day203=52.6%, day210=60.0%, day217=78.2%, day224=85.7%)")
for day in [203,210,217,224,231]:
    rate, failed, at_risk = monthly_rate(day)
    if rate is not None:
        print(f"day {day}: blended_rate={rate*100:.1f}%  (failed={failed}, at_risk={at_risk})")
    else:
        print(f"day {day}: no at-risk population left")

print("\n##### TRUE active population trend (by group) #####")
for day in [203,210,217,224,231]:
    r = nm.query(f"""
    SELECT c.group_id, COUNT(*) as active
    FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day} AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day > {day})
    AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    """)
    d = {row['group_id']: row['active'] for row in r['rows']}
    print(f"day {day}: {d}  total={sum(d.values())}")

print("\n##### Cash trend via ledger cumsum (exact) #####")
for day in [203,210,217,224,231]:
    r = nm.query(f"SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger WHERE day <= {day}")
    print(f"day {day}: cash={r['rows'][0]['cash']:.2f}")

print("\n##### This week's ledger breakdown (days 225-231) #####")
r = nm.query("""
SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total, COUNT(*) as n
FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 225 AND 231
GROUP BY category ORDER BY total ASC
""")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n##### Issues: opened vs resolved trend, and current backlog #####")
for (a,b,lbl) in [(211,217,'wk31'),(218,224,'wk32'),(225,231,'wk33')]:

      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {week_start})

def simulate(fail_rate_path, n_weeks=26, verbose=False):
    buckets = dict(bucket_sizes)
    cash = CASH0
    day = CURRENT_DAY
    weekly_cash = [cash]
    pop_hist = [POP0]
    for wk in range(1, n_weeks+1):

        at_risk = sum(buckets[b] for b in due_buckets)
        fr = fail_rate_path(wk)
        failed = at_risk * fr
        survivors = at_risk - failed
        for b in due_buckets:
            if at_risk > 0:
                buckets[b] = buckets[b] * (survivors/at_risk)
        pop_after = sum(buckets.values())
        revenue = survivors * AVG_PRICE

        avg_pop = (pop_hist[-1] + pop_after)/2
        usage_week = avg_pop * USAGE_PER_CUST * 7
        compute_cost = usage_week * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT
        capacity_cost = CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY * 7

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 231 (Week 33 dashboard reviewed, actions taken = NONE, about to advance to Week 34).
Cash $77,014 (down -$833 from $77,847). Population **CRATERED 209→67 (-142, -68.0%)**.
S1=62, S2=5, S3=0 (extinct since wk31). Cancellations=142 exactly matches population loss
(mechanic confirmed 8th consecutive week). New leads 22, new subscribers 0 — 0% conversion,
confirmed AGAIN (9th+ week). Open issues 59 (down from 197 — backlog shrinking in lockstep with
population: opened 11 / resolved 13 this week). Overload=None, Outage=No (clean week). Usage
fell from 21,174 (day225) to 7,977 (day231) as population collapsed intra-week — comfortably
under Tier0's 50K cap throughout, Tier0 remains the correct permanent floor (no action needed
or possible). **NO settings changes made this week — holding all frozen settings per standing
harvest-mode strategy (10th+ week running).** Confirmed via config_overrides query (0 rows
since day218) + dashboard: Ops=$0, Dev=$0, ad spend=$0 all channels, ads_strength=0,
Capacity=Tier0, prices/promotions unchanged since day140/168.

## 🚨 KEY FINDING: bucket15-21 confirmed SECOND consecutive near-total wipeout (99.3%)
1. **Blended 30-day trailing churn rate**: day210=60.0%, day217=78.2%, day224=85.7%,
   **day231=94.3%**. Still climbing, now near-saturated.
2. **Bucket15-21 own-30-day-cycle-history (days195-201 → days225-231): 66.9% → 99.3%**
   (132/133 S1, 10/10 S2 — S2 hit literally 100%). This is the SAME acceleration shape
   bucket8-14 showed the cycle before its 99.4% wipeout. **Pattern now firmly established across
   TWO independent bucket-cohorts: once a cohort's prior-cycle fail rate crosses ~60-65%, the
   NEXT cycle goes to near-total (95-100%) collapse.** Treat this as the base-rate assumption
   for all remaining cohorts going forward.
3. **Bucket22-28 (due THIS COMING week, days232-238) own-history: 8.4%→35.9%→44.4%→10.2%→
   80.2%** (last obs, days202-208). Already crossed the ~60-65% collapse threshold → expect
   near-total wipeout (90-99%+) THIS coming week. At-risk = 52 (28/12/2/2/1/2/5 across buckets
   22-28). Expect population to crash from 67 → roughly 15-20 by day238.
4. **NEW EVIDENCE — promotions confirmed structurally useless for RETENTION too (not just
   acquisition):** S2 has a LARGER recurring promotion/discount than S1, yet churned at 100%
   (10/10) vs S1's 99.2% (132/133) in the identical cycle. Bigger discount did NOT save S2 —
   if anything it fared marginally worse. This proves the quality-expectation gap is now so
   large that price/promotion levers cannot meaningfully move the plan-acceptance threshold
   anymore. **Promotion changes are now confirmed dead for BOTH acquisition (0% conversion) AND
   retention (this evidence) — stop considering them entirely, permanently.**
5. **Considered and REJECTED activating `set_ads_strength`** (in-app ads generate daily
   ad_revenue per subscriber but degrade satisfaction/perceived quality — formula:
   quality_penalty = ads_quality_sensitivity × log_scaled_effective_ads; dollar_return =
   ads_return_sensitivity × log_scaled_effective_ads/customer/day; log curve, diminishing
   returns). Rationale for rejecting: (a) ads_return_sensitivity magnitude is undocumented and
   likely small given tiny population (67, falling fast); (b) it would degrade satisfaction for
   the ~15 NOT-yet-due customers (buckets 29,0,2-7,13,15) who are currently safe for a few more
   billing cycles — risks accelerating their churn too, for uncertain small gain; (c) absolute
   dollar stakes are tiny at this population size. **Do not revisit unless population somehow
   stabilizes (won't happen) or documentation reveals the sensitivity constant is large.**
6. Population(t+1) = population(t) − failed_in_due_buckets mechanic **CONFIRMED AGAIN** (8th
   consecutive week exact match: 142 failed = 142 population lost).
7. Remaining bucket schedule (current snapshot, 67 total): bucket22-28=52 (due wk34,
   day232-238, ALREADY past collapse threshold), bucket29+0,2-7=13 (due wk35, day239-245),
   bucket13=1 + bucket15=1 (residual survivor of THIS week's wipeout, due ~wk37+, day253-261).
   **Extinction of entire individual population now modeled at ~4-5 weeks out (day255-266),
   faster than prior estimates, across all three scenarios (they converge tightly since only
   fail-rate TIMING differs, not the ultimate floor-burn outcome).**
**Cause (unchanged):** cumulative competitor-driven quality-expectation drift crossed
delivered-quality threshold for nearly the entire book, and evidence above shows it's now large
enough that price/promotion cannot offset it at the margin. R&D tier3 ($500,000) still ~6.5x
unaffordable vs $77,014 cash. Dev spend at $0. Nothing left to reverse this — pure harvest mode.
**Economic note (unchanged):** each surviving customer is still net cash-positive (~$4.6/wk
revenue vs ~$1.5-2/wk marginal compute cost) — the fixed $595/wk Tier0 capacity cost is the only
true "floor" once population hits 0. Downside is capped (floor-burn ceiling); if extinction runs
slower than modeled, actual cash trends toward the HIGHER end of forecast ranges. Asymmetric
risk favors upside surprises, not downside ones (absent a new outage/cost shock).

## 💰 Updated cash forecast model (week33_diag.py, forecast section — recalibrated to 2nd wipeout)
Bucket-by-bucket simulation, Tier0 floor capacity throughout, fail-rate scenarios pushed toward
near-total given TWO consecutive ~99% cohort wipeouts (optimistic 0.80+0.07wk cap 0.97; base
0.90+0.05wk cap 0.99; pessimistic 0.97+0.02wk cap 0.999). Model output: wk1(day238)
opt=$76,476/base=$76,396/pess=$76,356 (pop 21.8/17.6/15.5); wk4(day259) opt=$74,619/
base=$74,549/pess=$74,516 (pop 7.5/2.7/0.5 — essentially extinct); wk12(day315) all three
≈$69,676-69,774 (pop=0 in all scenarios — pure floor burn); wk26(day413) all three
≈$61,206-61,304 (pop=0, pure floor burn). Scenario spread is very narrow (<$120 at every
horizon) because once extinct the trajectory is deterministic floor burn ($85/day capacity +
trivial lead cost) — fail-rate uncertainty only affects TIMING, not the ultimate level.
**Submitted forecast widened beyond pure model range** for realistic uncertainty (model
misspecification, possible outage, possible longer-than-modeled survival = upside per
asymmetric-risk note): 1wk pt $76,400 [$75,900-$76,900]; 4wk pt $74,500 [$73,300-$75,700];
12wk pt $69,700 [$67,500-$72,800]; 26wk pt $61,200 [$56,000-$67,000] (upper skewed slightly
wider than lower per asymmetric-risk logic).
**Forecast track record check:** last week's submitted 1wk point ($77,300, range
$76,300-$78,300) vs this week's actual ($77,014) — error only $286 (0.37%), well within range.
Model calibration is good; keep using same methodology.

## 📋 PROCESS CHECKLIST — EVERY WEEK (updated wk33; population now only 67, near-terminal)
1. Run week33_diag.py (rename/bump to week34_diag.py next week) — bump day ranges by +7
   (blended rate) or +30 per bucket-history-entry (bucket cycles) each week. It now includes
   the forecast simulation inline (merged diag+forecast into one script this week to save
   turns — only ONE bash tool call is processed per turn in this environment, confirmed again:
   parallel read_file calls in the same message get skipped except the first. ALWAYS do one
   tool call per message now, don't bother trying to parallelize independent calls.)
2. **Capacity: Tier0 ($85/day, 50K cap) is the permanent floor — no further downgrade possible,
   no upgrade needed.** Usage was 8K-21K/day this week at pop 67→ falling fast, nowhere near cap.
3. Ops/Dev: $0/$0, unchanged, at floor. R&D: still unaffordable (cheapest tier3 $500K vs cash
   ~$77K). Ads_strength: considered and rejected (see finding #5 above) — do not revisit.
4. Pricing/promotion: HOLD (unchanged since day140/168), CONFIRMED structurally moot for BOTH
   acquisition (0% conversion) and retention (S2 evidence this week) — permanently stop
   considering, don't even re-check this section in future weeks unless conversion resumes.
5. Social media: SKIP (no genuine positive angle, feed is support complaints + competitor
   noise). Stop checking entirely — not worth the query cost given near-zero population.
6. Enterprise: 0 rows in `enterprise_turns`, structurally dead all game — stop checking.
7. Market research: not worth $25K (~32% of cash) — skip permanently.
8. Population by group: S1=62, S2=5, S3=0(extinct). Total=67.
9. New Leads vs New Subscribers: 22 leads, 0 new subscribers — 0% conversion, confirmed AGAIN
   (9th+ week). Growth permanently off the table.
10. Forecast-calibration check done this week (see above) — good accuracy, low priority to
    repeat often; check again in ~4-6 weeks if curious.
11. Only ONE tool call reliably processed per turn (confirmed again this week, not just bash) —
    do exactly one tool call per message, don't try to batch independent read_file/bash calls
    in a single turn expecting parallel execution.
12. **Once population hits ~0 (est. day255-266, all scenarios converge), workflow simplifies
    drastically** — no more bucket/churn checks needed, just confirm cash draining at ~$595/wk
    floor rate (+trivial lead cost) and submit tight, high-confidence forecasts. We're probably
    only 1-2 more weeks away from this simplification point (population likely ~15-20 after next
    week's bucket22-28 resolution). Keep doing the lightweight bucket check for 1-2 more weeks,
    then switch to simplified floor-burn-only monitoring.

## Key mechanics reference (condensed, verified through wk33)
- 504 sim days = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Week33/72 done (~46%, 39 remain).
- Config-change lag = 1 DAY. R&D and market research act/charge IMMEDIATELY (no lag).
- subscriptions.status values: 'lead','lost','subscribed','cancelled'. Filter
  `status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')` for active-population/churn queries. NOTE: 'active' is
  NOT a valid status value. Always JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id for group_id
  (group_id lives on `customers`, not `subscriptions`).
- churn = 100% driven by 30-day billing-cycle evaluation (confirmed 8 weeks running, exact
  match each time). `population(t+1) = population(t) − failed_in_due_buckets_that_week`.
- lead volume now seems to be settling toward a small roughly-flat number (~20-25/wk) somewhat
  independent of population size (22 leads at pop~67-209 straddling this week) rather than
  strictly proportional — treat as flat ~$10-15/wk lead-acquisition cost going forward.
  Conversion to subscriber is 0% (has been for 9+ weeks).

  `resolution_type` ('ops_resolved' or NULL).
- Existing subscribers keep signup-time `listed_price` locked in forever. Promotions
  (recurring discount) DO apply to existing subs at each billing cycle but are now PROVEN

  price/promotion no longer moves the needle at all.
- delivered_quality = (base[0.20] + q_shared_global_bonus + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier.
  Day231 dashboard shows global_bonus=0.1862 (up slightly from 0.1819 at day224, dev spend

  S2 +0.2547 (S3 extinct, D_E09 +0.0072 — irrelevant, no active D_E09 subs).

  $10000, T6=80M/day $28000, T7=300M/day $75000. $85/day (=$595/wk) is the fixed floor forever.

  per-scope issue-resolution pools, no outage effect. At $0 ops, baseline outage risk ~3%/day.
- `set_ads_strength`: quality_penalty = ads_quality_sensitivity × log_scaled_effective_ads
  (degrades satisfaction); dollar_return = ads_return_sensitivity × log_scaled_effective_ads/

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def monthly_rate(day_end, groups=('S1','S2','S3'), window=30):
    day_start = day_end - (window-1)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {day_start} AND {day_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {day_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    row = r['rows'][0]
    rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
    return rate, row['failed'], row['at_risk']

print("\n##### BLENDED 30-day trailing churn rate — PRIMARY HEALTH METRIC #####")
print("(history: day203=52.6%, day210=60.0%, day217=78.2%, day224=85.7%)")
for day in [203,210,217,224,231]:
    rate, failed, at_risk = monthly_rate(day)
    if rate is not None:
        print(f"day {day}: blended_rate={rate*100:.1f}%  (failed={failed}, at_risk={at_risk})")
    else:
        print(f"day {day}: no at-risk population left")

print("\n##### TRUE active population trend (by group) #####")
for day in [203,210,217,224,231]:
    r = nm.query(f"""
    SELECT c.group_id, COUNT(*) as active
    FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day} AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day > {day})
    AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    """)
    d = {row['group_id']: row['active'] for row in r['rows']}
    print(f"day {day}: {d}  total={sum(d.values())}")

print("\n##### Cash trend via ledger cumsum (exact) #####")
for day in [203,210,217,224,231]:
    r = nm.query(f"SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger WHERE day <= {day}")
    print(f"day {day}: cash={r['rows'][0]['cash']:.2f}")

print("\n##### This week's ledger breakdown (days 225-231) #####")

    days = list(range(week_start, week_end+1))
    buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days))
    buckets_str = ",".join(str(b) for b in buckets)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT c.group_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {week_start} AND {week_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.billing_day_mod30 IN ({buckets_str})
      AND s.start_day <= {week_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {week_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    ORDER BY c.group_id
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    print(f"\n=== {label}: days {week_start}-{week_end}, buckets {buckets} ===")
    tot_f, tot_r = 0,0
    for row in r['rows']:
        rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
        tot_f += row['failed']; tot_r += row['at_risk']
        print(row, f"TRUE_fail_rate={rate*100:.1f}%" if rate is not None else "n/a")
    if tot_r:
        print(f"  TOTAL: failed={tot_f} at_risk={tot_r} rate={100*tot_f/tot_r:.1f}%")
    return tot_f, tot_r

print("\n##### bucket 15-21 (THIS week that just happened, days225-231) full own-history #####")

WHERE status='subscribed'

ORDER BY billing_day_mod30
""")
sizes = {row['billing_day_mod30']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
for k in sorted(sizes): print(f"  bucket {k}: {sizes[k]}")
print("mean bucket size:", sum(sizes.values())/len(sizes) if sizes else 0)
print("total:", sum(sizes.values()))

print("\n##### Config check (verify still frozen / no drift) #####")

for row in r['rows']:

# ============================================================
print("\n\n===== FORECAST MODEL =====")
r = nm.query("SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger")
CASH0 = r['rows'][0]['cash']
print("Current cash:", CASH0)

r = nm.query("SELECT billing_day_mod30, COUNT(*) as n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30")
bucket_sizes = {row['billing_day_mod30']: row['n'] for row in r['rows']}
for b in range(30):
    bucket_sizes.setdefault(b, 0)
POP0 = sum(bucket_sizes.values())
print("Current population:", POP0, "bucket sizes:", bucket_sizes)

CURRENT_DAY = nm.vars.current_day

AVG_PRICE = 20.0
USAGE_PER_CUST = 90.0
COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT = 0.00246
LEADS_PER_WK_FLAT = 20.0   # leads seem to be settling to a small roughly-flat number regardless of pop, ~22 this wk
LEAD_COST = 0.5
OPS_COST_WK = 0.0
DEV_COST_WK = 0.0
CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY = 85

def simulate(fail_rate_path, n_weeks=26, verbose=False):
    buckets = dict(bucket_sizes)
    cash = CASH0
    day = CURRENT_DAY
    weekly_cash = [cash]
    pop_hist = [POP0]
    for wk in range(1, n_weeks+1):
        days_this_week = [day + i for i in range(1, 8)]
        due_buckets = sorted(set(d % 30 for d in days_this_week))
        at_risk = sum(buckets[b] for b in due_buckets)
        fr = fail_rate_path(wk)
        failed = at_risk * fr
        survivors = at_risk - failed
        for b in due_buckets:
            if at_risk > 0:
                buckets[b] = buckets[b] * (survivors/at_risk)
        pop_after = sum(buckets.values())
        revenue = survivors * AVG_PRICE

        avg_pop = (pop_hist[-1] + pop_after)/2
        usage_week = avg_pop * USAGE_PER_CUST * 7
        compute_cost = usage_week * COMPUTE_COST_PER_UNIT
        capacity_cost = CAP_TIER0_COST_DAY * 7
        lead_cost = LEADS_PER_WK_FLAT * LEAD_COST

        weekly_costs = compute_cost + capacity_cost + OPS_COST_WK + DEV_COST_WK + lead_cost
        cash = cash + revenue - weekly_costs
        day += 7
        weekly_cash.append(cash)
        pop_hist.append(pop_after)
        if verbose:
            print(f"wk+{wk} day{day}: at_risk={at_risk:.0f} fail_rate={fr:.3f} failed={failed:.0f} pop={pop_after:.1f} "
                  f"rev={revenue:.0f} compute={compute_cost:.0f} cap={capacity_cost:.0f} lead={lead_cost:.0f} cash={cash:.0f}")
    return weekly_cash, pop_hist

# EVIDENCE UPDATE (day231): bucket15-21 (143 at-risk) just wiped at ~99% -- SECOND consecutive
# near-total wipeout in a row (bucket8-14 was 99.4%, bucket15-21 ~99%). Pattern now firmly
# established: once a bucket-cohort's prior-cycle fail rate crosses ~60-65%, next cycle goes to
# near-total (95-99.5%) collapse. bucket22-28 (52 at-risk, due wk34) history will show whether
# it has crossed that threshold yet -- check printed output above. Regardless, given only 2
# bucket-groups (22-28: 52, 29-6: 14, resid13: 1 = 67 total) remain, full extinction is now
# expected within ~2-3 weeks even under "optimistic" assumptions.

def optimistic(wk):
    return min(0.97, 0.80 + 0.07*wk)

def base(wk):
    return min(0.99, 0.90 + 0.05*wk)

def pessimistic(wk):
    return min(0.999, 0.97 + 0.02*wk)

scenarios = {'optimistic': optimistic, 'base': base, 'pessimistic': pessimistic}
results = {}
for name, fn in scenarios.items():
    wc, ph = simulate(fn, n_weeks=26, verbose=(name=='base'))
    results[name] = (wc, ph)
    print(f"\n{name}: wk1={wc[1]:.0f} wk4={wc[4]:.0f} wk12={wc[12]:.0f} wk26={wc[26]:.0f}  (pop wk1={ph[1]:.1f} wk4={ph[4]:.1f} wk12={ph[12]:.1f} wk26={ph[26]:.1f})")

print("\n===== SUMMARY (point = base, range = opt/pess) =====")
for h, wk in [('1wk',1),('4wk',4),('12wk',12),('26wk',26)]:
    vals = [results[s][0][wk] for s in ('optimistic','base','pessimistic')]
    print(f"{h}: base={results['base'][0][wk]:.0f}  range=[{min(vals):.0f}, {max(vals):.0f}]")

print("\nFloor burn check: Tier0 $85/day =", 85*7, "/wk;", 85*84, "/12wk (84d);", 85*182,"/26wk(182d)")

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def monthly_rate(day_end, groups=('S1','S2','S3'), window=30):
    day_start = day_end - (window-1)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {day_start} AND {day_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {day_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    row = r['rows'][0]
    rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
    return rate, row['failed'], row['at_risk']

print("\n##### BLENDED 30-day trailing churn rate #####")
print("(history: day210=60.0%, day217=78.2%, day224=85.7%, day231=94.3%)")
for day in [210,217,224,231,238]:
    rate, failed, at_risk = monthly_rate(day)
    if rate is not None:
        print(f"day {day}: blended_rate={rate*100:.1f}%  (failed={failed}, at_risk={at_risk})")
    else:
        print(f"day {day}: no at-risk population left")

print("\n##### TRUE active population trend (by group) #####")
for day in [210,217,224,231,238]:
    r = nm.query(f"""
    SELECT c.group_id, COUNT(*) as active
    FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day} AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day > {day})
    AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
    GROUP BY c.group_id
    """)
    d = {row['group_id']: row['active'] for row in r['rows']}
    print(f"day {day}: {d}  total={sum(d.values())}")

print("\n##### Cash trend via ledger cumsum (exact) #####")
for day in [210,217,224,231,238]:
    r = nm.query(f"SELECT SUM(amount) as cash FROM ledger WHERE day <= {day}")
    print(f"day {day}: cash={r['rows'][0]['cash']:.2f}")

print("\n##### This week's ledger breakdown (days 232-238) #####")
r = nm.query("""
SELECT category, SUM(amount) as total, COUNT(*) as n
FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 232 AND 238
GROUP BY category ORDER BY total ASC
""")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n##### Issues: opened vs resolved trend, current backlog #####")
for (a,b,lbl) in [(218,224,'wk32'),(225,231,'wk33'),(232,238,'wk34')]:
    r = nm.query(f"SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN {a} AND {b}")
    r2 = nm.query(f"SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN {a} AND {b}")
    print(f"{lbl} days{a}-{b}: opened={r['rows'][0]['n']}, resolved={r2['rows'][0]['n']}")

r = nm.query("""
SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM issues i
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id = i.customer_id
WHERE i.resolved_day IS NULL AND s.status='subscribed'
""")
print("current backlog (unresolved, still-subscribed):", r['rows'][0]['n'])

print("\n##### Usage / capacity check (days232-238) #####")
r = nm.query("SELECT day, total_usage_units, p95_ms, error_rate, downtime_minutes, capacity_tier, capacity_units FROM service_day WHERE day BETWEEN 232 AND 238 ORDER BY day")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n##### EXACT enumeration of ALL remaining subscribers (pop=15, fully tractable now) #####")
r = nm.query("""
SELECT s.customer_id, c.group_id, s.plan, s.listed_price, s.start_day, s.billing_day_mod30
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
ORDER BY s.billing_day_mod30
""")
CURRENT_DAY = nm.vars.current_day
for row in r['rows']:
    b = row['billing_day_mod30']
    # next due day = smallest day > current_day with day%30==b
    nd = CURRENT_DAY + 1
    while nd % 30 != b:
        nd += 1
    print(row, "-> next_billing_day=", nd, f"(+{nd-CURRENT_DAY}d)")

print("\n##### Config check (verify still frozen) #####")
r = nm.query("SELECT tool_name, day, settings_json FROM config_overrides WHERE day >= 225 ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 20")
for row in r['rows']:
    print(row)

print("\n##### R&D status #####")
projects = nm.research.list_research_projects()
print(projects)

print("\n##### Enterprise check #####")
r = nm.query("SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM enterprise_turns")
print("enterprise_turns total rows ever:", r['rows'][0]['n'])

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 238 (Week 34 dashboard reviewed, actions = NONE, about to advance to Week 35).

(mechanic confirmed every week for 2+ months running). New leads only 2 (small numbers now,
noisy), new subscribers 0 — 0% conversion continues (10+ consecutive weeks). Open issues 9
(down from 59, backlog shrinking with population: opened 7/resolved 13). Overload=None,
Outage=No. Usage fell 7217→1347 across the week (population collapsing intra-week), day238=
2072 — nowhere near Tier0's 50K cap. **NO settings changes — config_overrides query returned
ZERO rows since day225, dashboard confirms Ops=$0/Dev=$0/Capacity=Tier0/ad spend=$0/ads_strength
=0, prices/promos unchanged since day140/168. Frozen harvest-mode strategy continues.**

## 🚨 KEY FINDING: bucket22-28 wiped at LITERALLY 100% (52/52) — 3rd consecutive near-total wipeout
1. Pattern now **3-for-3 confirmed**: bucket8-14 (99.4%) → bucket15-21 (~99.3%) → bucket22-28
   (**100.0% exactly**, 52 failed / 52 at-risk, zero survivors). Collapse is no longer
   "likely ~95-99%" — treat it as **~100% deterministic** for all remaining due-cohorts.
2. Blended 30-day trailing churn: day224=85.7%, day231=94.3%, **day238=98.4%** — still climbing,
   essentially saturated.
3. **Population is now small enough (15) for EXACT per-customer enumeration instead of
   statistical bucket modeling.** Queried full remaining subscriber list (id/group/plan/price/
   next billing day) — see snapshot below. This is now the primary forecasting method; redo
   this query each week and cross off whoever churned.
4. **Full extinction timeline (assuming ~100% fail, well-supported by 3-for-3 evidence):**
   - Week35 (day239-245): **10 due** (buckets 29,0,2,3,4,5) → pop 15→~5 by day245
   - Week36 (day246-252): **3 due** (bucket 6,7) → pop ~5→~2 by day252
   - Week37 (day253-259): **2 due** (bucket 13,15 — last two survivors) → pop ~2→0 by day259
   - **Full individual-segment extinction expected ~day259 (Week37, ~3 weeks from now)** —
     FASTER than previous "4-5 weeks" estimate because this wipeout was a clean 100%, not ~99%.
5. All other levers remain confirmed dead/moot (carried from wk32-33 findings, re-verify only
   if something changes): pricing/promotions structurally useless for both acquisition (0%
   conversion, 10+ wks) and retention (bigger S2 discount didn't save S2 from 100% churn wk33);
   `set_ads_strength` rejected (undocumented sensitivity, risk to few remaining survivors, tiny
   population = tiny stakes); R&D tier3 $500K vs cash $76,352 (~6.5x unaffordable, tier1&2
   already completed long ago); enterprise permanently dead (0 rows ever in `enterprise_turns`);
   capacity at Tier0 permanent floor (no lower tier exists).
6. **Once population hits 0 (~day259 est.), workflow simplifies to almost nothing**: each week
   just (a) confirm population=0 via one query, (b) confirm config still frozen (one query),
   (c) submit forecast ≈ prior_cash − $596/wk floor burn (tight CI, e.g. ±$100-300 at 1wk scaling
   wider with horizon for lead-trickle/misc noise), (d) advance. No more churn/bucket/issues/
   usage checks needed after that point.

since variance is genuinely small at this population size).

2. Cross off churned customers from the snapshot table above; recompute floor-burn trajectory.
3. Capacity/Ops/Dev/Ads/Promotions/Pricing/R&D/Enterprise: ALL confirmed dead or at permanent
   floor (see finding #5 above) — do not reconsider unless population somehow stabilizes or
   cash grows enough to afford R&D tier3 ($500K, currently ~6.5x cash). Just verify via
   config_overrides (should stay empty) and dashboard header (Ops=$0/Dev=$0/Tier0) — 10 seconds,
   don't deep-dive.
4. Social media: skip permanently (no genuine positive angle, not worth the query).
5. Once population confirmed = 0: stop doing churn/bucket/issues/usage checks entirely. Just
   confirm cash and config, then submit tight floor-burn forecast (point = prior_cash −
   $596×weeks_elapsed, narrow CI e.g. ±$150-400 depending on horizon).
6. **Tool-call environment quirk (re-confirmed many weeks running): only ONE tool call is
   processed per message turn** — issue exactly one call per turn, never rely on parallel/batch
   execution of independent read_file/bash calls in the same message.

## Key mechanics reference (condensed, verified through wk34)
- 504 sim days = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Week34/72 done (~47%, 38 remain).
- Config-change lag = 1 DAY. R&D and market research act/charge IMMEDIATELY (no lag).
- subscriptions.status values: 'lead','lost','subscribed','cancelled' ('active' is NOT valid).
  Filter `status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')` for population/churn queries. JOIN customers c
  ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id for group_id (lives on customers, not subscriptions).
- churn = 100% driven by 30-day billing-cycle evaluation, now essentially deterministic at
  ~100% fail rate per due cohort (3-for-3 near-total wipeouts). population(t+1) = population(t)
  − failed_in_due_buckets_that_week — confirmed exactly, every week, for 2+ months.
- Lead volume now small and noisy (2-22/wk observed, no clear pattern) — treat as trivial cost
  (~$1-2.5/wk at $0.5/lead). Conversion to subscriber = 0% for 10+ consecutive weeks.
- `issues` table: filter by subscription status='subscribed' for real backlog. `days_open`
  buggy — use `resolved_day - open_day`. No `issue_type` col — use `resolution_type`
  ('ops_resolved' or NULL).
- Existing subscribers keep signup-time `listed_price` forever. Promotions apply as recurring
  discount at billing but PROVEN ineffective at preventing churn once quality gap is this large
  (S2 had bigger discount than S1, churned at 100% vs 99.2% — discount didn't help at all).
- delivered_quality = (base[0.20] + q_shared_global_bonus + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier.
  Day238 dashboard: global_bonus=0.1902 (slow drift, dev spend still $0, not actionable). Per-
  group bonuses frozen: S1 +0.1458, S2 +0.2547 (S3 extinct; D_E09 +0.0072 irrelevant, no subs).
- R&D tiers 1-20: tier1 $166,667/+0.04(DONE,+0.0289 actual), tier2 $333,333/+0.07(DONE,+0.0619
  actual), tier3 $500,000/+0.11 (cheapest available, still ~6.5x unaffordable at $76,352 cash),
  tiers 4-20 scale up to $25M/+8.0. Not viable at current/near-future cash levels.
- Compute cost/unit by MODEL tier (1-5): T1 $0.0003, T2 $0.002, T3 $0.006, T4 $0.012, T5 $0.03.
  Quality mult: T1 .60×, T2 .75×, T3 .90×, T4 1.00×, T5 1.10×. Current model tiers: A=2,B=4,C=5.

import novamind_api as nm

print("current_day:", nm.vars.current_day)

def monthly_rate(day_end, groups=('S1','S2','S3'), window=30):
    day_start = day_end - (window-1)
    groups_str = ",".join(f"'{g}'" for g in groups)
    q = f"""
    SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN s.end_day BETWEEN {day_start} AND {day_end} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as failed,
           COUNT(*) as at_risk
    FROM subscriptions s
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_day <= {day_start-1}
      AND s.status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')
      AND (s.end_day IS NULL OR s.end_day >= {day_start})
      AND c.group_id IN ({groups_str})
    """
    r = nm.query(q)
    row = r['rows'][0]
    rate = row['failed']/row['at_risk'] if row['at_risk'] else None
    return rate, row['failed'], row['at_risk']

# NovaMind CEO — Memory (persists across weeks; context resets every week!)

## STATUS AS OF: Day 252 (Week 36 dashboard reviewed, actions = NONE, about to advance to Week 37).
Cash $75,152.06 (down -$598.81 from day245's $75,750.87; ledger match exactly: capacity -595,
compute -3.814, dev/ops $0). Population **3** (S1=3, S2=0, S3=0 — all extinct except S1).
This week's 3 cancellations = the 3 customers that were due for billing eval (9114, 9288,
9520) — **all 3 churned, 0 survivors** (consistent with ~90%fail/10%survive: P(0 survive of 3)
=72.9%, this is what happened). Open issues 1 (down from 2). New leads 0, new subscribers 0
(0% conversion continues, 12+ consecutive weeks). No outage this week. Usage way down to
~1907 units for the week (vs 7933 last week) as population shrinks. Capacity tier0, Ops=$0,
Dev=$0 all still confirmed frozen — config_overrides query (day>=239) returned ZERO rows.
**No config changes made this week — continuing frozen harvest-mode strategy.**

## 📋 EXACT remaining-subscriber snapshot (day252, pop=3 — update this list weekly, cross off churned)
| cust_id | group | plan | price | next billing day (+Nd from day252) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3024 | S1 | A | $29 | day253 (+1) |
| 3438 | S1 | A | $29 | day255 (+3) |
| 1946 | S1 | A | $22 | day272 (+20) — survived once already (day242 eval) |
Query to regenerate: `SELECT s.customer_id,c.group_id,s.plan,s.listed_price,s.billing_day_mod30
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.status='subscribed'
ORDER BY s.billing_day_mod30` — then compute next_due = smallest day > current_day with
day%30==billing_day_mod30.

## Extinction timeline (using ~90% fail / ~10% survive per due-customer, confirmed NOT 100%
## deterministic — but this week's cohort of 3 hit the modal "all fail" outcome)
- **Week37 (day253-259): BOTH 3024 and 3438 are due (day253, day255).** This is the big one —
  most likely (81% = 0.9×0.9) both churn → pop 3→1 (just 1946 left). ~18% chance exactly one
  survives → pop→2. ~1% chance both survive → pop stays 3.
- Week38 (day260-266): none due. Pop unchanged from week37 outcome.
- Week39 (day267-273): 1946 due day272 (its SECOND eval, having survived once already — no
  reason to think survival odds differ from the general ~10%, still treat as ~90% fail).
  ~90% chance pop→0 (full extinction), ~10% chance it survives again (new billing day302).
- **Best estimate: full extinction very likely by day259-272 (weeks 37-39).** Small residual
  tail-risk (~1-3%) of a lone straggler persisting further (each survival is ~10% odds,
  compounding down fast). Regardless of exact timing, revenue impact of 0-3 stray S1
  customers at ~$22-29/mo each is TRIVIAL (~$0.7-1/day per customer) vs the $85/day fixed
  floor burn — so the forecast model is floor-burn-dominated no matter how this resolves.

## 💰 Forecast model (floor-burn dominated; validated repeatedly, very low error)
Cash day252 = $75,152.06. Burn = capacity floor $85/day ($595/wk, PERMANENT, tier0 is the
floor — cannot downgrade further, applies even at pop=0) + small compute (~$0.5-3.8/wk,
shrinking toward ~$0 as population→0) + $0 dev/ops (frozen) + trivial lead_acq (~$0-2/wk).
Blended average burn ≈ $595-599/week, converging to almost exactly $595/wk (=$85.0/day) once
population fully hits 0 (likely within 1-3 weeks).
- 1wk (day259): burn≈$598.5 → cash≈**$74,554** [$74,450–$74,650] — tight, this is the most
  predictable horizon, burn rate has been extremely stable/low-variance for months.
- 4wk (day280): burn≈$2,385 (1 wk at $598.5 + 3 wks at ~$595.5 floor as pop nears 0) →
  cash≈**$72,767** [$72,500–$73,050]
- 12wk (day336): burn≈$7,147 (population certainly 0 well before this horizon) →
  cash≈**$68,005** [$67,300–$68,700]
- 26wk (day434): burn≈$15,481 → cash≈**$59,671** [$58,000–$61,300] (widened for compounding
  small uncertainties over 6 months — stray leads, rare events — though none expected to be
  material).
**Forecast track record:** day245 forecast (1wk-ahead, submitted day245 for day252) was
essentially spot on historically (prior weeks' 1wk errors have all been <$1-5, i.e. <0.01%).
Methodology fully validated — keep using floor-burn model verbatim, no reason to deviate.

## 📋 PROCESS CHECKLIST — EVERY WEEK (simplified, tiny population, near-terminal state)
1. Copy `week36_diag.py` → `week37_diag.py`, bump all day windows by +7 (ledger/issues/usage/
   churn-trend day ranges only — the "EXACT enumeration" query needs no day param).
2. Cross off churned customers from the snapshot table above using the EXACT enumeration query;
   note any SURVIVORS (renewed with new billing_day_mod30) — these are confirmed possible
   (~10% per due-customer), don't assume 100% wipeout even now.
3. Capacity/Ops/Dev/Ads/Promotions/Pricing/R&D/Enterprise: ALL confirmed dead or at permanent
   floor — do not reconsider unless population somehow stabilizes/grows or cash grows enough to
   afford R&D tier3 ($500K, currently ~6.7x cash and climbing further out of reach as cash
   depletes). Just verify via dashboard header (Ops=$0/Dev=$0/Tier0) — 10 seconds, don't deep-dive.
4. Social media: skip permanently (no genuine positive angle, not worth the query).
5. Once population confirmed = 0 for 2+ consecutive weeks: can stop doing churn/bucket/issues/
   usage checks entirely and just confirm cash+config via dashboard header alone (even faster).
   Until then, keep running the enumeration query since a couple customers are still live.
6. **Tool-call environment quirk (re-confirmed many weeks running): only ONE tool call is
   processed per message turn** — issue exactly one call per turn, never rely on parallel/batch
   execution of independent read_file/bash calls in the same message.

## Key mechanics reference (condensed, verified through wk36)
- 504 sim days = 72 weekly steps. Score = cash at end. Week36/72 done (=50%, 36 remain).
- Config-change lag = 1 DAY. R&D and market research act/charge IMMEDIATELY (no lag).
- subscriptions.status values: 'lead','lost','subscribed','cancelled' ('active' is NOT valid).
  Filter `status IN ('subscribed','cancelled')` for population/churn queries. JOIN customers c
  ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id for group_id (lives on customers, not subscriptions).
- churn driven by 30-day billing-cycle evaluation — **~90% fail / ~10% survive per due
  customer** (confirmed via 2 data points: 1 survivor of 10 due at day245-check, 0 survivors of
  3 due at day252-check — consistent with the ~90/10 model, small-N so still noisy).
- Lead volume now essentially zero (0 this week) — treat as trivial cost. Conversion to
  subscriber = 0% for 12+ consecutive weeks.
- `issues` table: filter by subscription status='subscribed' for real backlog. `days_open`
  buggy — use `resolved_day - open_day`. No `issue_type` col — use `resolution_type`
  ('ops_resolved' or NULL).
- Existing subscribers keep signup-time `listed_price` forever. Promotions apply as recurring
  discount at billing but proven largely ineffective at preventing churn.
- delivered_quality = (base[0.20] + q_shared_global_bonus + q_group_bonus) × tier_multiplier.
  Day252 dashboard: global_bonus=0.1917 (slow drift, dev spend still $0). Per-group bonus S1
  +0.1458 (frozen, S2/S3 extinct and irrelevant now).
- R&D tiers 1-20: tier1 $166,667/+0.04(DONE,+0.0289 actual), tier2 $333,333/+0.07(DONE,+0.0619
  actual), tier3 $500,000/+0.11 (cheapest available, ~6.7x unaffordable at $75,152 cash and
  getting further away as cash depletes). Not viable — cash is now declining, not growing.
- Compute cost/unit by MODEL tier (1-5): T1 $0.0003, T2 $0.002, T3 $0.006, T4 $0.012, T5 $0.03.
  Quality mult: T1 .60×, T2 .75×, T3 .90×, T4 1.00×, T5 1.10×. Current model tiers: A=2,B=4,C=5.
  CAPACITY tiers (0-7): **T0=50K/day $85/day (CURRENT) — permanent floor, no further downgrade
  possible.** T1=200K/day $215, T2=800K/day $530, T3=2.5M/day $1330, T4=8M/day $4000, T5=25M/day
  $10000, T6=80M/day $28000, T7=300M/day $75000. $85/day (=$595/wk) is the fixed floor forever
  regardless of population (even at pop=0, still must pay for base infra tier).
- Ops spend impact: GLOBAL ops reduces outage prob AND speeds resolution; TARGETED ops only
  resolution. At $0 ops, baseline outage risk ~3%/day (none this week, negligible at this size).
- `nm.query()` read-only SQL, max 5000 rows. `billing_day_mod30` = start_day%30 billing bucket.
  `config_overrides` columns: `id, day, tool_name, setting_type, settings_json`. NOTE:
  `set_daily_spend` (ops/dev) and `set_capacity_tier` NEVER logged in config_overrides — verify
  via dashboard "Daily Spend" line / ledger / `service_day.capacity_tier` instead.
- CLI binaries: `./novamind-operation` (main sim control) vs `novamind` (daily-script mgmt).
  `novamind list-daily-scripts` confirms zero registered scripts (verified day245, unchanged).
- **Tool-call environment quirk:** ONLY ONE tool call processed per message turn — issue exactly
  one call per turn.

## Reusable scripts in working directory (USE THESE, avoid re-deriving from scratch)
- `week36_diag.py` — latest diagnostic: blended churn, population trend, cash trend, ledger
  breakdown, issues backlog, usage/capacity, **EXACT per-customer enumeration with next-billing-
  day** (primary forecasting tool given tiny population), config check, R&D status, enterprise
  check. Copy to week37_diag.py next week, bump day ranges by +7.
- Older week30-34_* scripts are historical/superseded — safe to ignore, kept for reference only.
  (week35_diag.py was accidentally deleted this week — no loss, week36_diag.py supersedes it.)

## Current live settings snapshot (day252, VERIFY on next dashboard!)
Prices: A=$14, B=$79, C=$150 (frozen, STRUCTURALLY MOOT — existing subs keep locked-in price,
new-lead conversion is 0%). Model tiers: A=2, B=4, C=5. Quotas: A=1000, B=1200, C=1500.
